title: How to Choose a Disposable Vape: 7 Things to Check First
summary: Puff count, battery, flavor, strength and price all matter. Here is a simple checklist adult buyers can use to pick the right disposable vape.
body:
Disposable vapes are sold fully charged and pre-filled, which makes them the easiest way into vaping for adults. They are also the category with the widest spread in quality and price, so a few minutes of checking pays off.

## 1. Puff count versus how you vape
Puff counts on the box are manufacturer estimates. A 5,000-puff device and a 30,000-puff device can both feel the same in your hand, but the larger one holds more liquid and usually carries a bigger battery. If you vape a few times a day, a mid-range device will last weeks. Heavy daily users often prefer the higher counts because the cost per puff is lower.

## 2. Rechargeable or not
Many current devices have a USB-C port so you can top up the battery after the liquid is still going strong. Non-rechargeable models are lighter but can run out of battery before the liquid. Read the product page for a charging port before you buy. Our guide to [charging a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/) explains the basics.

## 3. Flavor family
Pick the flavor style you already enjoy: fruit, mint, dessert, tobacco or a mix. Cooling versions with "ice" in the name add a menthol-type chill. Browse the full range in [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/).

## 4. Nicotine strength
Most disposables are sold around 5% nicotine (50 mg/mL). Check the label for the exact strength and read our [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/) if you are unsure. Nicotine is addictive, and these products are for adults 21 and over.

## 5. Screen and extras
Some devices show battery and liquid levels on a small display. It is helpful, but not essential.

## 6. Price per puff
Divide the price by the puff count to compare fairly. Bulk and multi-pack deals often lower it further.

## 7. Where you buy
Buy from a retailer that verifies age, ships with adult signature and publishes clear [shipping](/shipping/) and refund terms.

faq.q: How long does a disposable vape last?
faq.a: It depends on the device and how often you use it. A higher puff count generally lasts longer, but real-world life varies with draw length and frequency.

faq.q: Can I refill a disposable vape?
faq.a: No. Disposables are designed to be used once. Refilling can damage the device and is not recommended by manufacturers.

title: Disposable vs Pod System vs Box Mod: Which Suits You?
summary: Three device types, three trade-offs. Compare cost, effort, flavor control and portability to decide between a disposable, a pod kit and a box mod.
body:
Vape hardware falls into three broad groups. Each solves a different problem, and the right choice depends on how much effort and money you want to put in.

## Disposables: zero upkeep
A disposable comes ready to use. There is nothing to fill, no coil to change and no settings. You use it until it is empty, then recycle it where local rules allow. The trade-off is a higher long-term cost and less flavor choice per device. Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) if convenience is your priority.

## Pod systems: the middle ground
A pod system uses a rechargeable battery with a replaceable pod. You can pick closed pods that arrive pre-filled or refillable pods you fill with your own e-liquid. Running costs are lower than disposables once you buy a few bottles, and you control flavor and strength. Our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) include several starter pod systems.

## Box mods: maximum control
Box mods have larger batteries, adjustable wattage and airflow, and use refillable tanks with replaceable coils. They suit people who like to tune the experience and are comfortable learning about coils and battery handling. They are the most involved option, and our [first vape kit guide](/blog/first-vape-kit-guide/) is a good starting point.

## Quick comparison
- **Cost to start:** disposable lowest, box mod highest.
- **Cost over time:** disposable highest, pod and mod lower.
- **Effort:** disposable none, pod low, mod moderate.
- **Flavor choice:** disposable limited, pod and mod unlimited.

## Which should you pick?
If you want to try vaping with no learning curve, start with a disposable. If you vape daily and want to cut costs, move to a pod system. If you enjoy tinkering, a box mod is rewarding. All of these are for adults 21+.

faq.q: Is a pod system cheaper than disposables?
faq.a: Usually, after the first purchase. You buy a device once and then pay for e-liquid and the occasional replacement pod or coil.

faq.q: Do I need experience for a box mod?
faq.a: It helps. Beginners are usually better served by a pod system and can move to a box mod later.

title: Puff Counts Explained: What 5K, 20K and 50K Really Mean
summary: A disposable's puff count is an estimate, not a promise. Learn how it is calculated and how to compare devices by real value.
body:
You will see numbers like 5K, 20K, 30K or 50K printed on nearly every disposable vape. These are puff counts, and they are the first thing many buyers compare. They are genuinely useful, but only if you understand what they represent, what changes them in real life and how to turn them into a fair comparison of value. This guide explains what a puff count is, why your results will differ from the box, how liquid and battery limit a device, how to compare cost per puff and how to choose a size. It is general information for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What a puff count is
A puff count is the manufacturer's estimate of how many draws the device can deliver before it runs out of liquid or battery. It is usually based on a standard test draw of roughly two to three seconds at a consistent rate under controlled conditions. In a lab, the machine takes the same puff every time with a pause in between. In your hand, you do not.

That makes the figure a ballpark for comparison, not a guarantee. Two devices rated 20,000 puffs will be broadly similar to each other, and a 50,000-puff device will generally last much longer than a 5,000-puff one. But neither will deliver exactly the stated number for every user.

## Why your real number will differ
- **Draw length:** longer pulls use more liquid and more battery per puff. If your puffs are twice as long as the test puff, you may get closer to half the stated count.
- **Airflow and power mode:** boost or high-power modes drain the battery faster and heat the coil harder.
- **Chain use:** back-to-back pulls heat the coil without giving the wick time to refill, which can burn through liquid faster and affect flavor.
- **Temperature and storage:** very hot or cold conditions can reduce battery performance and change how liquid flows. See [how to store disposable vapes](/blog/how-to-store-disposable-vapes/).
- **Flavor and liquid:** thicker liquids wick differently and can change the consumption rate.
- **Charging habits:** on rechargeable devices, regularly topping up keeps the battery from being the limit.

## Liquid versus battery
Every disposable has two limits: the amount of e-liquid in the reservoir and the energy in the battery. A device is finished when either runs out. Higher puff counts generally mean a larger reservoir and a bigger battery, but the design differs.

- **Non-rechargeable devices** carry a battery sized to match the liquid, so both tend to end around the same time. If the battery runs out first, the device stops with liquid left inside.
- **Rechargeable devices** use a USB-C port so the battery can be topped up, which lets you finish all of the liquid. Many large-capacity devices are rechargeable for this reason. Our guide to [rechargeable vs non-rechargeable disposables](/blog/rechargeable-vs-non-rechargeable-disposables/) explains how to check.

If you buy a large device, charge it on a hard, dry surface with a standard cable and unplug it when full. See [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/) and [how to extend vape battery life](/blog/how-to-extend-vape-battery-life/).

## Turning puff count into cost per puff
Divide the price by the puff count to compare value. The result is tiny, so it is easier to compare per 1,000 puffs.

- A $15 device rated at 5,000 puffs costs $3.00 per 1,000 puffs.
- A $20 device rated at 20,000 puffs costs $1.00 per 1,000 puffs.
- A $25 device rated at 50,000 puffs costs $0.50 per 1,000 puffs.

In these examples the largest device costs a sixth as much per puff as the smallest, even though its sticker price is higher. That is why heavy users often save money on big devices. Our guide to [comparing vape prices per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/) walks through the method with live examples.

## Features that matter more than the headline number
- **USB-C charging:** extends the life of a large device.
- **Display screen:** shows battery and liquid so you know when it is nearly finished. See [screen vs no-screen disposables](/blog/screen-vs-no-screen-disposable-vapes/).
- **Adjustable airflow:** lets you tune the draw and can improve flavor. See [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).
- **Coil technology:** mesh coils heat more evenly and help keep flavor consistent across the device's life. See [what is a mesh coil](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/).
- **Flavor consistency:** a very high puff count is only worth it if you enjoy the flavor for the whole device.

## Which size should you buy?
- **Occasional use or trying a new flavor:** a smaller device is perfectly sensible. You avoid being stuck with a flavor you do not enjoy.
- **Daily use:** larger devices generally cost less per puff and mean fewer purchases and less waste.
- **Travel:** compact, lighter devices are easier to carry. See [best vapes for travel](/blog/best-vapes-for-travel/).
- **Flavor explorers:** several smaller devices let you sample more flavors for the same budget.

Our [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) range lists puff counts on product pages so you can compare quickly, and [how to choose a disposable vape](/blog/how-to-choose-a-disposable-vape/) puts all of these factors together.

## Common misconceptions
- **"The count is exact."** It is an estimate under test conditions.
- **"More puffs always means better."** It means longer life, but only worthwhile if you enjoy the flavor and will use it.
- **"Non-rechargeable is worse."** It is simply a different design, lighter and simpler, usually with a smaller capacity.
- **"Liquid is the only limit."** On non-rechargeable devices, battery can be the limit.
- **"A device that stops early is faulty."** Heavy or chain use can shorten life, as can heat and cold.

## Using disposables responsibly
Take gentle, short puffs, keep the device upright and cool, and do not open or modify it. When it is finished, recycle it at an electronics or battery collection point where available. See [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). Keep devices away from children and pets. Every product we sell is for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Buying from One Stop Vape Store
Choose your device, check the puff count and strength on the product page, and add it to your cart. Pay with Cash App, Apple Pay, Chime, cryptocurrency or gift cards. Crypto and supported gift cards save 10%, and orders of $200 or more after discounts ship free, which makes multi-device orders especially good value. We process orders within 24 to 72 business hours in Phoenix, Arizona and ship with tracking, and an adult 21 or older signs on delivery. If you run a shop, read the [wholesale ordering guide](/blog/wholesale-ordering-guide/).

## Quick checklist before you buy
Look at the puff count, the price per 1,000 puffs, the charging port, the strength and the flavor. If two devices are close on value, choose the one with the flavor you are more likely to finish, because a cheaper device you stop enjoying halfway is not good value. And if you are not sure how a particular listing compares, send us a message through the [contact page](/contact/) and we will point you to a sensible option.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is the puff count the same as the number of times I can draw?
In principle, yes, but it is based on test conditions. A real puff is rarely identical to the test puff, so treat the number as a way to compare devices rather than a promise about your own usage.

### Do bigger devices cost more to ship or have different rules?
Orders ship at a flat $15 or free over $200 after discounts, regardless of the size of the device. Delivery still requires an adult 21 or older to sign. See [minimum order and free shipping explained](/blog/minimum-order-and-free-shipping-explained/).

### How can I tell when my disposable is nearly finished?
Common signs are fading flavor, thinner vapor, a burnt taste or a battery light that blinks. Some devices include a screen that shows battery and liquid levels. If flavor fades but the device still works, it may be near the end of its liquid. See [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/).

### Does a larger puff count mean a stronger product?
No. Strength is set by the concentration of nicotine in the liquid, not by the size of the device. A 50K device and a 5K device can have the same listed strength. See the [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/).

### What should I do with a device that still has charge but no flavor?
Treat it as finished. Do not try to open it or refill it. Recycle it at an electronics or battery collection point where available, following our guide on [disposing of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

### Is it worth buying several smaller devices instead of one large one?
If you like to sample flavors, yes. If you have a favorite and vape daily, a larger device usually costs less per puff. Many adults do both: one large device for their main flavor and a smaller one to try something new.

### Can I trust puff counts on very cheap devices?
Treat any figure with the same caution, but look at the whole listing. A reputable listing shows the strength, the charging port and clear packaging, and it comes from a brand with a track record. If a very low price comes with a very high puff count and little other information, compare it with similar devices before you buy, and read [how to spot counterfeit vapes](/blog/how-to-spot-counterfeit-vapes/) so you know what a genuine product looks like.

faq.q: What does a puff count of 50K mean?
faq.a: It is the manufacturer's estimate that the device can deliver about 50,000 draws under standard test conditions. Real results depend on how you use it.

faq.q: Why did my disposable run out before the stated puff count?
faq.a: Long draws, chain use, high-power modes and heat all use liquid and battery faster than the test puff, so many people get less than the stated number.

faq.q: Is a bigger puff count better value?
faq.a: Usually per puff, yes. Divide price by puffs to compare. Larger devices often cost much less per 1,000 puffs, but only if you will use them.

faq.q: Can I recharge a disposable vape?
faq.a: Many large-capacity models have a USB-C port and can be recharged. Smaller models may be non-rechargeable. Check the product page.

faq.q: Do mesh coils change the puff count?
faq.a: Mesh coils do not change the stated count, but they heat more evenly and help keep flavor consistent across the life of the device.

faq.q: How do I compare two disposables fairly?
faq.a: Compare price per 1,000 puffs, strength, charging port and flavor. The best value is the device you will enjoy to the end.

title: Nicotine Strength Guide: mg/mL, Percent and What to Pick
summary: Understand how nicotine strength is labeled, how mg/mL converts to percent, and how adults can choose a strength that matches their habits.
body:
Nicotine strength is the number on a vape product that adults most often misread, and it is also the number that matters most. Get it wrong and a product that should feel pleasant feels harsh, or a purchase feels too weak to be worth finishing. This guide explains how strength is written on labels, how milligrams per milliliter and percentages relate, which ranges are typical for each kind of product, and how adults sensibly choose a level. It is general information for adults aged 21 and over, not medical advice, and nicotine is addictive.

## The two ways strength is written
Labels use two systems that describe exactly the same thing. The first is milligrams per milliliter, written mg/mL or just mg. The second is a percentage. To convert, divide the mg/mL figure by 10 to get the percentage, or multiply the percentage by 10 to get mg/mL. So 3 mg/mL is 0.3%, 12 mg/mL is 1.2%, 20 mg/mL is 2%, and 50 mg/mL is 5%.

Many disposable devices and nicotine-salt liquids show both, such as "50mg (5%)". Some US labels show only the percentage, and some imported products show only milligrams, so it is worth keeping the rule in your head. When you compare two products, always compare in the same unit.

## What the number actually tells you
The figure is a concentration, not a dose. A 50 mg/mL liquid contains 50 milligrams of nicotine in every milliliter of liquid. How much nicotine you take in depends on how much liquid you vaporize, which depends on your device, your power, the size of each puff and how often you puff. A small pod device that vaporizes very little liquid per puff and a large tank that vaporizes a lot can deliver very different amounts from the same strength.

That is why strength is always chosen together with the device. A high-strength salt in a low-power pod behaves very differently from the same strength in a powerful tank, and the second combination would usually be unpleasant and is not what the liquid is made for. Read the hardware recommendation before you read anything else.

## Typical ranges by product type
- **0 to 3 mg/mL (0 to 0.3%):** usually freebase liquids made for large sub-ohm tanks, where each puff uses a lot of liquid. Zero-nicotine versions exist for flavor only.
- **6 to 12 mg/mL (0.6 to 1.2%):** moderate freebase strengths for mouth-to-lung tanks and starter kits.
- **18 to 24 mg/mL (1.8 to 2.4%):** higher freebase strengths, and the start of the nicotine-salt range.
- **20 to 35 mg/mL (2 to 3.5%):** the common range for nicotine salts in small pod devices.
- **50 mg/mL (5%):** typical for many disposable vapes and high-strength salts, and common in the US market.
- **Pouches:** listed per pouch in milligrams, commonly from about 3 mg to 12 mg or more, which is a different scale from liquid strength. See [nicotine pouch strengths explained](/blog/nicotine-pouch-strengths-explained/).

## Why salts and freebase use different scales
Freebase nicotine is the older form. At higher strengths it feels sharp on the throat, so freebase liquids are sold at lower strengths and used in devices that produce more vapor per puff. Nicotine salts bind nicotine to an acid, which changes the pH and makes the vapor feel smoother at higher strengths. That is why pods and disposables, which produce small puffs, use salts at 20 to 50 mg/mL. Our comparison of [nicotine salts vs freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/) goes into the chemistry and the cost differences.

## How adults choose a starting strength
There is no universal right answer, but there are sensible habits:

1. **Start from what you already use.** If you are moving from another nicotine product, compare the strength to that product and start at or below it rather than above it.
2. **Match the device.** Low-power pods pair with salts, powerful tanks pair with low-strength freebase. A mismatch is the most common cause of a bad experience.
3. **Prefer lower to higher when unsure.** It is easy to move up later and unpleasant to move down. A strength that is too high often shows up as dizziness, nausea or a racing heart, and the right response is to stop and use a lower strength next time.
4. **Change one thing at a time.** If you switch strength, flavor and device all at once, you will not know which change made the difference.
5. **Allow for habit.** People who vape very frequently often find they drift towards stronger products. Noticing that drift is useful information, and it is a reason to keep track of how much you use.

## Disposables and the 5% standard
Most disposable vapes sold in the US list 50mg (5%). Because the puffs are small and the devices are low-power, that concentration is designed for the format. If a disposable feels too strong, taking shorter, less frequent puffs changes your intake far more than the label does. Some brands offer lower-strength versions, and our [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) pages show the strength on each product, with options where a listing offers more than one.

## Reading strength on our product pages
Every product page in the store shows the nicotine strength where the manufacturer lists it. Where a product comes in several strengths, such as 9mg, 12mg and 15mg, you choose the strength above the Add to Cart button and the page shows your choice. See [how to read a vape product page](/blog/how-to-read-a-vape-product-page/) for a walkthrough, and [how to read an e-liquid label](/blog/how-to-read-an-e-liquid-label/) if you are holding a bottle.

## Zero nicotine and flavor-only liquids
Some adults want the flavor and ritual without nicotine, and 0 mg liquids exist for them. They are labelled clearly, and they are still for adults aged 21 and over. If you move between nicotine and zero-nicotine liquids, rinse and refill the device properly so flavors do not mix, and replace the coil when the taste changes.

## Common mistakes
- **Buying the highest number available.** High strength is not a quality marker. For most people it is the wrong place to start.
- **Mixing up mg and percent.** 5% is 50 mg/mL, not 5 mg/mL. Misreading the unit is easy to do with an unfamiliar label.
- **Using salts in a high-power tank.** The combination is harsh and wasteful, and the liquid is not designed for it.
- **Ignoring the pouch scale.** A 6 mg pouch and a 6 mg/mL liquid are not equivalent. Compare within the same product type.
- **Not allowing time.** Your sense of what feels right changes over the first week of a new device, so avoid judging on the first few puffs alone.

## Keeping nicotine in perspective
Nicotine is an addictive chemical. The products on this site are for adults aged 21 and over, are not for use by anyone who is pregnant or nursing, and should be kept away from children and pets. If you have a medical condition or take medication, ask a healthcare professional before using any nicotine product. Nothing in this guide is medical advice, and no product described here is claimed to treat or prevent any condition. For the rules that govern sales and delivery, read [what 21+ age verification means](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/) and the [FDA and vaping products overview](/blog/fda-and-vaping-products-what-adults-should-know/).

## Putting it into practice at checkout
When you shop, filter by the product type that suits your device first, then compare strengths within that type. Choose the strength and pack size on the product page, check the price updates, and add it to your cart. Orders of $200 or more after discounts ship free, and paying with cryptocurrency or a supported gift card saves 10%, which you can read about in [how the crypto discount works](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/). If you are unsure which strength fits your device, contact us before ordering through the [contact page](/contact/) or WhatsApp and we will help you read the label.

## A short worked example
Suppose you currently use a pod device with a 30 mL bottle of 35 mg/mL salt, and you are considering a disposable. The disposable lists 50mg (5%). Converting, 35 mg/mL is 3.5%, so the disposable is about 43% stronger by concentration. Because disposable puffs are small and the device is low-power, many people find the experience comparable, but if you are sensitive you might choose a lower-strength option where one is listed, or take fewer, shorter puffs. The point is to compare like with like and then adjust gently, not to chase the biggest number.

Now suppose you use a sub-ohm tank with a 3 mg/mL freebase liquid. Converting to 50 mg/mL salts would be a 16-fold jump in concentration in a device that vaporizes far more liquid per puff, which is exactly the situation to avoid. In that case you would stay with freebase in a similar range and compare flavors, not strengths.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does strength change how long a bottle or device lasts?
Not directly. Strength is a concentration, so a higher-strength liquid does not last longer or shorter because of the number itself. What changes consumption is the device and how you puff. Many people notice that with a higher-strength product they take fewer puffs to feel satisfied, which can make a bottle last longer, while others take the same number of puffs and simply use more nicotine. Keeping track of how many days a bottle or device lasts is a simple, honest way to see how your use is changing over time.

### Should I change strength with the seasons or my routine?
Some adults adjust strength to their routine, for example using a lower strength at home and a higher one on a long working day. If you do this, keep the changes small and deliberate. Having two devices at two strengths is easier than constantly mixing liquids, and it keeps each setup consistent so you can tell what is working.

### What if a strength feels too strong?
Stop, wait until you feel normal and use a lower strength next time. Taking shorter, slower puffs and spacing them out reduces intake with any product. If you repeatedly feel unwell at a given strength, it is the wrong strength for you, and a healthcare professional can advise if you have questions about nicotine.

### What if a strength feels too weak?
Check the device first. A worn coil, a low battery or a mismatched liquid can make a good strength feel flat. Replace the coil or pod, charge the device and check the ratio before you move up in strength. See [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/) and [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/).

### How should I read strength on pouches and other products?
Different product types use different scales. A pouch lists milligrams per pouch, a liquid lists milligrams per milliliter or a percentage, and a disposable lists the strength of the liquid inside. Compare only within the same type. If you move between types, start low and learn the new product.

faq.q: How do I convert mg/mL to percent?
faq.a: Divide the mg/mL figure by 10. For example 20 mg/mL is 2% and 50 mg/mL is 5%. To go the other way, multiply the percentage by 10.

faq.q: What strength do disposable vapes usually have?
faq.a: Most disposables sold in the US list 50mg (5%), because they use nicotine salts in low-power devices. Check each product page for the exact figure.

faq.q: Is a higher strength better?
faq.a: No. Higher strength means a higher concentration, not a better product. Most adults do better starting at or below the level they already use and adjusting gradually.

faq.q: Can I use nicotine salts in a sub-ohm tank?
faq.a: It is not recommended. Salts are made for low-power pods. In a powerful tank the high concentration and large puffs make for a harsh experience.

faq.q: Do you sell zero-nicotine products?
faq.a: Yes, some e-liquids and disposables are available at 0 mg. They are still for adults 21 and over and are labelled clearly on the product page.

faq.q: Where do I choose a strength on the product page?
faq.a: Where a product offers more than one strength, the options appear above the Add to Cart button and the price updates when you choose one.

title: Nicotine Salts vs Freebase E-Liquid: Key Differences
summary: Salts and freebase deliver nicotine differently. See how they feel, which devices suit each and how to choose between them.
body:
Walk into any vape shop or browse any online catalog and you will see two kinds of nicotine on the label of e-liquid: salts and freebase. They look similar on the shelf, but they behave differently in your device, they come in different strengths and they suit different hardware. Choosing the wrong one for your setup is one of the most common reasons a new vaper finds the experience harsh, leaky or disappointing. This guide explains what each type is, how they feel, which devices suit them, how they compare on cost and how to choose. It is general information for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What freebase nicotine is
Freebase is the form of nicotine used in e-liquid for most of vaping's history. In freebase, nicotine is in its pure, unbound form, and it vaporizes easily. The trade-off is that it feels sharp on the throat, especially as strength rises. For that reason freebase liquids are made at lower strengths, commonly 0 to 12 mg/mL and occasionally up to about 24 mg/mL, and they are designed for devices that produce larger volumes of vapor per puff.

That sharper feel is called throat hit, and some people like it because it resembles the sensation of a traditional cigarette. Others find it unpleasant. If throat hit matters to you, our guide to [throat hit explained](/blog/throat-hit-explained/) covers what drives it.

## What nicotine salts are
Nicotine salts, usually written "nic salts", combine nicotine with an acid such as benzoic acid. This lowers the pH of the liquid, which makes the vapor feel smoother even at high strengths. The nicotine is also absorbed in a way that many users describe as quicker and more satisfying with fewer, smaller puffs. Because of the smoother feel, salts are sold at higher strengths, from around 20 mg/mL up to 50 mg/mL (5%), and they dominate pods and disposables.

Nearly every disposable vape on the market uses nicotine salts, which is why you will see 50mg (5%) so often on product pages. See the [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/) for how that number relates to what you vape.

## Side-by-side comparison
- **Typical strength:** freebase 0 to 12 mg/mL (sometimes higher); salts 20 to 50 mg/mL.
- **Feel at the throat:** freebase is sharper; salts are smoother.
- **Puff size:** freebase suits large puffs and big clouds; salts suit small, frequent puffs.
- **Best hardware:** freebase in higher-wattage and sub-ohm tanks; salts in low-power pods and small devices.
- **Bottle sizes:** freebase is often sold in 60 mL to 120 mL bottles; salts in 30 mL bottles.
- **PG/VG:** freebase often higher VG for clouds; salts often balanced or higher PG for pods. See [PG and VG ratios explained](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## Which device suits which liquid
The device decides the answer more than preference does.

### Freebase devices
Sub-ohm tanks, rebuildable atomizers and many box mods use low-resistance coils that run at higher power and vaporize a lot of liquid per puff. A low-strength freebase liquid in a thicker, higher-VG blend works well here. The large puffs deliver plenty of nicotine even at 3 mg/mL.

### Salt devices
Pod systems, pen-style devices and disposables run at lower power with higher-resistance coils, which vaporize little liquid per puff. High-strength salts make up for the small puffs and stay smooth. Using a low-strength freebase in these devices can feel weak, and using salts in a powerful tank would be harsh.

If you are not sure what your device is, check the manual or the product page. Our [guide to disposable vs pod vs box mod](/blog/disposable-vs-pod-vs-box-mod/) explains the main categories.

## Cost and how long a bottle lasts
Because salts are used in small, frequent puffs at high strength, a 30 mL bottle can last a long time, and many people find salts economical for that reason. Freebase is typically bought in larger bottles because tanks use more liquid, and the cost per milliliter is often lower even though you use more of it. Compare cost per milliliter and the volume you expect to use per day, not just the price on the front. Our [bottle sizes guide](/blog/e-liquid-bottle-sizes-30ml-60ml-100ml/) explains what 30 mL, 60 mL and 100 mL mean in practice.

## Flavor and the two types
Both types can carry excellent flavor, and many brands release the same flavor in both formats. Salts tend to taste a touch smoother and sweeter because of the lower pH, while freebase can taste slightly more distinct and crisp. If you love a flavor in one format and want to try it in the other, expect it to be recognizable but not identical. You can browse both in our [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) range, where each product page lists its strength and bottle size.

## Mixing types and switching between them
Do not mix salts and freebase in the same bottle or tank, and avoid topping up one type into a tank still holding the other. Strength and pH will be unpredictable. When you switch, empty the tank, rinse it, replace the coil and start fresh. If you are going from freebase to salts, keep in mind that the jump in strength is large and your device must be designed for it, which means a pod system or similar. Take it gently, because the concentration is much higher than you are used to.

## Common mistakes
- **Using salts in a sub-ohm tank.** Concentration and puff size together are far too much.
- **Using low-strength freebase in a small pod.** It can feel weak and encourage frequent puffing.
- **Ignoring the PG/VG ratio.** A thick liquid in a small pod can fail to wick and burn the coil. See [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/).
- **Chasing strength.** A higher figure is not a better product.
- **Skipping the label.** Always confirm strength, volume and the hardware recommendation. Our guide to [reading an e-liquid label](/blog/how-to-read-an-e-liquid-label/) shows what to look for.

## How to choose, step by step
1. Identify your device type and its recommended power range.
2. Choose the nicotine type that matches: salts for low-power pods, freebase for tanks.
3. Pick a strength inside the normal range for that type, starting lower if you are unsure.
4. Choose a PG/VG ratio recommended for your hardware.
5. Choose a bottle size that fits how quickly you use liquid.
6. Pick a flavor you enjoy and plan to vape consistently, then judge it over several uses.

## Safety, storage and responsibility
Nicotine is addictive, and e-liquid is for adults aged 21 and over only. Keep bottles capped and out of reach of children and pets, store them in a cool, dark place and wipe up spills promptly. Our guide to [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/) covers shelf life and storage in detail. If you have a medical condition or are pregnant or nursing, speak to a healthcare professional before using any nicotine product. Nothing here is medical advice.

## Ordering e-liquid from One Stop Vape Store
Browse by nicotine type, bottle size and brand, choose your options on the product page and check out with Cash App, Apple Pay, Chime, cryptocurrency or gift cards. Crypto and supported gift cards save 10%, and orders of $200 or more after discounts ship free. We ship from our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse with tracking, and an adult 21 or older must sign on delivery, as explained in [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/). If you want help matching a liquid to a device, message us through the [contact page](/contact/).

## A practical way to test the difference
If you own both a pod device and a tank, the clearest way to understand the difference is to try a sensible product in each. Choose a nicotine-salt liquid at a moderate strength for the pod and a low-strength freebase for the tank, vape each for a few days and notice how many puffs you take, how the throat feels and how satisfied you are afterwards. Keep notes if that helps. Most people discover quickly which pairing matches their habits, and it is far cheaper to learn that with one bottle than with several.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Are salts stronger than freebase?
Salts are sold at higher listed strengths, but strength alone does not tell you how strong the experience is. Because salts are smoother, you can use them at 50 mg/mL in a small pod without the harshness that the same concentration of freebase would cause. The device, puff size and your habits matter as much as the label.

### Why do disposables use salts?
Disposables are small, low-power devices that vaporize a little liquid per puff. High-strength salts suit that design: they stay smooth at high concentration and deliver satisfaction in small, frequent puffs. A freebase liquid at the same concentration would be harsh in the same device.

### Do salts and freebase taste different?
Often slightly. The lower pH of salts can make flavor feel rounder and sweeter, while freebase can feel crisper. Makers adjust recipes for each type, so the same named flavor will be close but not identical.

### Which should a beginner choose?
Choose by device. If you are starting with a small pod kit or a disposable, salts are what the device is made for. If you are starting with a tank, begin with a low-strength freebase. Beginners get into trouble when they combine the wrong type with the wrong device, so match first and refine later.

### Can salts leak or gunk up a device faster?
Not because of the nicotine type itself. Leaks and gunk usually come from a mismatched ratio, overfilling or a worn coil. See [vape leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/) and [how to clean a vape device](/blog/how-to-clean-a-vape-device/).

### Does the type change how I store the liquid?
No. Both are best kept capped, in a cool, dark place, away from heat and sunlight, and out of reach of children and pets. Check the date on the bottle and use older bottles first.

faq.q: What is the difference between nicotine salts and freebase?
faq.a: Freebase is nicotine in its pure form, which feels sharper and is sold at lower strengths. Salts bind nicotine to an acid, which feels smoother at higher strengths, so they are sold from about 20 to 50 mg/mL.

faq.q: Which type do disposable vapes use?
faq.a: Almost all disposable vapes use nicotine salts, typically listed as 50mg (5%).

faq.q: Can I use salts in my sub-ohm tank?
faq.a: It is not recommended. Salts are made for low-power pods, and in a powerful tank the concentration and puff size make the vapor harsh.

faq.q: Is freebase cheaper than salts?
faq.a: Often the cost per milliliter is lower for freebase because it is sold in larger bottles, but you also use more liquid. Compare cost per milliliter and your daily use.

faq.q: Can I mix salts and freebase?
faq.a: No. Mixing changes the strength and pH unpredictably. Empty and rinse the tank before switching types.

faq.q: How do I know which one my device needs?
faq.a: Check the manual or product page. Low-power pods and disposables suit salts; sub-ohm tanks and box mods suit freebase.

title: PG and VG Ratios Explained: How They Change Your Vape
summary: E-liquid is mostly propylene glycol and vegetable glycerin. Learn how the ratio affects throat feel, vapor and which device it suits.
body:
Almost every e-liquid on the market is built on two ingredients: propylene glycol, written PG, and vegetable glycerin, written VG. The ratio between them is printed on most bottles, often as numbers such as 50/50 or 70/30, and it shapes how your vape feels, how it tastes and, most importantly, whether it works in your device at all. This guide explains what each ingredient does, what the common ratios mean, how to match a ratio to hardware and how to troubleshoot the problems a mismatch causes. It is general information for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## The two base liquids
PG and VG are both clear, odorless liquids used widely in food, cosmetics and many other products. In e-liquid they act as carriers: they hold flavor and nicotine, and they turn into vapor when heated by the coil. Each has distinct properties, and e-liquid makers blend them to suit different devices.

### What PG does
Propylene glycol is thin and runny. It carries flavor very well, which is why high-PG liquids often taste crisp and distinct. It also produces more of the throat hit that some users associate with a classic vape. Because it is thin, it wicks quickly through small coils, which suits pods and starter kits with small, high-resistance coils. The downside is that it creates thinner, less dense vapor.

### What VG does
Vegetable glycerin is thicker and slightly sweet. It produces denser, softer vapor and a smoother feel. Because it is thick, it wicks slowly and needs coils with big wicking channels and generous airflow, such as sub-ohm tanks. It is the ingredient that produces large clouds. The downside is that very thick liquid can starve a small coil and cause a burnt taste.

## Reading ratios on a bottle
The ratio is written PG first and VG second, though some brands put VG first, so read the label carefully. A bottle marked 50/50 contains equal parts. A bottle marked 70/30 might mean 70% PG and 30% VG or the reverse depending on the brand, and brands that print "70VG/30PG" remove the doubt. Many labels also list "max VG", which means as much VG as the flavor and nicotine allow, typically around 70 to 80% VG after the other ingredients are added.

## Common ratios and what they suit
- **50/50:** a balanced blend that works in most pods, pen devices and mouth-to-lung tanks. It is the default for many flavored liquids because it carries flavor well and wicks reliably.
- **60/40 or 70/30 PG-heavy:** very thin. Best for small pod systems and the tiniest coils, and can feel crisp on the throat.
- **70/30 VG-heavy:** thicker, intended for sub-ohm tanks and higher-power devices with larger wicking holes.
- **Max VG:** the thickest option, only suitable for hardware designed for it, and it produces the largest, smoothest clouds.

Nicotine-salt liquids for pods and disposables are commonly balanced or PG-leaning so that they wick through small coils, which is part of why the two nicotine types suit different devices. See [nicotine salts vs freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/).

## How the ratio changes the experience
### Flavor
PG carries flavor strongly, so a 50/50 or PG-heavy liquid often tastes sharper. VG dilutes flavor slightly but adds sweetness and smoothness. If you find a high-VG liquid flavorless in a pod, it may simply be too thick to wick properly rather than lacking flavor.

### Throat feel
More PG usually means more throat hit; more VG means a softer feel. If a liquid seems harsh, a higher-VG blend at the same strength can feel gentler, as long as your hardware can handle it.

### Vapor volume
VG produces more visible vapor. Large clouds need both a high-VG liquid and a device that can vaporize a lot of it. In a small pod, a high-VG liquid will not make large clouds, and it may not work at all.

### Coil life
Thick, sweet liquids can leave residue on coils faster, which shortens coil life in some devices. Thinner liquids tend to keep small coils cleaner. If you notice flavor fading earlier than expected, see [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/).

## Matching the ratio to hardware
This is the rule that prevents most problems: use the ratio the hardware is designed for.

- **Small pods and starter kits:** 50/50 or PG-leaning, and usually nicotine salts.
- **Mouth-to-lung tanks:** 50/50 or 60/40.
- **Sub-ohm tanks:** 70/30 VG or higher, usually low-strength freebase.
- **Disposables:** the liquid is pre-filled with a ratio chosen by the maker, so there is nothing to match.

If you are unsure what your device is designed for, check the manual or product page. Our [guide to sub-ohm vs mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/) explains the two main styles.

## What a mismatch looks like
- **Thick liquid in a small pod:** the coil cannot soak up liquid fast enough, so it dries out and burns. You get a harsh, burnt taste and weak vapor. See [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/) and [dry hits explained](/blog/dry-hits-explained/).
- **Thin liquid in a powerful tank:** the coil is flooded and the tank leaks or gurgles. See [vape leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/) and [fixing a gurgling vape](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/).
- **Weak flavor:** often a ratio and power mismatch rather than a problem with the liquid itself.

## Allergies and sensitivities
Some people notice irritation or a dry mouth and throat with one base or the other. If you experience irritation, stop using the product and talk to a healthcare professional. Nothing in this guide is medical advice. Nicotine is addictive, and products are for adults aged 21 and over.

## Flavorings and other ingredients
E-liquid also contains flavorings and, in nicotine products, nicotine. The ratio refers only to PG and VG, and the overall liquid may include other components in small amounts. Our guide to [e-liquid ingredients explained](/blog/e-liquid-ingredients-explained/) covers the full list, and our guide on [steeping](/blog/what-is-steeping-and-does-it-matter/) explains why some liquids taste better after resting.

## How to choose a ratio, step by step
1. Find out what your device is designed for, from the manual or product page.
2. Choose the matching ratio range: PG-leaning or 50/50 for pods, higher VG for sub-ohm tanks.
3. Match the nicotine type to the same device class.
4. Choose a bottle size that suits your use. See [e-liquid bottle sizes](/blog/e-liquid-bottle-sizes-30ml-60ml-100ml/).
5. Try one bottle first. If wicking, flavor or throat feel is off, adjust the ratio before changing everything else.

## Shopping for the right ratio
Our [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) range lists the ratio and strength on product pages where the manufacturer provides them, and our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) pages describe what each device is built for. Choose your options above the Add to Cart button, and check out with Cash App, Apple Pay, Chime, cryptocurrency or gift cards. Crypto and supported gift cards save 10%, orders of $200 or more after discounts ship free, and an adult 21 or older must sign on delivery. If you are unsure, message us through the [contact page](/contact/) and we will help you match a liquid to your hardware.

## A quick cheat sheet
Keep this short summary in mind when you shop. If your device is a small pod, a disposable refill system or a pen-style kit, look for 50/50 or PG-leaning liquids, usually nicotine salts, in 30 mL bottles. If your device is a mouth-to-lung tank, look for 50/50 or 60/40 liquids. If your device is a sub-ohm tank or box mod with large airflow, look for 70/30 VG or higher in freebase strengths from 0 to 6 mg/mL and bottle sizes of 60 to 100 mL. When a label does not state the ratio, ask us before you buy, because the ratio is the single detail that most often explains a leak, a gurgle or a burnt taste.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is a higher VG liquid always better for big clouds?
Only in the right hardware. VG creates dense vapor, but the device needs large coils, wide wicking channels and enough power to vaporize a thick liquid. In a small pod, high VG fails to wick and tastes burnt. Cloud size is as much about the hardware as the liquid.

### Why do some labels say "70/30" without saying which is which?
Brands differ. Some write PG first, others VG first, and many now write "70VG/30PG" to be clear. If a label is ambiguous, check the brand's product page or contact us, because assuming the wrong way around is exactly how thick liquid ends up in a small pod.

### Does the ratio affect nicotine strength?
The strength is a concentration in the finished liquid, so the ratio does not change the labelled strength. It does change how the liquid feels and how much vapor you make, which affects how satisfying a given strength seems.

### Can I add flavor shots or nicotine to change the ratio?
Adding anything to a finished liquid shifts the ratio and strength. Makers formulate carefully, and altering a bottle is rarely worth the trouble. If you want a different strength or ratio, buy that version instead.

### What ratio should I use for a disposable refill or pod?
Disposables are sealed, so there is nothing to refill. For refillable pods, follow the maker's recommendation, which is usually 50/50 or PG-leaning, and use nicotine salts if the pod is a low-power design.

### Why is my liquid thick in winter and runny in summer?
All liquids thin as they warm and thicken as they cool. A high-VG liquid kept in a cold room can become sluggish, so let it come to room temperature before filling. Do not heat it with a flame or a microwave.

faq.q: What does 50/50 mean on an e-liquid bottle?
faq.a: It means the liquid is made of roughly equal parts propylene glycol (PG) and vegetable glycerin (VG). It is a balanced blend that works in most pods and mouth-to-lung devices.

faq.q: Which ratio makes bigger clouds?
faq.a: Higher-VG liquids such as 70/30 VG or max VG produce denser vapor, but only in hardware designed for them, like sub-ohm tanks.

faq.q: Why does my pod taste burnt with a thick liquid?
faq.a: A high-VG liquid is too thick for a small coil to wick, so the coil dries out and burns. Use a 50/50 or PG-leaning liquid in small pods.

faq.q: Does PG or VG give more throat hit?
faq.a: PG gives more throat hit and carries flavor more strongly. VG feels softer and smoother.

faq.q: Can I mix different ratios?
faq.a: You can, but it changes the thickness and strength in ways that are hard to predict. It is easier to buy the ratio your hardware is designed for.

faq.q: Do disposables have a PG/VG ratio I need to match?
faq.a: No. The liquid in a disposable is pre-filled with a ratio chosen by the maker, so there is nothing to match.

title: Your First Vape Kit: A Plain-English Buyer's Guide
summary: Choosing a starter kit as an adult? Here is what is in the box, what to look for, and how to avoid the common beginner mistakes.
body:
A vape kit bundles everything needed to start: a battery device, a tank or pod and usually a charging cable. If you are an adult trying vaping for the first time, a kit is often a better value than a disposable.

## What comes in the box
Most starter kits include the device, one or two pods or a tank, a replacement coil and a USB cable. Some include a lanyard or case. Liquid is normally sold separately.

## Pod kit or tank kit
Pod kits are the simplest. You fill or swap a pod and press to draw or use a button. Tank kits add adjustable airflow and more power. For beginners, a pod kit is easier. Browse our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and compare sizes.

## Features that matter
- **Battery size:** measured in mAh. Larger lasts longer, but is bulkier.
- **Charging:** USB-C is faster and easier to replace than older ports.
- **Draw style:** auto-draw devices fire when you inhale; button devices fire when pressed.
- **Pod capacity:** bigger pods mean fewer refills.

## Picking a liquid
Match nicotine type to the device. Pods generally pair with nicotine salts, so look at [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) labeled for pods. Our guide to [salts versus freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/) explains why.

## Common beginner mistakes
- Overfilling a pod, which causes leaks.
- Not priming a new coil, which can burn it.
- Using the wrong liquid thickness.
Read [how to prime a coil](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/) before the first use. Nicotine is addictive and these products are for adults 21+.

faq.q: Do kits come with liquid?
faq.a: Usually not. Some pre-filled pod kits include a pod, but most kits require you to buy e-liquid separately.

faq.q: How long does a starter kit last?
faq.a: The device can last a long time with care. Pods and coils are consumable and are replaced every few weeks depending on use.

title: Rechargeable vs Non-Rechargeable Disposables Compared
summary: Should you buy a disposable you can recharge? Compare battery life, weight, price and waste so you pick the right type.
body:
Not every disposable vape is truly single-charge. Many modern devices include a USB-C port, and the difference changes how long you get out of the product.

## How non-rechargeable devices work
A non-rechargeable disposable ships with a battery sized to last roughly as long as the liquid inside. They are small and light, but if the battery drains early there is no fix. They tend to be cheaper and best for occasional use.

## How rechargeable devices work
A rechargeable disposable has a larger battery and a charging port. If the liquid outlasts the battery, you plug it in and carry on. That makes them suitable for heavy or daily use and for higher puff counts. See our [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/) guide.

## Compare at a glance
- **Weight and size:** non-rechargeable lighter.
- **Cost:** non-rechargeable cheaper up front.
- **Life:** rechargeable usually delivers the full stated puff count.
- **Waste:** both contain a lithium battery that needs proper recycling.

## How to tell which you are buying
Product pages and packaging mention a Type-C or USB-C port when one is present. Look for it in the listing for any device in [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). If the page is silent, ask support through the [contact page](/contact/).

## Disposal
Never put a battery-containing device in household trash if local rules say otherwise. See our [disposal guide](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). Nicotine is addictive; adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Is it okay to charge a non-rechargeable disposable?
faq.a: No. If there is no charging port, do not try to charge it by other means.

faq.q: Do rechargeable ones cost more?
faq.a: Usually slightly more, but they often give better value per puff.

title: Mesh Coils vs Standard Coils: Flavor, Heat and Lifespan
summary: Mesh coils heat more evenly than traditional wire coils. See how they compare for flavor, vapor and how long each type lasts.
body:
The coil is the heating element that turns liquid into vapor. In recent years mesh coils have become standard in many disposables and pods, and the reason is how they heat.

## Traditional wire coils
A wire coil is a wire wrapped around cotton. It heats from a small area and can create hot spots. Wire coils are simple, widely available and low-cost, and they remain common in many tanks.

## Mesh coils
A mesh coil uses a thin sheet of metal mesh with a much larger surface area touching the cotton. It heats more evenly and quickly, which usually gives smoother flavor and consistent vapor from the first puff to the last.

## How they compare
- **Flavor:** mesh often tastes cleaner and fuller.
- **Warm-up time:** mesh heats faster.
- **Lifespan:** well-matched mesh can last longer, but thick or sweet liquids shorten any coil.
- **Cost:** mesh coils are usually a little more expensive.

## Dual-mesh designs
Some devices use two mesh layers for even more surface area. They promise smooth, consistent flavor, though results still depend on liquid and battery.

## Shopping for replacements
If you are buying parts, check the exact model before ordering. Our [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) catalog lists compatibility. Care matters as much as type, so see [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/). Nicotine is addictive. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Do mesh coils last longer?
faq.a: They often do, but liquid type, power and care have a bigger effect than coil material.

faq.q: Can I use any coil in my tank?
faq.a: No. Coils are designed for specific tanks and pods, so always match the model.

title: What Is a Pod Vape? Open vs Closed Pods Explained
summary: Pod vapes are compact and simple. Learn the difference between open and closed pods, and how to pick one that fits your lifestyle.
body:
A pod vape is a small battery unit that uses a snap-in pod holding the liquid and coil. It is popular because it is compact, easy to use and less fiddly than a tank.

## Closed pods
Closed pods arrive pre-filled and are thrown away or recycled when empty. They are convenient and leak-resistant, but you are limited to the flavors the manufacturer sells for that device. Many [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) work this way.

## Open pods
Open pods are refillable. You fill them with your own e-liquid and replace the coil when it wears out. They cost less over time and give unlimited flavor choice, at the price of a little extra effort.

## Things to look for
- **Pod capacity:** typically 2 mL, which is the limit in many regions.
- **Coil type:** mesh coils give smoother flavor.
- **Battery:** 400 to 1,000 mAh is typical for pod devices.
- **Draw activation:** auto-draw is easy, button-fire gives more control.

## Choosing liquid
Pods pair well with nicotine salts. Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) designed for them, and check our [salts versus freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/) guide.

## Care tips
Do not overfill, keep pods upright when storing, and let a new coil soak before the first puff. Our guide on [priming a coil](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/) covers it. Nicotine is addictive; adults 21 and over only.

faq.q: Are pod vapes better than disposables?
faq.a: They suit people who vape often and want lower running costs. Disposables suit people who want zero upkeep.

faq.q: How often do pods need replacing?
faq.a: Closed pods when they are empty. Refillable pod coils typically every one to three weeks depending on use.

title: Sub-Ohm vs Mouth-to-Lung Vaping: What's the Difference?
summary: Two draw styles, two hardware setups. See how sub-ohm and mouth-to-lung differ in airflow, power, liquid choice and feel.
body:
Vaping styles are described by how you inhale. The two most common are mouth-to-lung (MTL) and sub-ohm direct-to-lung (DTL), and they require different gear.

## Mouth-to-lung
You draw vapor into your mouth first, pause, then inhale. It feels similar to drawing on a cigarette. MTL devices use tighter airflow, higher-resistance coils and lower power. This pairs well with nicotine salts and higher-PG liquids. Most pod systems and disposables are MTL.

## Direct-to-lung
You inhale directly into the lungs with a wide-open draw. Sub-ohm coils have resistance below one ohm, use more power and make more vapor. They work best with lower-strength, higher-VG freebase liquid.

## Key differences
- **Airflow:** MTL tight, DTL open.
- **Power:** MTL low, DTL high.
- **Liquid use:** DTL uses much more.
- **Nicotine strength:** MTL higher, DTL lower.

## Picking hardware
For MTL, start with a pod kit from our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). For DTL, look at box mods and sub-ohm tanks. Always match liquid to hardware; see [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## A caution on power
High-power devices need correctly rated batteries and careful handling. Read the manual, never mix batteries and keep devices away from heat. Nicotine is addictive; these products are for adults 21 and over.

faq.q: Which style is best for beginners?
faq.a: MTL is generally easier because the hardware is simpler and the liquid is lower volume.

faq.q: Can I do both with one device?
faq.a: Some adjustable devices support both, but they are usually designed primarily for one style.

title: How to Read an E-Liquid Label (Strength, Ratio, Warnings)
summary: Every e-liquid bottle carries the same key facts. Here is how to read bottle size, nicotine strength, PG/VG ratio and the required warning.
body:
An e-liquid label looks busy, but it follows a predictable pattern. Once you know where to look, you can compare bottles in seconds.

## Bottle size and fill
The volume appears in milliliters (mL), for example 30 mL or 100 mL. Large bottles often contain a "shortfill": less liquid than the bottle's capacity so you can add nicotine shots. Nicotine-ready bottles are filled to the top.

## Nicotine strength
Look for mg/mL or a percent. The conversion is simple: divide mg/mL by 10 to get percent. Our [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/) has the full table.

## PG/VG ratio
Printed as numbers such as 50/50 or 70/30, the first is usually PG and the second VG. The ratio guides which device suits the liquid; see [PG and VG explained](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## Nicotine type
Salts and freebase are labeled differently. Salts often say "nic salt" or "salt nicotine". If it is not stated, check the product page in [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/).

## Warning statement
Labels in the United States carry a warning that the product contains nicotine and that nicotine is an addictive chemical. If a bottle lacks this, do not buy it.

## Batch and date information
Many bottles show a batch code and best-by date. Use liquid before the date, and store it away from heat and light as explained in [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/).

## Child-resistant packaging
Look for a child-resistant cap. Always keep liquids out of reach of children and pets. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: What does shortfill mean?
faq.a: A shortfill bottle contains less liquid than its capacity, leaving room to add nicotine shots yourself.

faq.q: Why is there no nicotine on my bottle?
faq.a: Some liquids are sold at 0 mg for people who want flavor without nicotine. The label will say 0 mg or 0%.

title: 30 mL, 60 mL or 100 mL? Choosing the Right E-Liquid Bottle
summary: Bottle size changes both price and how fast you use liquid. Learn when a small 30 mL makes sense and when a 100 mL bottle saves money.
body:
E-liquid bottles come in several sizes. The best one is not always the largest, and the right choice depends on strength, device and how often you vape.

## 30 mL: salts and pods
Thirty milliliters is the standard size for nicotine salts. Because salts are high strength and used in small pods, a 30 mL bottle lasts a long time. They are also easy to carry and store. Browse them in our [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) range.

## 60 mL: balanced shortfills
Sixty milliliter bottles are common for freebase and for shortfill recipes. They suit regular users of small to mid-size tanks.

## 100 mL: tank users
Hundred-milliliter bottles are best for sub-ohm tanks, which burn through liquid. They usually offer the lowest price per milliliter, but only if you will use it before the best-by date.

## Price per milliliter
Divide the price by the size to compare fairly. A 100 mL bottle at $12 costs about 12 cents per mL, while a 30 mL at $12 costs 40 cents. That gap makes larger sizes attractive for heavy use of low-strength liquid.

## Freshness and storage
Large bottles stay open longer, so keep them cool and dark and use a smaller refill bottle for travel. See [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/) for details.

## Which should you pick?
Salts in pods: 30 mL. Freebase in small tanks: 60 mL. Freebase in large tanks: 100 mL. If you are unsure of your hardware, our [first vape kit guide](/blog/first-vape-kit-guide/) can help. Adults 21+ only; nicotine is addictive.

faq.q: Is a bigger bottle always cheaper?
faq.a: Per milliliter, usually yes. But it is only a saving if you finish it before it ages.

faq.q: Can I carry a large bottle when traveling?
faq.a: Rules vary. Decant into a small bottle for convenience and check carrier rules before you travel.

title: How to Compare Vape Prices: Cost per Puff and Cost per mL
summary: A low sticker price can be poor value. Use cost per puff, cost per mL and total running cost to compare vapes fairly.
body:
Vape prices vary widely, so a simple method helps you compare. These three numbers make it easy.

## Cost per puff (disposables)
Divide the price by the stated puff count. A $17.99 device rated at 30,000 puffs costs about six-hundredths of a cent per puff. A $12.99 device rated at 5,000 puffs costs about a quarter of a cent. Higher puff counts usually win on value, though real counts vary. Read [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/) for the caveats.

## Cost per mL (e-liquid)
Divide the price by the bottle size. Larger bottles are cheaper per mL, but salts are consumed slowly because of their strength, so a 30 mL bottle may last as long as a larger freebase bottle. Compare inside [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/).

## Running cost (kits)
For a refillable kit, add up the device, the liquid you will use per week and the replacement coils or pods. A kit often costs more up front but less per month than disposables.

## Check what is included
A multi-pack, free shipping threshold or crypto and gift card discount can change the total. We offer a discount for crypto and gift card payments, and free shipping on qualifying orders. See the [shipping policy](/shipping/).

## Beware false economy
The cheapest device is not a bargain if it fails early. Look at product details and brand reputation in our [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) listings before you decide.

## A quick example
Two items at $18 and $24 look far apart, but if the second lasts three times longer, it costs less per puff. Always compare the full picture. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Is cost per puff reliable?
faq.a: It is a useful guide, but because puff counts are estimates it should be treated as a comparison tool, not an exact figure.

faq.q: Do multi-pack deals save money?
faq.a: Often yes. Check whether the per-unit price drops enough to justify buying more than you will use soon.

title: How to Pick the Right Replacement Coil or Pod
summary: Coils and pods are not universal. Follow these steps to find the exact replacement for your device and avoid returns.
body:
Replacement coils and pods are the most common reason for a wrong-part order. They look similar, but fitments differ. Here is how to get it right the first time.

## Start with your device name
Find the exact model on the device or box, not just the brand. Many brands make a dozen pod systems that all use different pods.

## Check the series
Coil and pod listings usually name compatible devices. In our [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) category, each product states what it fits. If your device is not listed, do not guess.

## Match the resistance
Coils list a resistance in ohms. Lower resistance means more power and more vapor, higher resistance suits tighter draws. Use the resistance your device was designed for. Our guide to [sub-ohm and mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/) helps you decide.

## Pick the liquid type
Some coils suit thicker liquid and higher power, others suit thin salt-based liquid. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## Buy a spare
Keep one spare on hand so a worn coil does not leave you without a working device. Learn [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/).

## Avoid counterfeit parts
Buy from a reputable seller. Poorly made coils can taste burnt or fail early.

## When you are stuck
Send us the model name and a photo through the [contact page](/contact/) and we will point you to the right part. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Can I use a different brand's coil in my device?
faq.a: Generally no. Fitments and wattage ranges are specific, so use only parts listed as compatible.

faq.q: How do I know a coil needs replacing?
faq.a: A burnt taste, weak flavor or gurgling are the common signs.

title: Disposable Vapes With Screens: Are They Worth It?
summary: Display disposables show battery and liquid levels. See what the screen tells you, what it costs and whether you need one.
body:
A growing number of disposables include a small display. It is a nice feature, but is it worth paying for? That depends on how you vape.

## What the screen shows
Most displays show battery level and remaining liquid. Some show puff count, the current power mode or a charging indicator. The idea is to remove guesswork about when the device is nearly empty.

## Benefits
- **No surprises:** you see when the battery or liquid is low.
- **Planning:** you can top up the battery or order a replacement in time.
- **Mode feedback:** devices with power modes show which is active.

## Drawbacks
- **Price:** devices with screens usually cost slightly more.
- **Battery draw:** the display uses a little power.
- **Failure points:** one more component that can fail.

## Who benefits most
Heavy daily users and anyone who travels often get the most value, since running out is inconvenient. Occasional users can do fine without one.

## Alternatives
Many devices without screens use an LED that blinks when the battery is low. Our guide to [indicator lights](/blog/understanding-vape-device-indicator-lights/) explains the common patterns.

## Where to look
Filter [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) for models that mention a display in the description, and compare them using [price per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/). Adults 21+ only; nicotine is addictive.

faq.q: Does a screen mean a better device?
faq.a: Not automatically. It adds information, but flavor and performance depend on the coil, liquid and battery.

faq.q: Can the display be wrong?
faq.a: Liquid level on some devices is an estimate based on use, so treat it as a guide.

title: Adjustable Airflow Explained: Tighter or Looser Draw
summary: Airflow controls how easily air passes through your device. Learn how to adjust it for flavor, vapor and a comfortable draw.
body:
Many tanks and some pod devices include an airflow ring or slider. It looks minor, but it has a real effect on how your vape feels.

## What airflow does
Airflow sets how much air mixes with the vapor. Closing it restricts the draw and concentrates flavor. Opening it makes the draw easy and the vapor cooler and larger.

## Tight airflow
A tight draw is similar to drawing on a cigarette. It suits nicotine salts and mouth-to-lung style. Flavor is concentrated, and the throat feel is stronger.

## Open airflow
An open draw suits larger tanks and lower-strength liquid. The vapor is denser and cooler, and flavor is a little more diluted.

## How to find your setting
Start in the middle and move a quarter turn at a time. If the draw feels hot or harsh, open the airflow. If flavor is weak, close it a little. Take a few puffs at each change.

## Match with coil and liquid
Higher-resistance coils work with tight airflow; sub-ohm coils need more air. See [sub-ohm versus mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/). Liquids that are too thick can also cause gurgling when airflow is wrong; see [fixing a gurgling vape](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/).

## Choosing hardware
If you enjoy tuning, pick a kit with adjustable airflow from our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). Otherwise, a fixed-airflow pod is simpler. Adults 21 and over only.

faq.q: Does airflow change nicotine intake?
faq.a: Airflow changes how much vapor and air you draw per puff, which can change how strong it feels. Strength itself is set by the liquid.

faq.q: Is a loose draw better?
faq.a: It is a preference. Some people prefer a loose, cool draw and others a tight one.

title: Choosing a Vape for Travel: Size, Leaks and Battery
summary: Traveling with a vape takes planning. Compare compact devices, leak resistance and battery options for trips and commutes.
body:
Whether you are commuting or flying, a travel-friendly vape is compact, leak-resistant and easy to charge. Here is what to look for.

## Choose a compact device
Slim pod systems and small disposables slip into a pocket. Large box mods are bulky and need more careful packing.

## Leak resistance matters
Pressure changes during a flight can push liquid out of a full pod or tank. Closed pods and disposables resist leaks better than open tanks. If you carry refillable gear, keep it nearly empty and sealed in a bag. Read our guide to [stopping a vape from leaking](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/).

## Battery and charging
A USB-C rechargeable device is the easiest to top up from a power bank or laptop. Always carry batteries in your hand luggage, not checked bags. Our [airline rules overview](/blog/traveling-with-vapes-airline-rules/) explains the basics.

## Pack spares sensibly
Take one spare pod and a short charging cable. For refills, use small bottles instead of a large one.

## Check local laws
Vape rules differ between states and countries. Some places ban use in public spaces or even possession. Always check the rules where you are going; see [state and local vape laws](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## Where to shop
Browse compact [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) with travel in mind. Adults 21+ only, and keep products away from children.

faq.q: Can I vape on a plane?
faq.a: No. Vaping is prohibited on commercial flights, and devices must go in carry-on baggage.

faq.q: How do I stop leaks in my bag?
faq.a: Keep pods upright, nearly empty and in a sealed pouch, and avoid sudden pressure changes where possible.

title: Best Disposable Vapes for Flavor Lovers: How to Choose
summary: Want flavor above all? Here is how to choose a disposable by flavor family, cooling level and sweetness, and what to try first.
body:
If flavor drives your choice, you can narrow hundreds of options with a few questions. Use this approach to find a device you will enjoy to the last puff.

## Pick a flavor family
Fruit is the largest group: berry blends, citrus, tropical and melon. Mint and menthol are crisp, dessert flavors lean creamy and sweet, and tobacco profiles lean earthy. Decide which family you naturally prefer.

## Decide on cooling
Names that include "ice" usually add a cooling effect. It can brighten fruit flavors, but too much can mute sweetness. Try a version with and without ice to learn your preference. Our list of [ice flavors](/blog/ice-vape-flavors-guide/) goes deeper.

## Consider sweetness
Some recipes are very sweet, others tart or balanced. If you find sweet liquids heavy after a while, look for tart or mixed-fruit names with citrus.

## Mix and rotate
Many flavor fans keep two or three devices and rotate, which reduces taste fatigue. Check bulk and multi-pack offers in [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/).

## Quality factors
A mesh coil, steady battery and well-balanced recipe all improve flavor. See [mesh versus standard coils](/blog/dual-mesh-vs-single-mesh-coils/).

## Start small
Order one new flavor at a time before committing to a pack. Browse by taste in our flavor guides like [watermelon vapes](/blog/watermelon-vape-flavors-guide/) and [blue razz vapes](/blog/blue-razz-vape-flavors-guide/). Adults 21 and over only.

faq.q: Why does flavor fade after a while?
faq.a: Taste fatigue is common, so rotating between flavors can help. A weakening coil can also dull flavor.

faq.q: Do sweeter flavors use more liquid?
faq.a: Not by themselves, but very sweet liquids can leave residue on the coil and shorten its life.

title: Vapes for Adult Beginners: Where to Start Without Wasting Money
summary: New to vaping as an adult? Compare a first disposable, a pod kit and basic accessories, plus the mistakes that cost beginners money.
body:
Starting as an adult can feel overwhelming. The market is crowded, but a few sensible choices keep it simple and affordable.

## Option 1: a disposable
The simplest start. No refilling, no coils and no setup. Choose one with a flavor you already like and a mid-range puff count. See [how to choose a disposable](/blog/how-to-choose-a-disposable-vape/).

## Option 2: a pod kit
If you expect to use a vape regularly, a pod kit costs less over time. It needs a bit more learning, such as filling a pod and priming the coil. Our [first vape kit guide](/blog/first-vape-kit-guide/) explains what to buy.

## Pick the right nicotine
Nicotine strength should match the device. Read our [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/). Remember nicotine is addictive; if you do not already use nicotine, vaping is not recommended.

## Avoid these mistakes
- Buying the largest puff count right away.
- Using the wrong liquid thickness for your pod.
- Not charging a rechargeable device before first use.
- Keeping a vape in a hot car, which can harm the battery.

## Accessories worth having
A spare pod or coil and a USB-C cable are enough. Skip extras until you know what you like.

## Age and ID
You must be 21 or older, and delivery requires an adult signature with photo ID. See [age verification explained](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/). Browse our [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) when ready.

faq.q: Is a disposable or a kit better for a beginner?
faq.a: A disposable is easier to start, while a kit is cheaper if you plan to vape regularly.

faq.q: How much should I spend to start?
faq.a: A disposable or basic pod kit in the $15 to $40 range is typical. Spending more is not required to begin.
