title: How to Pay With Bitcoin at One Stop Vape Store, Step by Step
summary: Pay for your order with Bitcoin in a few minutes. Follow this walkthrough from choosing BTC at checkout to sending the exact amount.
body:
Bitcoin (BTC) is one of the cryptocurrency options at One Stop Vape Store checkout, and paying with it qualifies for our 10% crypto discount. If you have paid with Bitcoin before, the process will feel familiar. If you have not, this guide walks through every step in the order you will see it, explains the numbers on the payment window, covers fees and timing, and lists the mistakes that cause most delays. It is written for adults aged 21 and over, and nothing here is financial advice.

## Before you start
You need a wallet or an exchange account that holds Bitcoin and lets you send it to an outside address. Popular choices include mobile wallets, hardware wallets and the withdrawal feature of a regulated exchange. If you do not own any Bitcoin yet, read [how to buy crypto with a card](/blog/how-to-buy-crypto-with-a-card/) first, because buying can take from a few minutes to a day depending on the provider and your verification status.

Two practical points before you begin. First, check that your wallet or exchange has enough Bitcoin to cover both the order amount and the network fee, because the fee is paid on top. Second, if you are sending from an exchange, look for minimum withdrawal limits and any withdrawal fee the exchange charges, which is separate from the network fee. Both are easier to plan for before you open the payment window than after.

## Step 1: fill your cart and open checkout
Add products to your cart and go to checkout. Where a product offers options such as a strength or pack size, choose them on the product page before you add it, so the right option appears in your cart. Enter your contact and shipping details and confirm you are 21 or older. We require an email address because order updates and your private order link are sent there. The minimum order is $100, and orders of $200 or more after discounts ship free; smaller orders pay a flat $15 shipping fee. See [minimum order and free shipping explained](/blog/minimum-order-and-free-shipping-explained/).

## Step 2: choose Cryptocurrency and Bitcoin
Select Cryptocurrency as the payment method, then choose Bitcoin from the token list. The checkout page shows the discount in your order summary, so you can see the total you will owe in dollars before the payment window opens. The payment window opens straight away when you continue.

## Step 3: read the payment window
The window shows everything you need in one place:

- **Your order reference,** which identifies your order.
- **The dollar amount due** after the 10% crypto discount and including any shipping.
- **The amount of BTC to send,** converted from the dollar total at the live exchange rate.
- **A QR code and the wallet address** for the Bitcoin network.
- **Copy buttons** next to the address and amount so you do not have to type them.

The BTC amount is based on the live rate and refreshes about every 30 seconds, so send the amount shown at the time you pay. Because Bitcoin's price moves, the amount of BTC can differ slightly from one minute to the next, but the dollar value stays the same. Always use the copy button, because one wrong character in a Bitcoin address sends your money to a different wallet and it cannot be reversed.

## Step 4: send from your wallet
Open your wallet. You can either scan the QR code, which fills in the address, or paste the address and enter the amount manually. Check the first and last few characters of the address against the window before you confirm. Choose the network fee your wallet suggests, and confirm the transaction. Network fees are paid by you on top of the order amount, and they go to the network, not to us.

If your wallet lets you choose a fee level, a standard or medium fee is usually fine for a normal order. A very low fee can leave a transaction waiting for a long time when the network is busy, and a very high fee wastes money. Our guide to [crypto network fees explained](/blog/crypto-network-fees-explained/) covers how fees work.

## Step 5: press "I have paid"
Return to the payment window and press the button once your wallet shows the transaction as sent. Your order is placed and you land on the order status page. From there, our system reads public blockchain data for the shop wallet and looks for an incoming transfer that fits your order. You do not need to wait for anyone to read a screenshot. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/) for what is checked.

## How long does it take?
Bitcoin transactions are usually visible on the network within a minute or two, but they are not final until they have confirmations. A confirmation is a block added to the chain that includes your transaction. One confirmation often takes about ten minutes, though it can be faster or slower. Our status page shows when a payment is detected and when it is confirmed, and we email you when it is matched. After confirmation your order enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours before it ships. See [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/).

## What the amounts mean
- **Dollar total:** the figure that matters for your order. Everything is priced in US dollars.
- **BTC amount:** the dollar total converted at the rate when the window was opened or refreshed.
- **Tolerance:** because prices move between quote and payment, we allow a small tolerance when matching. A tiny shortfall caused by market movement is not a problem, but a substantial shortfall will show as underpaid. Read [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/).
- **Network fee:** separate and extra. If your wallet deducts the fee from the amount you send, the recipient receives less. Send enough that the full amount arrives.

## Sending from an exchange
Many people pay straight from an exchange. That works, but two details cause most problems. First, some exchanges let you choose the amount to withdraw and take their own fee out of it, which can leave the received amount short. Add the exchange's fee to the amount you enter. Second, some exchanges batch or delay withdrawals for security checks, which can make the transaction appear later than expected. If your withdrawal is pending, you can still press "I have paid" so the order is in the system, then wait for the transfer to arrive. Our guide to [sending crypto from an exchange to a wallet](/blog/send-crypto-from-an-exchange-to-a-wallet/) goes through it in detail.

## Common mistakes
- **Using the wrong network.** Bitcoin addresses on the Bitcoin network only receive BTC. If you hold another asset, choose that token in checkout instead.
- **Typing the address.** Always copy and paste or scan.
- **Sending an old amount.** If you leave the window open for a long time, refresh it and send the current amount.
- **Resending when nothing shows.** Do not send a second payment. A payment can be pending for a while. Check the status page first and contact us if it is stuck.
- **Sharing private keys.** We never ask for private keys or seed phrases. Never send them to anyone.

## If something looks wrong
If the status page shows waiting for longer than you expect, or shows underpaid, do not resend. Add your transaction hash and a screenshot on the status page, which helps us find the transfer quickly. See [how to upload a payment screenshot](/blog/how-to-upload-a-payment-screenshot/). You can also contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your order reference.

## Privacy and security
We only use public blockchain data to match payments. Your wallet balance and other transactions are not visible to us. To keep your own funds secure, use a wallet you trust, keep your recovery phrase offline and never share it. If you want to understand how networks differ, read [what is a crypto network](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/).

## After payment
Once your payment is confirmed you receive an email, and your order status updates. We process orders within 24 to 72 business hours and ship from our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse with tracking by a regional carrier. Delivery requires an adult aged 21 or older to sign. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) and [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/).

## Why choose Bitcoin?
Bitcoin is the most widely supported cryptocurrency, so almost every exchange and wallet can send it. The trade-offs are that confirmations can take longer than some other networks and fees can rise when the network is busy. If you want a cheaper, faster option, compare [USDT on TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/), [USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/) or [Solana](/blog/pay-with-solana-sol/). Our [payment methods comparison](/blog/payment-methods-compared/) lays out speed, fees and discounts side by side.

## A quick checklist before you press send
Confirm the token is Bitcoin and the network is Bitcoin. Confirm the address on your wallet screen matches the window. Confirm the amount covers the order and that the fee is paid on top. Then send once, press "I have paid", and watch the status page. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

### Can I pay in more than one transaction?
It is best to send a single transaction for the full amount, because our system matches one transaction to one order. If you must split a payment, contact us before you send so we can note it against your order and match both transfers.

title: USDT on ERC20 or TRC20? Choosing the Right Network to Pay
summary: We accept Tether (USDT) on Ethereum (ERC20) and Tron (TRC20). Compare fees, speed and how to pick the network that suits your wallet.
body:
USDT, also called Tether, is a stablecoin designed to track the US dollar. That makes it popular for payments, because the amount you owe does not swing the way Bitcoin or Ethereum can between the moment you see a price and the moment you pay. At One Stop Vape Store checkout you choose USDT and then choose a network for it, and that second choice matters more than most people expect. This guide explains why there are two networks, how they differ on fees and speed, how to choose, what to do if you pick wrong and how to send correctly. It is for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## Why there are two networks
A token is not tied to a single blockchain. The same token can exist on several blockchains at once, each one a separate ledger with its own address format, its own fees and its own rules. We accept USDT on **Ethereum**, written ERC20, and on **Tron**, written TRC20. Each has its own wallet address in our payment window, and the network you select at checkout decides which address is shown. You must send on the network you selected.

Think of it like sending a parcel by two different carriers. The contents are the same, but each carrier has its own address system, and a parcel handed to the wrong carrier does not arrive. If you want the bigger picture, read [what is a crypto network](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/).

## TRC20: usually cheaper and quick
Tron transfers typically cost much less than Ethereum and settle within a minute or two. For a payment of a few hundred dollars, many people choose TRC20 to keep fees low. The main requirement is that your wallet or exchange must support Tron withdrawals, and some wallets need a small amount of Tron's native currency, TRX, to cover energy or bandwidth costs. Exchanges that support TRC20 withdrawals usually handle this for you and show the fee in USDT.

## ERC20: widely supported
Ethereum is the most widely supported smart-contract network, so almost every wallet and exchange can send USDT on it. The cost is that fees can be higher, especially when the network is busy, and they are paid in ETH. If you hold USDT on Ethereum already, or your exchange offers only ERC20, it is a perfectly sensible choice. Just make sure you have enough ETH in the wallet to pay the fee, because the transfer cannot be made without it.

## Side-by-side comparison
- **Typical cost:** TRC20 is usually a small fraction of an ERC20 fee. ERC20 fees rise with network traffic.
- **Speed:** both usually confirm within minutes; TRC20 often feels faster.
- **Compatibility:** ERC20 is supported almost everywhere; TRC20 is supported by most exchanges and many wallets but not all.
- **Gas or fee currency:** ERC20 needs ETH; TRC20 needs TRX or an exchange that covers it.
- **Address format:** ERC20 addresses start with 0x; TRC20 addresses start with T.

## How to choose
1. **If you want the lowest fee,** choose TRC20, provided your wallet supports it.
2. **If your balance is already on one network,** use that one. Do not bridge or swap just to pay, because bridging adds cost and risk.
3. **If you want maximum compatibility,** choose ERC20.
4. **If you are sending from an exchange,** check which networks the exchange lists for USDT withdrawals and what each costs, then pick the cheaper one we support.

## The most important rule
Send on exactly the network shown in the payment window. A USDT transfer on the wrong network will not arrive at the address and may not be recoverable. The address formats make an accidental mix-up less likely, because a Tron address will not be accepted by an Ethereum withdrawal form, but some wallets let you paste an address and pick any network, which is where mistakes happen. Always select the network in your wallet that matches the window, and compare the address you paste against the window before you confirm. If you have already sent on the wrong network, read [what to do after sending crypto on the wrong network](/blog/sent-crypto-on-the-wrong-network/) and contact us promptly with your order reference and transaction hash.

## Step-by-step payment
1. At checkout choose Cryptocurrency, then USDT, then the network.
2. The payment window shows your order reference, the amount in USDT, a QR code and the address for that network.
3. In your wallet, choose USDT, choose the matching network, scan the QR or paste the address and enter the amount. Use the copy buttons to avoid typing errors.
4. Confirm the transfer, paying the network fee on top.
5. Press "I have paid". Your order is placed and our system watches the blockchain for a matching transfer. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/).

Because USDT is pegged to the dollar, the amount to send is essentially your dollar total after the crypto discount, so there is no exchange-rate movement to worry about. That is one of the reasons stablecoins are convenient for orders.

## Fees in practice
The fee is paid by you and goes to the network. On Tron it is usually small and predictable. On Ethereum it varies with demand and can be noticeably larger for a small payment. If you are paying a smaller order, the fee can be a meaningful share of the total, which is another reason many customers prefer TRC20. Our guide to [crypto network fees explained](/blog/crypto-network-fees-explained/) goes into more detail, including how to estimate fees before you send.

## Amount and tolerance
Send the amount shown. If your exchange takes its withdrawal fee out of the amount you enter, the received amount will be lower than you intended, so add the exchange's fee to the amount you enter. A tiny difference is tolerated, but a larger shortfall shows as underpaid; see [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/).

## What the discount means for USDT
Cryptocurrency payments save 10% on your order total, which applies equally whichever token or network you choose. The discount is calculated on your product subtotal before shipping is added. Orders of $200 or more after discounts ship free, and smaller orders pay a flat $15 shipping fee. Read [the 10% crypto and gift card discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/) for worked examples.

## Common mistakes
- **Choosing a network your wallet does not support.** Check before you start.
- **Forgetting the fee currency.** ERC20 needs ETH; TRC20 may need TRX.
- **Sending USDC or another token by mistake.** Choose USDT in both checkout and your wallet.
- **Resending when a payment is pending.** Wait for the status page and contact us if it is stuck.
- **Assuming all USDT is the same.** The network is part of the address, so match it.

## After your payment is confirmed
We email you once the transfer is matched and confirmed. Orders are processed within 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse and ship with tracking. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery, as described in [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/). If you would like to compare other tokens, see [paying with USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/), [paying with Ethereum](/blog/pay-with-ethereum-eth/) and [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I use the same wallet for both networks?
Many wallets hold USDT on both networks and show them as separate balances. Check which balance you are spending, because the network shown in our window must match the network of the balance you send from. If your wallet shows one combined USDT balance, look for a network selector on the send screen.

### Which network is better for a small order?
For smaller payments the fee is a bigger share of the total, so the cheaper network usually makes more sense. On most days that is TRC20. If your funds are on Ethereum, compare the quoted fee with the order size before you send, and consider whether moving funds first would cost more than it saves.

### What should I do before sending a large amount?
Send nothing until you have checked the address and network twice. Some people send a very small test amount first to confirm everything works, but remember that our system matches one transaction to one order, so tell us if you do this and give us both transaction hashes. For a normal order, careful checking of the address and network is enough.

### How do I find my transaction hash?
Your wallet or exchange shows it in the transaction details after you send, often called TXID or transaction hash. Copy it into the status page together with a screenshot if we ask for one, so we can find the transfer immediately.

### Does choosing a network change what I pay?
The dollar total is the same on either network. The only difference is the network fee, which you pay to the network, not to us, and which differs between ERC20 and TRC20.

### What if my exchange only supports one network?
Then use that one, provided it is one we accept. We accept USDT on Ethereum (ERC20) and Tron (TRC20). If your exchange offers a different network, choose another token or another way to pay, and contact us if you are unsure.

faq.q: Which USDT network is cheaper, ERC20 or TRC20?
faq.a: TRC20 (Tron) is usually much cheaper than ERC20 (Ethereum), whose fees rise when the network is busy.

faq.q: What happens if I send USDT on the wrong network?
faq.a: The funds will not arrive at the address and may not be recoverable. Contact us immediately with your order reference and transaction hash.

faq.q: Do I need ETH or TRX to send USDT?
faq.a: ERC20 transfers need ETH for the fee. TRC20 transfers may need TRX, although many exchanges cover this for you.

faq.q: Is the discount the same for both networks?
faq.a: Yes. Any cryptocurrency payment saves 10% on your order total, whichever token or network you choose.

faq.q: Why is the USDT amount stable?
faq.a: USDT is pegged to the US dollar, so the amount to send is essentially your dollar total after the crypto discount.

faq.q: How do I know which network my wallet supports?
faq.a: Open your wallet's USDT send screen and look for the list of networks. Match one of them with the network shown in our payment window.

title: Paying With USDC on Solana: Fast, Low-Fee Stablecoin Payments
summary: USDC on the Solana network settles in seconds with tiny fees. Here is how to pay your order and avoid the common mistakes.
body:
USDC is a stablecoin pegged to the US dollar, and on the Solana network it moves in seconds and costs a fraction of a cent. That makes it one of the most convenient ways to pay an order at One Stop Vape Store: the amount you send is essentially your dollar total, so there is no exchange-rate movement to worry about, and USDC payments qualify for our 10% crypto discount. This guide explains what you need, walks through each step, covers the mistakes that cause most problems, explains how detection works and compares USDC on Solana with other options. It is for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## What you need
You need a wallet that supports Solana and holds USDC, such as a popular browser or mobile Solana wallet, or an exchange that allows USDC withdrawals on Solana. If you use a self-custody wallet, you also need a tiny amount of SOL in the same wallet to cover the network fee, because Solana fees are paid in SOL even when you send USDC. A few cents' worth is plenty. If you use an exchange, the exchange usually deducts the fee for you, often in USDC.

## Why USDC on Solana
- **Speed:** transfers usually finish in seconds.
- **Cost:** the fee is a fraction of a cent, so almost all of the 10% saving stays with you.
- **Stable amount:** because USDC tracks the dollar, you owe the same dollar value regardless of market moves.
- **Simple matching:** the amount is predictable, so detection is straightforward.

If you want a general explanation of why networks matter, read [what is a crypto network](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/).

## Step by step
1. Fill your cart, choose options such as strength and pack size on the product page and go to checkout. Enter your contact and shipping details and confirm you are 21 or older.
2. Choose Cryptocurrency at checkout, then USDC. Solana is the only network offered for USDC at our store.
3. In the payment window, copy the wallet address or scan the QR code. Use the copy button to avoid typing errors.
4. In your wallet, choose Send, select USDC and paste the address. Check the first and last characters.
5. Enter the amount shown and confirm.
6. Press "I have paid". Your order is placed and you land on the status page, where your payment is looked for on the Solana network and confirmed automatically.

## How detection works
Our system reads public Solana data for the shop wallet and looks for an incoming USDC transfer that fits your order: the right token, the right address, a dollar value close to your total, a recent time and a transaction that has not paid another order. When a transfer matches, we email you and the order moves into processing. Because USDC is a dollar stablecoin, the amount matches your total closely, which keeps tolerance concerns small. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/).

## Common mistakes
- **Sending USDC on a different network, such as Ethereum.** It will not arrive at our Solana address and may not be recoverable. Select Solana in your wallet or exchange.
- **Sending SOL instead of USDC.** They are different assets. If you chose USDC at checkout, send USDC.
- **Forgetting a little SOL for fees in a self-custody wallet.** Without it, the transfer cannot be made.
- **Sending a different stablecoin.** USDT is a different token with its own options. Choose it at checkout if you prefer USDT. See [USDT on ERC20 or TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/).
- **Resending a pending payment.** Check the status page and contact us first.

## Exchange withdrawals
If you pay from an exchange, choose USDC as the asset and Solana as the network on the withdrawal screen. Check the minimum and the fee, and if the exchange deducts its fee from the amount you enter, add the fee on top so the full amount arrives. Some exchanges hold new withdrawal addresses for a short security period. Our guide to [sending crypto from an exchange to a wallet](/blog/send-crypto-from-an-exchange-to-a-wallet/) covers the details.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is USDC the same as USDT?
No. Both are dollar stablecoins issued by different companies, and each exists on several networks. At our store, USDC is offered on Solana, and USDT is offered on Ethereum (ERC20) and Tron (TRC20). Choose the one your wallet holds.

### Do I get the 10% discount with USDC?
Yes. The discount is calculated on your product subtotal and applied automatically when you choose Cryptocurrency. Shipping is added afterward, and free shipping applies to orders of $200 or more after discount. See [the 10% crypto and gift card discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/).

### What if my wallet shows a different network name?
Look for Solana, SOL or SPL in the network list. If your wallet or exchange does not offer Solana for USDC, choose a different token or network that it does support.

### Can I buy USDC if I do not have any?
Yes. Read [how to buy crypto with a card](/blog/how-to-buy-crypto-with-a-card/). Buy USDC, choose Solana as the network when you withdraw, and then send it to our address.

## After your payment is confirmed
You receive an email, and your order status updates. We process orders within 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse and ship with tracking by a regional carrier. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) and [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/).

## If your payment looks short
If the status page shows underpaid, do not resend the full amount. A small shortfall is usually caused by an exchange fee being deducted from the amount. Contact us with your order reference and transaction hash, and we will tell you what is needed. See [underpaid messages](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/). Browse the [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) range, and compare every option in [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What happens after you pay with USDC on Solana
USDC transfers on Solana are usually detected within seconds to a couple of minutes, and the status page updates on its own. Once your payment is confirmed, you receive an email and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and the regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). If you need to change something, read [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/) before your order ships.

## Staying protected when you pay with USDC
Only trust payment instructions that come through our official email, our WhatsApp number or your private order page. Check that your wallet or exchange is set to the Solana network and the USDC asset before you confirm, because USDC on another network will not reach our address. We never ask for your passwords, PINs, card numbers, private keys or recovery phrases, and no genuine order needs them. Be wary of anyone who contacts you out of the blue claiming to represent the store, offers a different address or account to pay or pushes you to pay quickly outside the order. If a message does not match your order number and amount exactly, stop and contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) before you send anything. For more on keeping your account details secure, see [gift card code security tips](/blog/gift-card-code-security-tips/) and [why we need your email and phone](/blog/why-we-need-your-email-and-phone/).

## A worked example
Suppose your cart is $320. Paying with USDC applies the 10% discount, so the product total is $288.00, and shipping is free because the amount after discount is above $200. The payment window shows 288 USDC. In a self-custody wallet holding USDC and a few cents of SOL, you choose Send, select USDC, paste the address, enter 288 and confirm. The fee is a fraction of a cent, paid in SOL. If you use an exchange that deducts a 1 USDC withdrawal fee from the amount, enter 289 so that 288 arrives. You press "I have paid", the status page detects the transfer and your order is confirmed. Because USDC tracks the dollar, there is no rate movement to worry about.

## Comparing USDC on Solana with the alternatives
- **USDT on Tron (TRC20):** also cheap and fast, widely supported by exchanges. See [USDT ERC20 vs TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/).
- **SOL:** the same network and speed, but the amount moves with the price. See [paying with Solana](/blog/pay-with-solana-sol/).
- **Bitcoin:** the most widely held, but slower to confirm. See [how to pay with Bitcoin](/blog/how-to-pay-with-bitcoin/).

## A final checklist before you send
- Choose USDC and the Solana network in your wallet or exchange.
- Keep a few cents of SOL in a self-custody wallet for the fee.
- Add the exchange fee on top if it is deducted from the amount.
- Compare the address with the window before you confirm.

USDC on Solana is one of the simplest crypto routes because the amount is stable and fees are tiny. If anything looks wrong, contact us before you resend.

title: Paying With Ethereum (ETH): What to Know Before You Send
summary: Ethereum is supported at checkout. Learn how the live rate, gas fees and confirmations work so your ETH payment goes through smoothly.
body:
Ethereum (ETH) is one of the most widely held cryptocurrencies, and it is a popular way to pay at One Stop Vape Store because it qualifies for our 10% crypto discount. Paying with Ethereum is straightforward, but it has two features that catch newcomers out: the live exchange rate moves quickly, and every transfer pays a network fee called gas. This guide explains the whole process, how to estimate and reduce fees, how confirmation works, the mistakes to avoid and when another token might suit you better. It is for adults aged 21 and over, and it is not financial advice.

## The live quote
When you open the payment window we show the amount of ETH equal to your order total after the discount, based on a live rate. The rate refreshes about every 30 seconds, so the ETH figure can change slightly while you read it, while the dollar value of your order stays the same. ETH can move quickly, so send soon after you open the window, and if you leave it open for a long time, refresh it and send the current amount.

A useful way to think about it is that you owe a dollar amount, and the window tells you how much ETH equals that amount right now. If the price of ETH rises while you wait, you owe slightly less ETH; if it falls, slightly more. A small tolerance allows for movement between the quote and the confirmation, but a large gap shows as underpaid. See [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/).

## Gas fees
Every Ethereum transfer pays a network fee called gas. The fee is charged by your wallet on top of the amount you send, it is paid to the network rather than to us, and it changes with network demand. When many people are using Ethereum, gas rises; when it is quiet, gas falls. A simple transfer of ETH from one address to another uses a standard amount of gas, so the cost depends mostly on the current price per unit of gas.

Check the estimate your wallet shows before you confirm. If the fee looks unusually high, you can wait for a quieter time, such as early morning in US time zones or weekends, or choose a different payment token with lower fees. For a deeper explanation, read [crypto network fees explained](/blog/crypto-network-fees-explained/).

### Keeping enough for gas
Make sure your wallet holds enough ETH for both the payment amount and the gas fee. If you send your entire balance as the payment amount, there will be nothing left for gas and the transfer will fail or the wallet will reduce the amount. Leave a small buffer, and remember that the fee is separate from the amount we ask for.

## Step by step
1. Fill your cart, choose options such as strength and pack size on the product page, and go to checkout. Enter your details and confirm you are 21 or older.
2. Choose Cryptocurrency, then Ethereum. The order summary shows the 10% discount and your total.
3. In the payment window, copy the address or scan the QR code. Use the copy buttons to avoid typing errors.
4. In your wallet, choose ETH on the Ethereum network, paste the address and enter the amount shown.
5. Review the gas fee, confirm the transaction and wait for your wallet to show it as sent.
6. Press "I have paid" so we can find the transaction. Your order is placed and you land on the status page.

## Confirmation
We look for your transfer on the Ethereum network and match it to your order automatically, checking the address, the amount in dollars, the time and that the transaction has not already paid another order. A confirmed transfer sends you an email and moves the order to payment confirmed. Ethereum transactions usually confirm within a minute or a few minutes, depending on gas and network activity. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/) for the full list of checks.

After payment is confirmed, the order enters processing. We process orders within 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse and ship with tracking by a regional carrier. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery. See [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/).

## Native ETH only
Send ETH itself on the Ethereum network. Do not send tokens such as USDT or USDC to the ETH address unless the payment window asks for that token, because the window is built to match the token you chose and recovery of a wrong token is not guaranteed. In the same way, do not send ETH on a different network, such as a layer-2 network or another chain that also uses the ETH name, because it will not arrive at our Ethereum address. If you are unsure, read [what is a crypto network](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/).

## Sending from an exchange
Many customers pay straight from an exchange. Check that the exchange lets you withdraw ETH on the Ethereum network, check its minimum withdrawal and its fee, and add the exchange's fee to the amount if it deducts the fee from what you send. Some exchanges also hold new withdrawal addresses for a short security period, which is worth knowing before you start. Our guide to [sending crypto from an exchange to a wallet](/blog/send-crypto-from-an-exchange-to-a-wallet/) walks through the details.

## Typical timings
- **Detection:** a transfer usually appears within a minute of being broadcast.
- **Confirmation:** usually a few minutes.
- **Stuck transactions:** if gas was set too low, a transfer can sit pending. Many wallets let you speed it up or cancel and resend; do not send a second payment without checking.
- **Processing and shipping:** 24 to 72 business hours after confirmation.

## Common mistakes
- **Sending a token instead of ETH.** Check the asset in your wallet before you confirm.
- **Using the wrong network.** Match the Ethereum network exactly.
- **Typing the address.** Always copy or scan, and compare the first and last characters.
- **Sending your whole balance.** Leave enough for gas.
- **Sending an outdated amount.** Refresh the window if it has been open a while.
- **Resending when a transfer is pending.** Check your wallet and our status page first.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is Ethereum a good choice for small orders?
For smaller orders, gas can be a noticeable share of the total. If you are paying a low-value order, compare the fee with cheaper options such as USDT on Tron or Solana before you decide.

### Can I pay from a hardware wallet?
Yes. Use it exactly like any other wallet: scan or paste the address, confirm the amount and approve on the device. Check the address on the device screen as well as the computer screen.

### Do I get the 10% discount with ETH?
Yes. Every supported cryptocurrency qualifies. The discount is calculated on the product subtotal and applied automatically. See [the 10% crypto and gift card discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/) for worked examples.

### What if I paid slightly too little?
A very small difference from price movement is tolerated. If the gap is larger, the order shows as underpaid and we will tell you what to do. Do not resend the full amount; contact us with your order reference.

## Lower-fee alternatives
If gas is high, stablecoins on cheaper networks are an alternative: see [USDT on ERC20 or TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/) and [USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/). You can compare every option in [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/). Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What happens after you pay with Ethereum
Ethereum transfers are matched to your order automatically, so there is usually nothing more for you to do after pressing the button. Once your payment is confirmed, you receive an email and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and the regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). If you need to change something, read [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/) before your order ships.

## Staying protected when you pay with Ethereum
Only trust payment instructions that come through our official email, our WhatsApp number or your private order page. Always compare the address on your wallet screen with the address in the window before confirming, because a single wrong character sends funds somewhere else. We never ask for your passwords, PINs, card numbers, private keys or recovery phrases, and no genuine order needs them. Be wary of anyone who contacts you out of the blue claiming to represent the store, offers a different address or account to pay or pushes you to pay quickly outside the order. If a message does not match your order number and amount exactly, stop and contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) before you send anything. For more on keeping your account details secure, see [gift card code security tips](/blog/gift-card-code-security-tips/) and [why we need your email and phone](/blog/why-we-need-your-email-and-phone/).

## A final checklist before you send
- Choose ETH on the Ethereum network, not a token and not another network.
- Compare the first and last characters of the address with the window.
- Make sure your balance covers the amount plus gas.
- Refresh the window if it has been open for a while.

Taking a minute to run through the list prevents almost every problem we see. If something still looks wrong, contact us before you resend.

faq.a: You do. It is charged by your wallet on top of the amount and goes to the network, not to us.

faq.a: No. Send ETH itself on the Ethereum network. Tokens sent to the wrong payment address may not be recoverable.

faq.a: Usually a few minutes to confirm, depending on gas and network activity.

faq.a: Check your wallet for a speed-up option and do not resend until you have checked our status page. Contact us with your order reference if it stays pending.

title: Paying With BNB (BNB Smart Chain): A Practical Guide
summary: BNB is accepted on BNB Smart Chain (BEP20). See how to send it correctly and how BNB payments are confirmed.
body:
BNB is accepted on the BNB Smart Chain network, also called BSC or BEP20. It is a convenient option if your funds already sit on Binance or another BSC wallet, because transfers on this network are fast and cheap. At One Stop Vape Store, BNB payments qualify for our 10% crypto discount like every other supported coin. This guide explains how to pay with BNB, how to make sure you pick the right network, how confirmation works for BNB (which differs from some other coins), how to handle exchange fees and minimums and what to do if something looks wrong. It is for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## Know the network
Choose BNB at checkout and the payment window shows the BNB Smart Chain address. BNB exists on several networks, and the names are confusing. The older Binance Chain used the BEP2 standard, while BNB Smart Chain uses BEP20 and an Ethereum-style address beginning with 0x. Our payment address is on BNB Smart Chain. When you withdraw from an exchange or send from a wallet, make sure the network says BNB Smart Chain, BSC or BEP20, not BEP2 and not another chain.

If you want a general explanation of why networks matter, read [what is a crypto network](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/). The short version is that an address is only valid on the network it belongs to, and sending on the wrong network can mean the funds are lost.

## Step by step
1. Fill your cart, choose your options on the product page and go to checkout. Enter your contact and shipping details and confirm you are 21 or older.
2. Choose Cryptocurrency and select BNB. The order summary shows the 10% discount.
3. In the payment window, copy the address and the amount. The amount of BNB is converted from your dollar total at the live rate, refreshed about every 30 seconds.
4. In your exchange or wallet, withdraw or send BNB, selecting BNB Smart Chain (BEP20) as the network.
5. Confirm the transfer and wait for it to show as sent.
6. Press "I have paid" in the payment window, then upload a screenshot on the status page.

## How confirmation works for BNB
Some networks, such as Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana, are matched to orders automatically by reading public blockchain data. BNB Smart Chain payments are currently confirmed by our team after you upload a screenshot on the status page, so allow a little extra time during business hours compared with automatic networks. To help us confirm quickly, include a clear screenshot of the transaction and, if you can, paste the transaction hash into the status page. The hash is a long string of characters your wallet or exchange shows after you send.

Customer service hours are Monday to Friday, 8AM to 5PM Arizona time. If you pay outside those hours, expect the check the next business morning. After confirmation, the order enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours before it ships. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/) for how automatic and manual checks differ, and [how to upload a payment screenshot](/blog/how-to-upload-a-payment-screenshot/) for what makes a good screenshot.

## Check the fee and minimum
Exchanges set their own withdrawal minimums and fees, and these are separate from the network fee. Before you send, check the minimum withdrawal for BNB on BNB Smart Chain and the fee the exchange charges. Make sure the net amount arriving equals the amount shown in our window. If the exchange deducts its fee from the amount you enter, add the fee on top so the full amount arrives. BNB Smart Chain fees are usually very small, which is one of the reasons people like the network.

## What the amount means
Your order is priced in US dollars. The BNB amount is the dollar total converted at the live rate. BNB's price moves, so the figure can differ slightly from minute to minute. A small tolerance allows for movement between the quote and the confirmation, but a large gap shows as underpaid. To avoid trouble, send the amount shown, copy it with the copy button and refresh the window if it has been open for a while. See [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/).

## Common mistakes
- **Choosing the wrong network.** Select BNB Smart Chain (BEP20), not BEP2 or another chain.
- **Sending a different token.** Choose BNB itself, not a token on BNB Smart Chain, unless the window asks for it.
- **Forgetting the exchange fee.** If it is deducted from the amount, the order arrives short.
- **Skipping the screenshot.** Because BNB is confirmed by our team, the screenshot and hash speed things up considerably.
- **Resending.** If a payment is pending, check the status page and contact us before sending again.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why is BNB confirmed manually when other coins are automatic?
Each network needs its own detection support. BNB Smart Chain payments are currently reviewed by a person after you upload a screenshot. That keeps matching accurate while we use automatic detection on the networks where it is available.

### Can I pay from Binance directly?
Yes. Withdraw BNB to the address in our window, choosing BNB Smart Chain (BEP20) as the network. Check the minimum and fee, and copy the address exactly. Some exchanges hold new addresses for a short security period.

### Do BNB payments get the discount?
Yes. All supported cryptocurrencies save 10% on your order total. The discount is calculated on the product subtotal, and shipping is added afterward. Free shipping applies to orders of $200 or more after discount. See [the 10% crypto and gift card discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/).

### Is BNB fast enough for a same-day order?
Transfers are fast, but because confirmation is manual, same-day matching depends on when you pay and on our business hours. If timing matters, choose Solana, Bitcoin or another network with automatic detection.

## After your payment is confirmed
You receive an email and your order status updates. We process orders within 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse and ship with tracking by a regional carrier. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) and [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/).

## Alternatives
Prefer automatic detection? Consider [Bitcoin](/blog/how-to-pay-with-bitcoin/), [Solana](/blog/pay-with-solana-sol/) or [USDT](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/). All crypto payments use the [10% crypto discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/). Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What happens after you pay with BNB
Because BNB payments are confirmed by our team, the screenshot and transaction hash you upload are what we check against the blockchain, so make sure they are clear and complete. Once your payment is confirmed, you receive an email and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and the regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). If you need to change something, read [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/) before your order ships.

## Staying protected when you pay with BNB
Only trust payment instructions that come through our official email, our WhatsApp number or your private order page. Check that the network in your exchange or wallet says BNB Smart Chain (BEP20) and that the address begins with 0x, and do not use a withdrawal address from any message that did not come from us. We never ask for your passwords, PINs, card numbers, private keys or recovery phrases, and no genuine order needs them. Be wary of anyone who contacts you out of the blue claiming to represent the store, offers a different address or account to pay or pushes you to pay quickly outside the order. If a message does not match your order number and amount exactly, stop and contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) before you send anything. For more on keeping your account details secure, see [gift card code security tips](/blog/gift-card-code-security-tips/) and [why we need your email and phone](/blog/why-we-need-your-email-and-phone/).

## A worked example
Suppose your cart is $240. Paying with BNB applies the 10% discount, so the product total is $216.00 and shipping is free because the amount after discount is above $200. In the payment window, that dollar total is converted to BNB at the live rate. Say the quote is 0.36 BNB. Your exchange charges a withdrawal fee of 0.0005 BNB and deducts it from what you enter, so you enter 0.3605 BNB to make sure 0.36 BNB arrives. You select BNB Smart Chain (BEP20), paste the address, confirm, and then press "I have paid" and upload a screenshot with the transaction hash. Because the amount that arrived matches the quote, the check is quick.

## A final checklist before you send
- Select BNB Smart Chain (BEP20) as the network.
- Add any exchange withdrawal fee on top of the amount.
- Copy the address and amount with the copy buttons.
- Upload a clear screenshot and the transaction hash after you press the button.

Because BNB is confirmed by our team, a complete screenshot and hash are the quickest way to get your order moving. If it is outside business hours, expect the check the next business morning.

faq.q: Which BNB network do you accept?
faq.a: BNB Smart Chain, also written BSC or BEP20. Do not use the older BEP2 network or another chain.

faq.q: How are BNB payments confirmed?
faq.a: BNB payments are confirmed by our team after you upload a screenshot on the status page, so allow a little extra time in business hours.

faq.q: Do I get the crypto discount with BNB?
faq.a: Yes. All supported cryptocurrencies save 10% on your order total.

faq.q: How do I avoid sending too little?
faq.a: Add any exchange withdrawal fee on top of the amount so the full BNB amount arrives, and copy the amount from the window.

faq.q: What should I upload for confirmation?
faq.a: A clear screenshot of the transaction, plus the transaction hash if available, on your order status page.

faq.q: Can I use another coin if I want automatic confirmation?
faq.a: Yes. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, USDT and USDC are matched automatically on their networks where supported.

title: Paying With Solana (SOL): Quick Transfers, Tiny Fees
summary: SOL transfers confirm in seconds. Learn how to pay your order with Solana and what to double-check before you press send.
body:
Solana (SOL) is one of the quickest and cheapest ways to pay at One Stop Vape Store. Transfers usually confirm within seconds and cost a fraction of a cent, and paying with SOL qualifies for our 10% crypto discount. If you already use a Solana wallet on your phone or browser, it is a pleasant experience. This guide explains each step, how the live quote works, what the status page shows, how to avoid common mistakes with Solana's token system, why some people prefer a stablecoin instead and what to do if something goes wrong. It is for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## Choose SOL at checkout
Add products to your cart, choose options such as strength and pack size on the product page and go to checkout. Enter your contact and shipping details and confirm you are 21 or older. Select Cryptocurrency, then Solana (SOL). The order summary shows the 10% discount and your total. The payment window then shows the wallet address, a QR code and the SOL amount based on the live rate, which refreshes about every 30 seconds.

## Sending the payment
1. Open your Solana wallet, such as a mobile or browser wallet that supports SOL.
2. Scan the QR code or paste the address. Use the copy button to avoid typing errors, and compare the first and last characters.
3. Enter the SOL amount shown. Because SOL's price changes, send promptly after you open the window, and refresh it if it has been open for a while.
4. Confirm the transfer. The network fee is tiny, but keep a small balance for it so the transfer does not fail.
5. Press "I have paid" in the payment window. Your order is placed and you land on the status page.

## Native SOL, not tokens
Send SOL itself, the native coin. Solana also has many tokens, including stablecoins such as USDC, and a token transfer is a different kind of transaction from a SOL transfer. If you would rather use a stablecoin so the amount does not move with the market, choose [USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/) at checkout instead of SOL. Mixing them up is the most common Solana mistake: our window is built to match the token you choose, so a token sent to a SOL payment, or SOL sent to a token payment, will not match.

## Detection and confirmation
We look for an incoming SOL transfer matching your order value within the last few hours, checking the address, the dollar value of the amount, the time and that the transaction has not already paid another order. Solana finalizes quickly, so detection is usually within seconds to a couple of minutes. Once it confirms, we email you and the order moves forward. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/) for the full list of checks.

After confirmation, the order enters processing. We process orders within 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse and ship with tracking by a regional carrier. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery. See [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/).

## Why people choose Solana
- **Speed:** transfers usually confirm in seconds.
- **Cost:** the network fee is a fraction of a cent, so it barely affects the saving from the discount.
- **Simple wallets:** mobile Solana wallets are easy to use and scan QR codes smoothly.
- **Good for small orders:** because the fee is tiny, even a modest order keeps nearly all of the 10% saving.

The trade-off is price movement. SOL's price can change between the quote and the payment, so the amount of SOL you send is only correct for a short time. A small tolerance covers normal movement. If you are worried about it, stablecoins give an exact amount.

## Sending from an exchange
Many exchanges let you withdraw SOL. Check that the withdrawal is on the Solana network, check the minimum and the fee, and add the fee if it is deducted from what you send. Some exchanges hold new addresses for a security period. Our guide to [sending crypto from an exchange to a wallet](/blog/send-crypto-from-an-exchange-to-a-wallet/) goes through these details.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do I need extra SOL for fees if I am paying in SOL?
Yes, a very small amount. Solana fees are tiny, but a transfer of your entire balance may fail if there is nothing left to cover the fee. Leave a small buffer.

### Why does the SOL amount change when I refresh?
Because it is converted from your dollar total at the live rate. The dollar value of your order does not change, only the SOL equivalent.

### Can I pay with a Solana token instead?
Yes, USDC on Solana is available as its own option. Choose it at checkout, and send USDC rather than SOL.

### Is Solana fast enough for same-day orders?
Detection is usually within minutes, but processing still takes 24 to 72 business hours after confirmation. Paying quickly helps your order enter processing sooner.

## Common mistakes
- **Sending the wrong asset.** Check that you are sending SOL if you chose SOL, or USDC if you chose USDC.
- **Typing the address.** Always copy or scan.
- **Sending an outdated amount.** Refresh the window if it has been open a while.
- **Leaving no balance for fees.** Keep a small buffer.
- **Resending a pending payment.** Check the status page and contact us first.

## If you made a mistake
Check [what to do if you sent crypto on the wrong network](/blog/sent-crypto-on-the-wrong-network/) and contact us from the [contact page](/contact/) with your order reference and transaction hash. See the full list of options in [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/) and the [10% crypto discount guide](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/). Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What happens after you pay with Solana
Solana transfers are usually detected within seconds to a couple of minutes, and the status page updates on its own. Once your payment is confirmed, you receive an email and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and the regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). If you need to change something, read [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/) before your order ships.

## Staying protected when you pay with Solana
Only trust payment instructions that come through our official email, our WhatsApp number or your private order page. Check that you are sending the asset you chose, SOL or USDC, and that your wallet is on the Solana network before you confirm. We never ask for your passwords, PINs, card numbers, private keys or recovery phrases, and no genuine order needs them. Be wary of anyone who contacts you out of the blue claiming to represent the store, offers a different address or account to pay or pushes you to pay quickly outside the order. If a message does not match your order number and amount exactly, stop and contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) before you send anything. For more on keeping your account details secure, see [gift card code security tips](/blog/gift-card-code-security-tips/) and [why we need your email and phone](/blog/why-we-need-your-email-and-phone/).

## A worked example
Suppose your cart is $180. Paying with SOL applies the 10% discount, so the product total is $162.00. Because that is under $200, the flat $15 shipping fee applies, and the amount due is $177.00. In the payment window, $177.00 is converted to SOL at the live rate. Say the quote is 1.15 SOL. You open your wallet, scan the QR code, enter 1.15 SOL and confirm. The fee is a fraction of a cent. You press "I have paid", and the status page moves from payment sent to detected to confirmed within a couple of minutes. If SOL's price rose slightly between the quote and your payment, the small tolerance covers it, and you do not need to do anything.

## When a stablecoin may suit you better
If you are paying a larger order and would rather not worry about the price of SOL moving, USDC on Solana gives the same speed and tiny fees with a stable amount. Choose it at checkout instead of SOL. See [paying with USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/). For a side-by-side view of every option, read [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/).

## A final checklist before you send
- Confirm you are sending SOL, or USDC if you chose that option.
- Keep a small SOL balance for the network fee.
- Scan the QR code or copy the address; never type it.
- Refresh the window if it has been open for a while.

Solana is quick, so there is little waiting. If the status page still shows waiting after several minutes, add your transaction hash on the status page and contact us.

title: No Crypto? How to Buy It With a Card (MoonPay and Alternatives)
summary: Never bought crypto before? Follow this beginner guide to buy Bitcoin, USDT or other coins with a card and send them to pay your order.
body:
You do not need to own cryptocurrency to use our crypto checkout. You can buy it first with a card or bank transfer from a service such as MoonPay, Coinbase, Transak or Changelly, and then send it to the address shown at checkout. For many orders the 10% crypto discount is larger than the extra cost of buying, which makes it worth considering. This guide walks through each step, explains what the fees are, shows how to choose a coin and network, covers identity verification and timing, lists the mistakes that cost people money and explains when buying crypto is not worth it. It is for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## Why bother
Crypto and gift card payments get a 10% discount at checkout. On a $200 order, that is $20. If the provider's fee and the network fee together cost less than $20, you come out ahead. On a larger order the saving grows, because the discount scales with the order while some fees do not. On a very small order the fees may cancel the saving, so run the numbers first. Our guide to [the 10% crypto and gift card discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/) shows worked examples, including how the discount interacts with free shipping.

## Choosing a coin and network
The best coin for a purchase is usually the one with the lowest total cost and the least price movement.

- **Stablecoins (USDT, USDC):** priced at one dollar, so there is no price movement between buying and paying. USDC on Solana and USDT on Tron are typically cheap to send. See [USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/) and [USDT ERC20 vs TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/).
- **Bitcoin:** the most widely available coin, but confirmations can be slower and fees higher when busy. See [how to pay with Bitcoin](/blog/how-to-pay-with-bitcoin/).
- **Solana:** fast and cheap, but its price moves. See [paying with Solana](/blog/pay-with-solana-sol/).
- **Ethereum and BNB:** workable, but check fees. See [paying with Ethereum](/blog/pay-with-ethereum-eth/) and [paying with BNB](/blog/pay-with-bnb-smart-chain/).

For most first-time buyers, a stablecoin on a low-fee network is the simplest choice, because the amount is predictable.

## Step 1: open the payment window
At checkout, choose Cryptocurrency and the coin you want to pay with. The window includes a "Don't have this coin?" section with a MoonPay button and alternatives. Keep the window open, or note the coin, the network, the address and the amount, because you will need them in a moment. If you prefer, you can place the order later; the window will give you a fresh quote.

## Step 2: buy the coin
On the provider's site, pick the same coin and, where asked, the same network as in our window. Enter the amount you want to buy. Allow a little extra for the provider's fee and for the network fee. If you need to pay $180 after discount, buy a little more than $180, because fees and small price moves can leave you slightly short. Complete the card or bank payment and any identity checks the provider requires.

## Step 3: send it to us
When the provider asks where to send the coins, paste the address from our payment window. This step is the most important. Double-check that the first and last characters match, and choose the exact network. Some providers let you buy and send in one step, and others deliver the coins to a wallet you must then send from. Follow the provider's prompts carefully and do not rush.

## Step 4: press "I have paid"
Return to our window and press the button. We look for your transfer and confirm the order automatically on networks that support automatic detection. For other networks, such as BNB, a team member confirms after you upload a screenshot on the status page. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/) and [how to upload a payment screenshot](/blog/how-to-upload-a-payment-screenshot/).

## Costs and timing
Provider fees vary. Card purchases usually cost more than bank transfers, but they are faster. First-time purchases may need identity verification, which can take minutes to days depending on the provider and your documents. Start before you need the order, and do not wait until the last moment. Typical costs to consider:

- **Provider fee:** often a percentage of the purchase, higher for card payments.
- **Spread:** the provider may buy at a slightly worse rate than the market.
- **Network fee:** paid when you send the coins to us. See [crypto network fees explained](/blog/crypto-network-fees-explained/).
- **Withdrawal fee:** some exchanges charge a flat fee for sending coins out.

Add them up and compare with the 10% discount before you decide. If the total is more than the discount, a standard-price method such as Cash App, Apple Pay or Chime may be cheaper overall.

## Identity checks and privacy
Regulated providers must verify identity before selling crypto, which usually means a photo ID and sometimes a selfie. That is between you and the provider. We never ask for your ID, your wallet recovery phrase or your private keys, and you should never share those with anyone. We use only public blockchain data to match your payment.

## Common mistakes
- **Buying on the wrong network.** Make sure the network you choose matches the network in our window.
- **Buying the wrong coin.** Confirm the coin before you pay the provider.
- **Forgetting fees.** If you buy exactly your order total, fees can leave you short.
- **Typing the address.** Always paste it.
- **Waiting too long.** Identity checks and card limits can take time, so start early.
- **Resending when pending.** Check the status page first.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is it worth buying crypto for one order?
It can be, if the discount exceeds your total costs. For a larger order it usually is. For a small order, compare it with other options. Remember free shipping applies to orders of $200 or more after discount.

### What if the provider only sells coins I cannot use?
Then buy a coin we accept, such as USDT, USDC, Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB or Solana, or choose another payment method.

### Can I use a gift card instead?
Yes. Gift cards also earn the 10% discount and avoid crypto altogether. See [how gift card payment works](/blog/how-gift-card-payment-works/).

### How long does the whole process take?
If you already have a verified account, a card purchase can be done in minutes. A first-time verification can take longer. Our confirmation after you send is usually quick on automatic networks, and then orders are processed within 24 to 72 business hours.

## After you pay
Once your payment is confirmed you receive an email. We ship from our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse with tracking by a regional carrier, and an adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery. Compare all options in [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/). Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What happens after you pay with crypto you bought with a card
After you send the coins to our address and press the button, we look for your transfer and match it to your order, automatically on most networks and with a manual check on others. Once your payment is confirmed, you receive an email and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and the regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). If you need to change something, read [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/) before your order ships.

## Staying protected when you pay with crypto
Only trust payment instructions that come through our official email, our WhatsApp number or your private order page. Only buy from a regulated provider you trust, type the provider's address into your browser yourself and be wary of links in unexpected messages offering to sell you crypto for an order. We never ask for your passwords, PINs, card numbers, private keys or recovery phrases, and no genuine order needs them. Be wary of anyone who contacts you out of the blue claiming to represent the store, offers a different address or account to pay or pushes you to pay quickly outside the order. If a message does not match your order number and amount exactly, stop and contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) before you send anything. For more on keeping your account details secure, see [gift card code security tips](/blog/gift-card-code-security-tips/) and [why we need your email and phone](/blog/why-we-need-your-email-and-phone/).

## A final checklist before you send
- Decide the coin and network first, using our payment window.
- Buy a little more than the order total to cover fees.
- Start identity verification early if you are new to the provider.
- Paste the address and check the first and last characters before you send.

Buying crypto adds steps, but for a larger order the saving can be worth it. If you would rather avoid it, a gift card also earns the 10% discount, and app payments are available at the standard price.

faq.a: A stablecoin such as USDC on Solana or USDT on Tron, because the amount is predictable and fees are low.
