title: What Is a Crypto Network, and Why Does It Matter When You Pay?
summary: The same coin can live on several blockchains. Learn what a network is and why choosing the right one decides whether your payment arrives.
body:
When you pay with cryptocurrency at One Stop Vape Store you choose two things: a coin and a network. The coin is what you are sending, such as Bitcoin, USDT, USDC, Ethereum, BNB or Solana. The network is the blockchain that carries the transfer. Getting the network right is the single most important step in a crypto payment, because an address that works on one network is not valid on another, and a transfer sent on the wrong one may never arrive. This guide explains what a network is in plain language, how it differs from the coin, why the same token can exist on several networks, how to recognize each network by its address format, how fees differ and how to match networks between our payment window and your wallet or exchange. It is written for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## Coin versus network
A coin or token is the unit of value. A network is the system that records who owns what. Bitcoin only lives on the Bitcoin network, so there is nothing to choose: Bitcoin is both the coin and the network. Ethereum's coin, ETH, lives on the Ethereum network. But a stablecoin like USDT is a token that is issued separately on several blockchains, including Ethereum and Tron. The tokens are the same in name and value, but each one lives on a different ledger with its own address format, its own fees and its own rules. USDC, similarly, exists on several networks, and at our store it is offered on Solana.

A useful comparison is money in different banks. A dollar in one bank cannot simply be moved to an account at another bank by quoting the account number, because each bank has its own system. In the same way, USDT on Ethereum and USDT on Tron are separate balances on separate systems, even though both are called USDT.

## Why a wrong network is a problem
An address on one network is not valid on another, even if it looks similar. Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain, for example, use the same style of address, beginning with 0x, which means a wallet may let you paste an Ethereum address into a BNB Smart Chain transfer without complaint. The transfer will go through on the chain you chose, but our wallet for that chain is a different thing, and the funds will not reach the one we are watching. In some cases the funds can be recovered if the receiver controls the same address on the other chain, and in others they cannot be recovered at all. Read [what to do after sending crypto on the wrong network](/blog/sent-crypto-on-the-wrong-network/) if it has happened to you.

The key rule is simple: send the coin you chose on the network we show. Everything else is detail.

## How to spot the network
The payment window states the network next to the address, for example "Tron (TRC20)", "Solana (SOL)", "Bitcoin" or "Ethereum". Exchanges and wallets show similar labels when you withdraw or send, sometimes with different names:

- **Ethereum** may be called ERC20, ETH or Ethereum mainnet.
- **Tron** may be called TRC20 or TRX.
- **BNB Smart Chain** may be called BSC, BEP20 or BNB Smart Chain. It is not the same as BEP2, the older Binance Chain.
- **Solana** may be called SOL or SPL for its tokens.
- **Bitcoin** may be called BTC or Bitcoin mainnet.

Match the label in our window with the label in your wallet exactly, and if you cannot find a match, do not guess. Choose a different coin or ask us.

## Address formats
Addresses look different on different networks, which gives you a quick sanity check:

- Bitcoin addresses start with bc1, 1 or 3.
- Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain addresses start with 0x and are 42 characters long.
- Tron addresses start with T and are 34 characters long.
- Solana addresses are long base58 strings, usually 32 to 44 characters, with no 0x or T prefix.

If you paste an address and the first characters do not match what you expect for the network you chose, stop and check. Remember that Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain addresses look alike, so the prefix will not tell them apart: only the network label will.

## Fees vary by network
Some networks cost cents, others dollars. Bitcoin fees depend on how busy the network is. Ethereum fees, called gas, rise with demand. Tron and Solana are usually cheap. BNB Smart Chain is usually cheap. The fee is paid by you to the network, not to us. See [crypto network fees explained](/blog/crypto-network-fees-explained/) for details, and compare the fee for each option before you choose, especially on smaller orders where a large fee can erase the saving from the 10% crypto discount.

## Speed varies by network
Solana and Tron usually confirm within seconds to a couple of minutes. Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain usually take a few minutes. Bitcoin is usually visible within a minute or two but is final only after it is included in a block, which often takes around ten minutes. Our system matches payments automatically on most networks, as explained in [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/), and BNB payments are confirmed by our team after you upload a screenshot.

## Which networks we accept
- **Bitcoin** on the Bitcoin network.
- **USDT** on Ethereum (ERC20) and Tron (TRC20).
- **USDC** on Solana.
- **Ethereum** on the Ethereum network.
- **BNB** on BNB Smart Chain (BEP20).
- **Solana** on the Solana network.

Each has its own guide: [Bitcoin](/blog/how-to-pay-with-bitcoin/), [USDT](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/), [USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/), [Ethereum](/blog/pay-with-ethereum-eth/), [BNB](/blog/pay-with-bnb-smart-chain/) and [Solana](/blog/pay-with-solana-sol/).

## How to match the network step by step
1. At checkout choose Cryptocurrency, then the coin, then the network if you are asked.
2. Note the network label in the payment window, next to the address.
3. In your wallet or exchange, choose the same coin and look for a network selector on the send or withdraw screen.
4. Choose the network that matches the label exactly.
5. Paste the address with the copy button and compare the first and last characters.
6. Confirm and press "I have paid" in our window.

## Common mistakes
- **Letting the exchange default.** Exchanges often preselect a network, and it is not always the one you need.
- **Assuming similar addresses are the same.** Ethereum and BNB addresses look alike but live on different chains.
- **Mixing up coin and network.** USDT on Ethereum is not USDT on Tron.
- **Using an old address.** Always copy the address from the current payment window.
- **Ignoring the label because the address "looks right".** The label is what counts.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I move funds between networks?
Yes, through a bridge or an exchange, but it adds fees and risk. It is usually better to pay on the network where your funds already are, if we accept it.

### Why do you offer two networks for USDT but only one for USDC?
Each option exists because customers commonly hold the token on that network and because we can match the payments reliably. We keep the list short to reduce mistakes.

### What happens if my wallet does not list the network I need?
Choose a different coin or network that your wallet supports, or use an exchange that supports the one we need. Our [payment methods comparison](/blog/payment-methods-compared/) can help you choose.

### Is one network more secure than another?
They all use cryptography, and the practical risk for a payment is human error, not the network. Matching the network and copying the address are the most important protections.

## After your payment is confirmed
Once your payment is confirmed you receive an email, and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and a regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). Read [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/) and [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) to prepare. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A worked example: two ways to pay with USDT
Imagine you hold 135 USDT and want to pay an order. At checkout you choose Cryptocurrency, then USDT, and then you see two network choices. If your balance sits on an exchange that offers both, you compare the withdrawal fees: Tron might charge 1 USDT and Ethereum 10 USDT. You choose Tron (TRC20), the payment window shows an address that starts with T and the label Tron (TRC20), and you withdraw 136 USDT so that 135 arrives after the fee. If instead your wallet already holds USDT on Ethereum, you choose Ethereum (ERC20), the window shows an address that starts with 0x and you pay the gas fee in ETH. Both routes lead to the same result, a confirmed order, but the cost and the steps differ. The only wrong move is to take an address from one route and use it with the network of the other.

## Why networks exist at all
Different blockchains were built for different goals. Bitcoin focuses on simple, secure value transfer. Ethereum adds programmable contracts, which is how tokens such as USDT and USDC exist there. Tron and Solana were designed for speed and low cost. BNB Smart Chain is run by a large exchange ecosystem and offers low fees. Because each chain is independent, companies that issue stablecoins deploy them on several chains to reach more users, and that is why you see the same token name on several networks. Understanding that each network is a separate system is the key to never mixing them up.

faq.q: What is the difference between a coin and a network?
faq.a: The coin is the unit you send, such as USDT. The network is the blockchain that carries it, such as Ethereum or Tron.

faq.q: Why does the network matter?
faq.a: An address on one network is not valid on another. Sending on the wrong network can mean the funds never arrive and may not be recoverable.

faq.q: How do I know which network to use?
faq.a: The payment window states it next to the address, for example Tron (TRC20) or Solana (SOL). Match it exactly in your wallet or exchange.

faq.q: Do Ethereum and BNB addresses look the same?
faq.a: Yes, both start with 0x, so only the network label tells them apart.

faq.q: Which networks do you accept?
faq.a: Bitcoin, Ethereum (ETH and USDT ERC20), Tron (USDT TRC20), BNB Smart Chain (BEP20) and Solana (SOL and USDC).

faq.q: Do fees differ by network?
faq.a: Yes. Tron and Solana are usually cheap, Ethereum varies with demand and Bitcoin depends on how busy the network is.

title: The 10% Crypto and Gift Card Discount: How It Works
summary: Pay with crypto or a gift card and save 10% on your product total. See how the discount interacts with shipping and the free-shipping threshold.
body:
We offer a 10% discount when you pay by cryptocurrency or with a supported gift card. It is applied automatically at checkout the moment you pick one of those methods, and it shows as its own line in the order summary so you can see exactly what you are saving. This guide explains what the discount applies to, how it interacts with the free-shipping threshold, worked examples with real numbers, which payment methods qualify, whether the extra steps are worth it and how to compare all the options. It is written for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## What the discount applies to
The discount is calculated on your product subtotal, which is the total of the items in your cart at their listed prices, including whichever strength or pack size you chose. It is not applied to shipping. Shipping is added after the discount, either as a flat $15 or as free when your order qualifies. Each line is shown in the order summary on the checkout page: subtotal, discount, shipping and total. If you change your payment method at checkout, the summary updates immediately, so you can compare totals before you decide.

Because prices are set on our server from the catalog, the discount cannot be changed or forced from your browser. What you see at checkout is the same figure the server calculates when the order is placed.

## Free shipping and the discount
This is the part that surprises people. Our free-shipping offer applies to orders of $200 or more after discount and before tax. That means the discount can bring a cart down below the threshold. A $215 cart paid by crypto becomes $193.50 after the 10% discount, which is under $200, so the flat $15 shipping fee is added. The same $215 cart paid by Cash App has no discount, so it stays above $200 and ships free.

That is not a trick; it is how the offer is defined, and it is described in the [shipping policy](/shipping/) and in [minimum order and free shipping explained](/blog/minimum-order-and-free-shipping-explained/). The practical advice is simple: check the order summary before you pay, and if you are close to the threshold, consider whether adding one more item changes the result in your favor.

## Worked examples
- **$150 cart, crypto:** discount $15.00, product total $135.00, plus $15 shipping, so $150.00 due. Under $200 after discount, so shipping applies.
- **$150 cart, Cash App:** no discount, product total $150.00, plus $15 shipping, so $165.00 due.
- **$230 cart, crypto:** discount $23.00, product total $207.00, shipping free, so $207.00 due. This is the best case: the discount lands above the free-shipping line.
- **$230 cart, Cash App:** no discount, product total $230.00, shipping free, so $230.00 due.
- **$215 cart, crypto:** discount $21.50, product total $193.50, plus $15 shipping, so $208.50 due. Compare with Cash App at $215.00 and free shipping, where Cash App is only $6.50 more.
- **$100 minimum cart, crypto:** the minimum order of $100 applies to the subtotal. After the discount the product total is $90.00, plus $15 shipping, so $105.00.

The comparison between the last two is the interesting one: the discount is always worth more than the shipping fee unless you sit just above the threshold on the other method.

## Which methods qualify
- **Cryptocurrency:** Bitcoin, USDT on ERC20 or TRC20, USDC, Ethereum, BNB and Solana.
- **Gift cards:** Apple, Razer Gold, Paysafe, Sephora and Macy's.

Cash App, Apple Pay and Chime do not carry the discount, because they pay at the standard price. All methods are available to adults aged 21 and over. You can compare them in [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/).

## Is it worth the extra steps?
That depends on where you are starting.

### If you already hold crypto
Definitely. You save 10% for the cost of a network fee, which is usually small compared with the saving on a typical order. Choose a network with low fees, such as USDT on TRC20 or Solana, to keep the saving as large as possible. See [USDT ERC20 vs TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/) and [paying with Solana](/blog/pay-with-solana-sol/).

### If you would need to buy crypto first
Factor in the provider's fees. Buying with a card often costs a few percent, which can eat much of the discount on a small order, while a bank transfer on an exchange may cost less but take longer. Read [how to buy crypto with a card](/blog/how-to-buy-crypto-with-a-card/) to compare, and compare the total cost with the standard-price options.

### If you have a gift card
Gift cards qualify too, and the process is straightforward. We send a buy link and an upload link after you order. See [how gift card payment works](/blog/how-gift-card-payment-works/) and the guides for [Apple](/blog/pay-with-apple-gift-card/), [Razer Gold](/blog/pay-with-razer-gold/), [Paysafecard](/blog/pay-with-paysafecard/), [Sephora](/blog/pay-with-sephora-gift-card/) and [Macy's](/blog/pay-with-macys-gift-card/).

## How the discount shows on your order
After you pay, your order page and confirmation email show the same breakdown as checkout: the subtotal, the discount, the shipping and the total. If a refund is ever due, it is calculated from what you actually paid and goes back through the payment method the payment was received through, less the 15% restocking fee where it applies. See [refund and return policy explained](/blog/refund-and-return-policy-explained/).

## Stacking and limits
The 10% discount does not stack with itself, and it applies to the order as a whole. There is a single payment method per order. If you want to use a gift card for part and another method for the rest, contact us before you order so we can advise; otherwise, choose one method. The minimum order is $100 before the discount.

## Common questions about timing
Crypto payments are matched automatically on the blockchain, usually within minutes, as explained in [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/). Gift card payments need a manual check once you upload the card details, so they take a little longer. After payment is confirmed, orders are processed within 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse and ship with tracking. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery.

## Mistakes to avoid
- **Assuming the discount keeps free shipping.** Check the summary, because the threshold is applied after the discount.
- **Choosing a high-fee network for a small order.** A large fee can cancel the saving.
- **Paying the wrong amount.** Send the exact amount shown. See [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/).
- **Expecting the discount on app payments.** It applies to crypto and gift cards only.

## Bottom line
For most customers who can pay in crypto or with a gift card, the 10% discount is the biggest saving on the site, and it is worth taking whenever it makes the total lower than the alternatives. Check the order summary, compare the totals and choose the method that costs you least while suiting your habits. Browse the [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) ranges, and remember all products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does the discount apply to every product?
Yes, it applies to the whole product subtotal, whatever you buy and whichever option you choose. There are no excluded categories.

### Is there a limit on the size of the discount?
The discount is a flat 10% of the product subtotal. It is not capped, so it grows with the size of your order, which makes it especially valuable on larger orders.

### Do wholesale orders get the discount?
Wholesale pricing is arranged separately. If you are ordering in volume as a retailer, contact us through the [wholesale page](/wholesale/) and we will explain how pricing and payment options work for your order.

### Can I apply the discount after I have placed the order?
No. The discount is part of the payment method you choose at checkout. If you want it, choose crypto or a gift card before you place the order, or contact us before paying if you wish to switch.

### What about taxes?
The free-shipping threshold is measured before tax. Any taxes that apply are shown in your order summary where relevant, so you always see the full amount before you pay.

### How do I check my savings?
Open the order summary at checkout. It shows the subtotal, the discount line, shipping and the total for the method you have selected, and it updates as you switch methods so you can compare.

### Can I see how much I saved after the order?
Yes. Your order page and confirmation email repeat the breakdown, including the discount line, so you can keep a record of the saving for your own bookkeeping.

### Does the discount change if I later return an item?
A refund is calculated from what you actually paid for the returned items, which already reflects the discount, less the 15% restocking fee where it applies, and it goes back through the same payment method. See [refund and return policy explained](/blog/refund-and-return-policy-explained/).

### Is the discount ever unavailable?
The discount is part of the standard checkout for crypto and gift cards. If it is ever changed, the order summary will always show the exact figure before you pay, so you are never surprised.

faq.q: How much is the crypto discount?
faq.a: 10% on your product subtotal when you pay with cryptocurrency or a supported gift card. It is applied automatically at checkout.

faq.q: Does the discount apply to shipping?
faq.a: No. The discount is calculated on the product subtotal, and shipping is added after it.

faq.q: Can the discount remove my free shipping?
faq.a: Yes. Free shipping applies to orders of $200 or more after discount, so a $215 cart paid by crypto becomes $193.50 and pays $15 shipping.

faq.q: Which payment methods qualify?
faq.a: Cryptocurrency (BTC, USDT, USDC, ETH, BNB, SOL) and gift cards (Apple, Razer Gold, Paysafe, Sephora, Macy's). Cash App, Apple Pay and Chime do not.

faq.q: Is paying with crypto worth it if I have to buy it first?
faq.a: It can be, but compare the buying fees with the saving. On a small order, card fees can cancel much of the discount.

faq.q: Where do refunds go for discounted orders?
faq.a: Back through the payment method used, calculated from what you paid, less the 15% restocking fee where it applies.

title: How We Detect Your Crypto Payment Automatically
summary: After you press I have paid, we look for your transfer on the blockchain. Here is how matching works, what we check and when a human steps in.
body:
You should not have to wait for someone to read a screenshot before your crypto payment counts. For most networks, we match payments to orders automatically by reading public blockchain data. This guide explains exactly what happens when you press "I have paid", what the system checks, the states you may see on your order page, how long each stage usually takes, when a person steps in, what to do if something looks wrong and what we do and do not see about your funds. It is written for adults aged 21 and over.

## What happens when you press "I have paid"
In the payment window you see your order reference, the amount in your chosen token, a QR code and the wallet address for the network you picked. When you have sent the payment from your wallet, you press "I have paid". At that point your order is created in our system with the status payment sent, and you are taken to a private status page. From there, our system reads public blockchain data for the shop wallet on the network you chose and looks for an incoming transfer that fits your order. You do not need to do anything else while it looks.

The status page refreshes on its own, and you can leave it and come back later using the private link in your order email. Nothing about the automatic check requires you to stay on the page.

## What we check
A transfer has to pass several tests before we link it to an order:

- **Network and address:** the transfer must arrive at the correct wallet on the correct network. A transfer to a different address, or on a different network, will not match.
- **Token:** it must be the token you chose, such as BTC, USDT, USDC, ETH, BNB or SOL.
- **Amount:** the US dollar value of the transfer must be close to your order total, with a small tolerance for market movement between the quote and the payment. We convert the received amount at the market rate to compare it with your total.
- **Time:** the transfer must be recent, shortly before or after you placed the order. This stops an old unrelated transfer from being matched.
- **Uniqueness:** a single transaction can pay only one order. Once a transfer is matched, it is claimed, so it cannot be applied to a second order.

If a transfer passes all of these, it is matched to your order. If more than one order could fit, the best match by amount and time is used.

## The states you may see
- **Awaiting payment or payment sent:** your order exists and we are looking for a matching transfer.
- **Detected:** a matching transfer is visible on the network but has not yet reached the number of confirmations we require.
- **Confirmed:** the transfer is matched and confirmed. You receive an email and your order moves into processing.
- **Underpaid:** we found a payment that is short of the order total. See [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/).
- **Submitted for review:** you added a screenshot or transaction hash, and a team member will check it.

You can see the current state on your private status page at any time, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/).

## How long each stage usually takes
Speed depends on the network. Solana and Tron payments are usually detected within seconds to a couple of minutes. Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain usually take a few minutes. Bitcoin is usually visible within a minute or two but is not final until it has been included in a block, which often takes around ten minutes and sometimes longer when the network is busy. Detection is only the first stage: after a payment is confirmed, the order enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours before it ships. See [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/).

## When a person steps in
Automatic detection covers the main networks, but a person reviews an order when:

- the network does not support automatic detection for that token,
- the amount does not match closely enough,
- there is more than one possible match,
- you submitted a transaction hash or screenshot that needs checking, or
- something looks unusual.

In those cases a team member checks your screenshot and the transaction hash against the blockchain. You can add both on the status page; see [how to upload a payment screenshot](/blog/how-to-upload-a-payment-screenshot/). A transaction hash, sometimes called a transaction ID, is the long string of characters your wallet shows after you send. Pasting it in lets us find the exact transfer immediately.

## What we see and what we do not
We use only public blockchain data. Because blockchains are public, anyone can see that an address received a transfer, how much and when. We do not see your wallet balance, your other transactions or your identity from the chain. We never ask for private keys, seed phrases or recovery words, and you should never share them with anyone. A genuine payment never requires them. If anyone asks you for them in connection with an order, do not respond and contact us.

## Why the tolerance exists
Crypto prices move. Between the moment you see the quote and the moment your transaction is confirmed, the dollar value of the amount you sent can differ slightly from your order total. A small tolerance allows for that, so a payment that is off by a tiny amount because of market movement is accepted. Larger gaps are not covered, and they show as underpaid. To avoid trouble, send the amount shown in the window, copy it with the copy button and keep network fees separate from the amount. If your exchange deducts its withdrawal fee from what you send, add the fee to the amount.

## Common reasons a payment does not match
- **Wrong network or token:** funds sent on a different network, or a different token, do not arrive at the address. See [sent crypto on the wrong network](/blog/sent-crypto-on-the-wrong-network/).
- **Short amount:** fees deducted from the amount, or a significant price move, can leave it under the total.
- **Late transfer:** a payment sent long after the order may fall outside the time window and need a manual check.
- **Already claimed:** a transaction can pay only one order, so reusing the same transfer for two orders will not work.
- **Pending withdrawal:** exchanges sometimes hold withdrawals for security checks, so the transfer appears later than expected.

## What you should do if it is taking a while
First, check the status page and your wallet's transaction record for confirmations. Second, if the status still shows waiting after the time that is normal for the network, add your transaction hash and a screenshot on the status page. Third, if you are still stuck, contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your order reference. Do not resend the payment, because duplicates are hard to unwind.

## Why automation matters
Automatic matching means most crypto orders move forward without anyone needing to read a screenshot, which is faster for you and more accurate for us. It also means each transaction is tied to one order only, which protects against mix-ups. People still handle the exceptions, which keeps the system fair when real-world payments do not match the quote perfectly.

## After your payment is confirmed
You receive an email, your order status updates and the order enters processing. We process orders within 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse and ship with tracking by a regional carrier. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery, as explained in [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/). Ready to pay? Start with [how to pay with Bitcoin](/blog/how-to-pay-with-bitcoin/) or compare [payment methods](/blog/payment-methods-compared/). Cryptocurrency payments save 10%, as explained in [the crypto discount guide](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do I have to keep the status page open?
No. The check runs on our side. You can close the page and return later using the private link in your order email, and the status will have updated.

### What if I paid before pressing the button?
That is fine. The system looks for transfers in a window around the time you placed the order, so a payment sent a little before or after you press the button can still be matched.

### Why do I see detected but not confirmed?
A detected transfer is visible on the network but has not yet reached the confirmations we require. It usually moves to confirmed on its own within minutes on most networks, and longer on Bitcoin when the network is busy.

### Can I help speed things up?
Yes. Add your transaction hash and a screenshot on the status page. It helps in manual checks and makes it easy to match the exact transfer.

### Is the match permanent?
Once a transfer is matched and confirmed to your order, it is claimed and cannot be applied to another order. That protects you and us against duplicates.

### What if the network is congested?
Congestion can delay confirmation. Your transfer is still valid, and the status will update when it confirms. Avoid resending, and contact us if it has been unusually long.

faq.q: Do I need to upload a screenshot for a crypto payment?
faq.a: Usually not. We match payments automatically from public blockchain data. A screenshot or transaction hash helps when the match needs a manual check.

faq.q: What does the system check?
faq.a: The network and address, the token, the dollar value of the amount, the timing and that the transaction has not already paid another order.

faq.q: How long does detection take?
faq.a: Solana and Tron are usually seconds to a couple of minutes, Ethereum and BNB a few minutes, and Bitcoin usually needs a block confirmation, often around ten minutes.

faq.q: What does 'underpaid' mean?
faq.a: We found a payment that is short of your order total. Do not resend; contact us with your reference and transaction hash.

faq.q: Can you see my wallet balance?
faq.a: No. We only use public blockchain data about transfers to our wallet. We never ask for private keys or recovery phrases.

faq.q: Can one transaction pay two orders?
faq.a: No. Each transaction can be claimed by only one order.

title: Sending Crypto From an Exchange: Withdrawal Steps and Pitfalls
summary: Paying from an exchange account? Here is how to withdraw to our address correctly, including network selection, fees and minimums.
body:
Many people hold crypto on an exchange rather than in a private wallet. You can pay from there, as long as the exchange allows withdrawals to external addresses. The process is simple, but it has more places to go wrong than sending from a personal wallet, because exchanges add their own fees, minimums, security checks and default settings. This guide walks through a withdrawal from an exchange to the address in our payment window, step by step, explains how to choose the right network, how to enter the right amount once fees are included, what security checks to expect, what delays can happen and how to find the transaction ID. It is written for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## Before you start
Check three things before you open the withdraw screen. First, that your account is verified to the level required for withdrawals, because some exchanges limit new accounts. Second, that the coin you want to send is available for external withdrawal, because some coins are only tradable. Third, that the exchange supports the network we accept for that coin: for example USDT on Tron (TRC20) or Ethereum (ERC20), USDC on Solana, Bitcoin on the Bitcoin network and BNB on BNB Smart Chain (BEP20). If your exchange does not support one of these, choose a different coin or buy crypto elsewhere; see [how to buy crypto with a card](/blog/how-to-buy-crypto-with-a-card/).

## Open the withdraw screen
In your exchange, find Withdraw or Send, then pick the coin. Do not use an internal transfer or "pay a friend" feature, because those only work between users of the same platform and the funds would not reach our address. Choose the option to send to an external address or wallet.

## Paste the address
Copy the address from our payment window with the copy button and paste it into the exchange. Compare the first and last four characters with the address on screen, because some malware swaps copied addresses for a different one. Some exchanges ask you to add the address to a whitelist first, and may hold new addresses for a short time for security. Plan for that if you are in a hurry.

## Choose the network
This is where most mistakes happen. Pick the network shown in our window, such as Tron (TRC20), Bitcoin, Solana or BNB Smart Chain (BEP20). Exchanges often default to a different network, so do not accept the preselected option without checking. If you are unsure what the names mean, read [what is a crypto network](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/). A wrong choice can mean the funds do not arrive and may not be recoverable.

## Enter the amount
Our window shows the amount to send. Exchanges deduct a withdrawal fee, either from the amount you enter or on top of it, and the withdrawal screen usually shows which. Make sure the amount that arrives equals the figure shown. If the exchange deducts the fee from your amount, add the fee to your withdrawal amount. For example, if the window shows 100 USDT and the exchange fee is 1 USDT deducted from what you enter, withdraw 101 USDT so that 100 arrives. A small shortfall is tolerated, but a larger one shows as underpaid. See [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/).

## Confirm and complete security checks
Exchanges often send an email or a two-factor code for withdrawals. Approve it, then wait for the transaction ID. Some exchanges add a delay for new devices or large amounts, and some require a captcha or a hold after a password change. These are normal protections. Do not share your two-factor codes or recovery details with anyone, including anyone claiming to be from us, because we never ask for them.

## Find and use the transaction ID
After the withdrawal is processed, the exchange shows a transaction ID, also called a hash or TXID. Copy it. You can add that ID on our status page, together with a screenshot if we ask for one, so we can find the transfer immediately. See [how to upload a payment screenshot](/blog/how-to-upload-a-payment-screenshot/). The ID also lets you look up the transaction on a public block explorer to see its status.

## Press "I have paid"
Once the exchange shows the withdrawal as sent, press "I have paid" in our payment window. Your order is placed and you land on the status page. If the withdrawal is still pending at the exchange, you can still press the button so the order exists, then wait for the transfer to arrive. See [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/).

## Minimums and delays
Some exchanges apply minimum withdrawals, so a small payment may not be allowed, or hold new addresses for a period. Plan ahead and check before you place the order. Some withdrawals are processed in batches rather than instantly, which can add minutes or hours. Learn about costs in [crypto network fees explained](/blog/crypto-network-fees-explained/).

## Common mistakes
- **Using an internal transfer.** It does not leave the exchange.
- **Accepting the default network.** Always check it against our window.
- **Forgetting the exchange fee.** The amount that arrives can be short.
- **Typing the address.** Always paste it.
- **Waiting too long to start.** Verification and holds can add days for a new account.
- **Resending when it is slow.** Check the status and contact us first.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I pay straight from an exchange to the payment window?
Yes. Withdraw to the address in the window on the matching network. The window does not know which exchange you use, and we match the payment by the transfer on the blockchain.

### What if my exchange charges a high fee?
Compare the fee between networks, or choose a different coin or network that the exchange supports at a lower cost. For smaller orders, a different payment method may be cheaper overall. See [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/).

### What if the exchange will not let me withdraw?
Contact the exchange's support, or choose a different way to pay. If time matters, a gift card or an app payment may be faster.

### Is it better to use a private wallet?
Either works. A private wallet gives you more control over the fee and avoids exchange holds, but needs setup. Use whichever you already have.

## A worked example
Suppose your order total after the 10% discount is $135.00 and you choose USDT on Tron. The payment window shows 135 USDT. Your exchange charges a flat withdrawal fee of 1 USDT, deducted from the amount. You open Withdraw, choose USDT, paste the address, choose Tron (TRC20), enter 136 USDT and confirm with your two-factor code. The exchange shows a transaction ID and the transfer arrives within a minute or two. You press "I have paid", the status page detects the transfer and your order is confirmed.

## After your payment is confirmed
Once your payment is confirmed you receive an email, and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and a regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). Read [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/) and [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) to prepare. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Security habits for exchange withdrawals
Exchange withdrawals are a common target for fraud, so a few habits help. Enable two-factor authentication on your exchange account, preferably with an authenticator app rather than text messages. Use a strong, unique password. Be wary of emails or messages that claim your withdrawal is blocked and ask you to click a link or share a code, because genuine exchanges do not ask for your codes. Type the exchange's address into your browser yourself instead of following links. And never share your recovery details with anyone. These habits protect your funds whether or not you are paying us.

## How long should you allow?
If your account is verified and the address is not new, a withdrawal can arrive in minutes. If you are adding a new address, expect a possible security hold of several hours or a day on some exchanges. If you are a new user waiting for verification, allow days. Plan around these delays, especially if you want your order to enter processing quickly. If timing is tight, a gift card or an app payment may be quicker; see [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/).

## If something goes wrong with a withdrawal
If the exchange shows the withdrawal as complete but the status page shows nothing after the normal time for that network, copy the transaction ID and look it up on a public block explorer for the network you used. The explorer shows whether the transfer is pending, confirmed or failed, and the destination address. If the destination does not match our window, contact the exchange immediately and tell us. If it matches and is confirmed, add the ID to the status page and contact us, and we will check the match. Having the ID ready turns a vague worry into a specific question that can be answered quickly.

faq.q: Can I pay directly from an exchange?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the exchange allows withdrawals to external addresses. Withdraw to the address in our payment window on the matching network.

faq.q: Why did less arrive than I sent?
faq.a: Some exchanges deduct their withdrawal fee from the amount you enter. Add the fee on top next time.

faq.q: Which network should I pick on the exchange?
faq.a: The one shown in our payment window. Exchanges often default to a different one, so check it carefully.

faq.q: What is a transaction ID?
faq.a: A unique code for your transfer, also called a hash or TXID. Add it on our status page so we can find the payment quickly.

faq.q: Why is my withdrawal delayed?
faq.a: Exchanges may hold new addresses or large amounts for security checks, or process withdrawals in batches.

faq.q: Can I use an internal transfer or pay-a-friend feature?
faq.a: No. Those only work between users of the same platform and do not reach our address.

title: Scanning a Wallet QR Code and Copying the Address Correctly
summary: A single wrong character sends crypto to the wrong place. Learn to use QR codes and copy buttons and to double-check an address before sending.
body:
Crypto addresses are long strings of letters and numbers, and one wrong character sends your funds to a different address, with no way to undo it. That is why you should never type an address by hand. The payment window at One Stop Vape Store gives you two reliable options: scan the QR code or use the copy button. This guide explains how each option works, how to scan from a phone and from a desktop, how to double-check the address after you paste or scan, why malware can swap copied addresses, how to check the network and the amount, whether a test transfer is worth it and what to do if something does not look right. It is written for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## What the address and QR code are
An address is where the payment goes. The QR code is simply the same address, and sometimes the amount, encoded as a picture your camera can read. Because the code and the text address come from the same source, they always match. Scanning is faster and avoids typing mistakes, and copying and pasting does the same job. Either way, your wallet gets the exact address without you typing a single character.

## Option 1: scan the QR code
Open your wallet app, choose Send, then tap the scan icon and point your camera at the QR code in the payment window. The wallet fills in the address for you, and sometimes the network and amount as well. Hold the phone steady and make sure the whole code is in view. If your screen is dim or glossy, increase the brightness or tilt the screen slightly to avoid glare. If the code does not scan, try again from a bit further back, and fall back to the copy button.

## Option 2: use the copy button
Tap the copy icon next to the address and paste it into your wallet. This avoids mistakes that come from retyping, and it works on a desktop where scanning is awkward. After you paste, look at the address in the wallet to confirm that it has pasted completely and nothing else was added to it.

## Always double-check
After pasting or scanning, compare the first four and last four characters with the address on screen. Some malware swaps copied addresses for a different one, so a quick visual check is a good habit, especially for larger payments. The check takes seconds. If the first or last characters differ, do not send. Clear your clipboard, copy the address again and, if it still differs, scan the QR code with a different device and contact us through the [contact page](/contact/).

## Check the network too
Your wallet may show a network selector, especially for tokens such as USDT, which exist on several networks. It must match the one in our window; see [what is a crypto network](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/). The address prefix gives a quick clue: Bitcoin addresses start with bc1, 1 or 3, Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain addresses start with 0x, Tron addresses start with T and Solana addresses are long strings with no prefix. Remember that Ethereum and BNB addresses look alike, so check the network label as well.

## Enter the amount
Use the amount shown, copied with its own button where available. Typing a number is fine, but read it twice. The amount is based on the live rate and refreshes about every 30 seconds, so if you leave the window open for a while, refresh it and use the new figure. A small tolerance covers normal movement, but a large gap shows as underpaid. See [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/) and the walkthrough in [how to pay with Bitcoin](/blog/how-to-pay-with-bitcoin/).

## Should you make a tiny test first?
For large amounts, some people send a small test transfer first. That adds a second network fee but can give peace of mind that the address and network are right. Whether it is worth it depends on the fee. On Solana or Tron the cost is tiny, so a test is cheap. On Ethereum it may cost more than it is worth. If you do send a test, tell us, because our system matches one transaction to one order, and we need to know both transaction IDs so we can match your payment correctly.

## If you are on a desktop
You can scan the QR code from your phone's wallet app while the payment window is open on your computer, or copy the address on the desktop and paste it into a browser-based wallet. Whichever you choose, do the compare-the-ends check on the final screen before you confirm. If you use a hardware wallet, check the address on the device's own screen as well, because that screen cannot be altered by malware on your computer.

## What a scam looks like
Genuine payment details come only from the payment window on our site or from our official email, WhatsApp number and private order page. We never ask you to send crypto to an address in a chat message from someone you do not know, and we never ask for private keys or recovery phrases. If anyone sends you a different address and says it is ours, do not use it, and contact us. See [how payment details reach you](/blog/how-payment-details-reach-you/).

## Common mistakes
- **Typing the address.** Always scan or copy.
- **Skipping the final check.** Compare the first and last characters.
- **Scanning the wrong code.** Scan only the QR code in the current window.
- **Ignoring the network.** Match it to the label.
- **Sending an old amount.** Refresh the window if it has been open a while.
- **Resending if it looks slow.** Check the status page first.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does the QR code include the amount?
It may, depending on your wallet. Always check the amount on the final send screen and compare it with the window.

### Why does my wallet say the address is invalid?
It may be the wrong network for the address or an incomplete paste. Check the network, paste again and compare the ends.

### Can I save the address for later?
Do not. Each payment window gives the current details, and you should copy them fresh each time.

### What if my camera cannot read the code?
Use the copy button, or open the window on a larger screen and try again.

## After your payment is confirmed
Once your payment is confirmed you receive an email, and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and a regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). Read [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/) and [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) to prepare. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Building a reliable habit for every payment
The best protection against address errors is a routine you follow every time. Open the payment window, scan or copy the address, paste it, read the first four and last four characters aloud or in your head, check the network label, enter or confirm the amount, and only then press send. The routine takes under thirty seconds and removes nearly every address mistake. If you ever skip a step because you are in a hurry, that is exactly the moment errors happen, so slow down on larger payments.

## Using more than one device
Some people keep the payment window on a computer and send from a phone. That works well, because the phone scans the code directly from the screen. Just make sure that the window you are looking at is the current one, that it has not expired and that you are not mixing it up with a window from an earlier order. Each order has its own reference, address details and amount, so always match the order reference on screen with the order you are paying.

## What to do if the address does not match
Stop and do not confirm. Clear your clipboard by copying a short piece of ordinary text, copy the address again from the payment window and paste it once more. If the pasted address still differs from the one on screen, your device may have software that alters copied text. Switch to scanning the QR code with a different device, or send from a different device altogether, and run a security scan on the affected one. Contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) so we know what happened, and never send funds to an address that does not match the current window. Most of the time the mismatch is a simple incomplete paste, and pasting again fixes it.

### Frequently asked questions in depth
**Can I screenshot the QR code and scan it later?** Please do not. Each payment window shows the current details for one order, and an old screenshot may be out of date. Scan or copy from the live window.

**Is it fine to share a photo of the QR code with a friend who will pay for me?** It is better to have them pay from the window itself, with your order reference visible, and to tell us who is paying so that we can match the payment correctly.

faq.q: Why shouldn't I type the address by hand?
faq.a: One wrong character sends the funds to a different address and cannot be undone. Scan the QR code or use the copy button.

faq.q: How do I check the address after pasting?
faq.a: Compare the first four and last four characters with the address in the payment window.

faq.q: Can malware change a copied address?
faq.a: Yes, some malware swaps copied addresses. A quick visual check of the ends, and checking the address on a hardware wallet screen if you use one, protects you.

faq.q: What if the QR code does not scan?
faq.a: Increase screen brightness, move back slightly or use the copy button.

faq.q: Does the QR code include the amount?
faq.a: It may, depending on your wallet. Always check the amount on the final send screen against the window.

faq.q: Should I send a test transfer first?
faq.a: It is optional and adds a second fee. If you do, tell us both transaction IDs so we can match your payment.

title: Crypto Network Fees Explained: Gas, Sats and Why They Vary
summary: Every crypto transfer pays a fee to the network, not to us. See how fees work on each chain and how to keep yours low.
body:
When you send cryptocurrency you pay a network fee to the people or validators who process transactions. We do not receive or control that fee, and it is separate from the amount of your order. Fees vary widely depending on the blockchain you use and how busy it is, which is why they matter when you choose a coin and network for a payment at One Stop Vape Store. A large fee on a small order can cancel much of the 10% crypto discount, while a tiny fee leaves almost all of it. This guide explains how fees work on each network we accept, why they change, how to estimate them, how to keep them low, how exchange fees differ from network fees and how to make sure the right amount arrives. It is written for adults aged 21 and over and is not financial advice.

## What a network fee is
Blockchains are maintained by many computers that agree on which transactions are valid. The people running them are paid, through fees, to include your transaction in the next block. When many people want to transact at once, space in blocks is scarce and fees rise. When the network is quiet, fees fall. Your wallet usually estimates the fee for you, and often lets you pick a speed: a higher fee for faster inclusion, a lower fee for slower.

There are two different kinds of fee to keep apart. The network fee is paid to the blockchain. An exchange or provider fee is charged by the platform you use, for example when you withdraw coins from an exchange. You may pay both, and neither goes to us.

## Bitcoin
Bitcoin fees depend on the size of the transaction in bytes and on network demand, usually expressed in satoshis per byte. A simple payment is a small transaction, so the fee is modest in quiet periods and higher when many people transact. Most wallets let you pick economy, standard or priority speeds. A standard setting is usually fine. A very low fee can leave a transaction waiting for hours when the network is busy. See [how to pay with Bitcoin](/blog/how-to-pay-with-bitcoin/).

## Ethereum
Fees on Ethereum are called gas. They depend on demand, and token transfers such as USDT cost more than plain ETH because they run more computation. Busy times can make a small payment expensive, while quiet times, such as early mornings and weekends in US time zones, can be much cheaper. Gas is paid in ETH, so you need some ETH in the wallet even if you are sending a token. See [paying with Ethereum](/blog/pay-with-ethereum-eth/).

## Tron
Tron uses resources called bandwidth and energy. If you do not hold them, the network burns a small amount of TRX to cover the transaction. Many exchanges simply charge a flat withdrawal fee in USDT, which is usually small and predictable. USDT on Tron is popular for payments because the cost is low and the speed is good. See [USDT on ERC20 or TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/).

## Solana
Fees are tiny, usually a fraction of a cent. Keep a small amount of SOL for fees even if you send USDC, because the fee is paid in SOL. This makes Solana ideal for smaller orders, because nearly all of the discount is kept. See [paying with Solana](/blog/pay-with-solana-sol/) and [USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/).

## BNB Smart Chain
Fees are low and paid in BNB. A transfer usually costs a few cents or less. See [paying with BNB](/blog/pay-with-bnb-smart-chain/).

## A fee comparison for planning
The numbers change all the time, so think in ranges:

- **Solana:** a fraction of a cent.
- **Tron (USDT):** typically well under a dollar, often a flat exchange fee.
- **BNB Smart Chain:** typically a few cents or less.
- **Bitcoin:** typically cents to a few dollars, depending on demand and the speed you choose.
- **Ethereum:** typically cents to many dollars, depending on demand and whether you send ETH or a token.

For a $150 order, the 10% discount is $15. A $0.01 fee leaves almost all of it. A $10 fee leaves a third. That is why the network matters.

## Ways to keep fees down
- **Choose a network with cheap fees,** such as TRC20 or Solana.
- **Avoid peak times on Ethereum,** and check an estimate before you send.
- **Compare withdrawal fees on exchanges,** because they differ by network and coin.
- **Choose a sensible speed setting,** not the fastest one by default.
- **Send one transaction,** not several small ones, because each pays a fee.
- **Pay on the network where your funds already sit,** instead of bridging, which adds fees.

## Fees and the amount we receive
Make sure the amount arriving equals the amount in our window. Some exchanges deduct their withdrawal fee from the amount you enter, so less arrives than you intended, and the payment shows as underpaid. The fix is to add the fee on top. Other wallets add the network fee on top, so the amount arriving matches what you entered. Check which your wallet does, and see [sending crypto from an exchange to a wallet](/blog/send-crypto-from-an-exchange-to-a-wallet/) and [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/).

## Fees and the 10% discount
The discount is calculated on your product subtotal and is not reduced by network fees. But your overall saving is the discount minus the fees you pay to get and send the crypto. If you have to buy crypto first, include provider fees too. Compare the total with a standard-price method before you decide. See [the 10% crypto and gift card discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/) and [how to buy crypto with a card](/blog/how-to-buy-crypto-with-a-card/).

## Common mistakes
- **Forgetting the fee currency.** Ethereum needs ETH, Solana needs SOL and Tron may need TRX.
- **Sending your whole balance.** Leave enough for the fee.
- **Choosing the lowest fee on a busy network.** The transaction can get stuck.
- **Sending twice because it looks slow.** Check the transaction status first.
- **Ignoring the exchange fee.** It is separate from the network fee.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do you charge a fee for crypto payments?
No. The only fees are the network fee and any fee charged by your exchange or wallet provider. We charge nothing extra for crypto, and we give a 10% discount.

### Can I get a refund of the network fee?
No. Network fees go to the network and are not refundable. If a refund of an order is ever due, it goes back through the same payment method, less the 15% restocking fee where it applies.

### Why did my fee change between two payments?
Demand changed. Fees move with how many people are transacting at that moment, and some networks change every few seconds.

### What if my transaction is stuck because the fee was too low?
Many wallets let you speed it up or cancel and resend. Check before you send a second payment, and contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) if you are unsure.

## After your payment is confirmed
Once your payment is confirmed you receive an email, and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and a regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). Read [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/) and [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) to prepare. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A worked example: the same $150 order on three networks
Suppose your order is $150 before the discount, so the 10% crypto discount is $15.00 and the product total is $135.00, plus $15 shipping because it is under $200, making $150.00 due. Paying in USDC on Solana costs a fraction of a cent in fees, so you keep almost all of the $15 saving. Paying in USDT on Tron through an exchange with a flat 1 USDT fee costs $1, so you keep $14. Paying in USDT on Ethereum in a busy period with a $10 gas fee costs $10, so you keep $5. The discount is identical, but the net saving is very different, which is why choosing the network with sensible fees is worth a minute of thought.

## When a higher fee is worth it
Sometimes paying a higher fee makes sense. If you need a payment to confirm quickly and the network is busy, a higher fee can be the difference between minutes and hours. If your funds are already on a particular network and moving them would cost more than the fee, it can be cheaper to pay the fee than to bridge. And if the order is large, a fee that looks big in absolute terms is small relative to the 10% saving. The goal is not always the lowest fee, but the best overall outcome for your order.

faq.a: The people or validators who process transactions on the blockchain. We do not receive or control it.

faq.a: Solana is usually a fraction of a cent. Tron and BNB Smart Chain are also cheap. Ethereum varies with demand.

faq.a: The discount itself is not reduced, but your overall saving is the discount minus the fees you pay to send or buy the crypto.

title: Sent Crypto on the Wrong Network? What to Do Next
summary: Mistakes happen. If you used the wrong network or address, here are the steps to take immediately and what is realistically recoverable.
body:
Sending crypto on the wrong network is one of the most common mistakes in crypto payments, and it can happen to careful people. A wallet or exchange defaults to a network you did not intend, or an address looks right because two chains use the same address style, and the transfer goes through on the wrong chain. If this has happened to you at One Stop Vape Store, do not panic, and do not send more funds. This guide explains what to do in the first minutes, what the different cases mean, what we can and cannot do, how to contact us and your provider, why you should wait before resending and how to avoid the mistake next time. It is written for adults aged 21 and over, it is general information and it is not financial or legal advice.

## Stop and gather details
Before you do anything else, stop. Do not send another transfer, and do not try to "fix" it by sending the same funds again. Then collect the details of what happened:

- **The transaction hash,** also called the transaction ID or TXID.
- **The coin** you sent and the **network** you used.
- **The amount** and the **time** of the transfer.
- **The address** you sent to.
- **Your order reference** from our payment window or email.
- Screenshots of the exchange or wallet confirmation.

Having these ready makes everything that follows faster, for you and for us.

## Understand what happened
There are a few cases, and which one you are in decides what can be done.

### Right coin, wrong network, address compatible
On some networks that use the same address style, such as Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain, the same address string is valid on several chains. The funds may be sitting at that address on the other chain. Whether we can recover them depends on whether we control the address on that chain and on whether our wallet software supports it. In some cases it can be done, and in others it cannot.

### Address format incompatible
If the address format does not match the network, the transaction usually fails or is blocked by the exchange or wallet before it leaves. In that case your funds typically remain where they were, and you can try again on the correct network. Check your balance and your transaction history to confirm.

### Sent to an address we do not control
If the transfer landed on an address that nobody we know controls, the funds are unrecoverable by anyone. That is the harshest case, and it is why checking the network and the address before you confirm matters so much.

### Right network, wrong token
A related mistake is sending a different token on the right network, for example sending USDC when the window asked for USDT. Recovery depends on the same question: whether we control the address and can handle that token.

## Contact us right away
Use the [contact page](/contact/) or WhatsApp with your order reference and the details above. We will check what arrived and tell you honestly whether anything can be done. We cannot promise recovery, as it depends on whether we control the receiving address on that chain and whether it is technically possible. If a recovery is possible, there may be costs, which we will explain before we do anything, and we will not proceed without your agreement. We will also tell you how your order is affected: it stays unpaid until a valid payment arrives, so do not assume that a transfer on the wrong network has paid it.

## Contact the sender's provider too
If you used an exchange, open a support ticket. Some can help with wrong-network deposits in limited cases, especially when the problem is on their side, such as a deposit to an address they control. Give them the transaction hash, the network and the details above. If you used a private wallet, check the wallet's support pages, because some have recovery tools for specific mistakes.

## Do not resend yet
Wait until we confirm what we can see. Resending without checking can double the problem: if the first transfer is recoverable and you pay again on the right network, you may end up having paid twice. If you need the order urgently, tell us, and we can discuss options, including switching to a different payment method for the order such as a gift card or an app payment, which we can set up while the first transfer is investigated.

## What happens to your order
Your order exists but remains unpaid until a valid payment arrives. Orders do not begin processing until payment is confirmed. If the original payment cannot be recovered, you will need to pay again, on the correct network or with another method. Unpaid orders may be released after a period so stock is not held indefinitely, so keep in touch with us so we can note your order while the situation is sorted out.

## Avoiding it next time
Most wrong-network mistakes come from a handful of habits that are easy to change:

- **Match the network label** in the payment window with the one in your wallet, every time.
- **Do not accept the default** network on an exchange without checking it.
- **Use the copy button** or scan the QR code, and compare the first and last characters.
- **Read [what is a crypto network](/blog/what-is-a-crypto-network/)** so that the names are familiar.
- **For stablecoins,** read [USDT on ERC20 or TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/) and [USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/), since the same token exists on several networks.
- **For larger amounts,** consider a small test transfer, and tell us if you do.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can you guarantee I will get my funds back?
No. Recovery depends on the specific situation and is sometimes impossible. We will tell you honestly what we can see and what, if anything, can be done.

### How long does a recovery take?
It varies. If recovery is possible, it usually takes longer than a normal payment because it needs manual steps. We will keep you informed.

### Will my order still ship?
Orders ship once a valid payment is confirmed. If the original transfer cannot be used, you will need to pay again or choose another method.

### Is there a fee for trying to recover?
If recovery involves costs, we will tell you before we start. We will not charge you without your agreement.

### What if the mistake involved a large amount?
Contact us immediately and the exchange or wallet provider too. The sooner everyone knows, the better the chance of a good outcome.

## Related reading
See [why your crypto payment shows underpaid](/blog/why-your-crypto-payment-shows-underpaid/) if only the amount was wrong, [how we detect your crypto payment](/blog/how-we-detect-your-crypto-payment/) for how matching works and [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/) if you would like a different route.

## After your payment is confirmed
Once your payment is confirmed you receive an email, and your order status changes to payment confirmed. The order then enters processing, which takes 24 to 72 business hours at our Phoenix, Arizona Stock Warehouse. When it ships, you receive a tracking email, and a regional carrier delivers it. An adult aged 21 or older must sign on delivery and may be asked to show photo ID, so choose an address where that is possible. You can follow every stage from the private link in your order email, and the meaning of each status is explained in [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/). Read [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/) and [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) to prepare. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A short checklist for when you are stressed
Mistakes feel urgent, and urgency leads to more mistakes. Use this calm sequence. First, breathe and stop sending. Second, write down the hash, the coin, the network, the amount, the time and the address. Third, take screenshots. Fourth, check your wallet or exchange to see whether the transfer is complete or failed. Fifth, contact us with your order reference and those details. Sixth, contact your exchange or wallet support. Seventh, wait for our reply before you try any other payment. Following the steps in order keeps you from making a second error while the first is being sorted out.

## How we handle these cases
When you contact us, we look at the blockchain data for the transaction, confirm which network and address it went to and check whether we control that address on that chain. We then tell you plainly what we found. If the transfer is recoverable, we explain the steps and any costs, and we proceed only with your agreement. If it is not, we say so, and we help you complete your order another way. In every case we keep your order open for a reasonable time so that you do not lose your place while we sort it out.

## Keeping a record
Whatever the outcome, keep a record of everything: the transaction hash, screenshots, your messages with us and with your provider and the dates and times. If a recovery is possible, a clear record speeds it up, and if it is not, the record helps you understand what happened and avoid it again. Store it somewhere private, and do not post transaction details or order references publicly. If you are asked for it by us, send it through the official channels listed on our [contact page](/contact/).

faq.a: Stop, do not send more funds, and gather the transaction hash, coin, network, amount, time, address and your order reference.

faq.q: Can you recover my funds?
faq.a: Maybe, but we cannot promise it. It depends on whether we control the receiving address on that chain and whether recovery is technically possible.

faq.q: Should I send the payment again?
faq.a: Wait until we confirm what we can see. Resending without checking can double the problem.

faq.q: Is my order affected?
faq.a: It stays unpaid until a valid payment arrives, so it does not begin processing until then.

faq.q: Who else should I contact?
faq.a: Your exchange's or wallet's support, with the transaction hash and network details.

faq.q: How do I avoid this next time?
faq.a: Match the network label in our window, do not accept defaults on exchanges, use the copy button or QR code and compare the first and last characters.
