title: Wholesale Ordering Guide for Vape Shops and Retailers
summary: Running a store? Learn how our wholesale program works, what to prepare and how to place a bulk order with volume pricing.
body:
We supply vape shops and other adult-only retailers with volume pricing across our catalog of disposables, e-liquids, pods and pouches. If you run or manage a retail business and want to buy in bulk, this guide explains who qualifies, how to apply, what to prepare, how pricing and payment work, how shipping and delivery apply to larger orders, how to plan your first order and what your responsibilities are as a reseller. It is written for adults aged 21 and over and for businesses that sell only to adults. It is general information, not legal advice, and you are responsible for following the laws that apply to your business.

## Who qualifies
Wholesale is for licensed retailers who can provide a business license or tax ID, and who sell only to adults aged 21 and over. Requirements vary by state and local law, and you are responsible for your own compliance, including any retail license, tax registration or product-listing rules in your area. We may ask for documents that show that your business is a registered retailer, and we may decline to supply a business that cannot show that it can lawfully sell vapor products. Our [wholesale page](/wholesale/) describes tax-exempt ordering for registered businesses, which applies where your documents support it.

## Why buy wholesale
Volume pricing lowers your cost per unit, which matters when you resell. Buying in bulk also reduces how often you reorder, which saves time and shipping costs, and it lets you stock a range of brands and flavors so your customers find what they want. Our catalog covers popular disposable brands, e-liquids in several bottle sizes, nicotine salts, pods, kits and nicotine pouches, so you can build a mixed order in one place.

## How to apply
Use the form on the [wholesale page](/wholesale/). Tell us your company name, your tax or resale ID, your contact details, your estimated monthly volume and what you want to stock. Our team replies by email, usually with questions or a request for supporting documents. The form sends a saved copy to our dashboard, so your request does not get lost. If you prefer to talk first, contact us through the [contact page](/contact/), WhatsApp, phone or email, and we will take it from there. See [how to become a wholesale customer](/blog/how-to-become-a-wholesale-customer/) for the step-by-step process.

## What to prepare
A complete application gets a faster reply. Have these ready:

- **Business name and legal entity.**
- **Tax or resale ID,** and a copy of your retail license where your state requires one.
- **A shipping address** that can accept adult-signature deliveries and has someone present during business hours.
- **A list of brands, products and quantities** you are interested in.
- **Your estimated monthly volume,** so that we can suggest sensible pricing tiers.
- **Contact details** for the person who will place orders and receive deliveries.

## Pricing
Volume pricing depends on quantity and product. It is not a single published list, because costs differ by brand and because quantities change what we can offer. Browse the [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) ranges to build a list of what you want, then send it to us with the quantities. We reply with availability and a quote for the items. Mixed orders are welcome, and you can negotiate quantities where it makes sense. Prices we quote are for the products and quantities we list, and we confirm them in writing before you pay.

### How the discounts relate
The 10% discount for cryptocurrency and gift cards applies to retail orders at checkout. For wholesale quotes, we explain whether it applies and how it combines with volume pricing when we send the quote. Do not assume that discounts stack until we confirm in writing.

## Payment
Wholesale orders can use the same payment options as retail: cryptocurrency, gift cards, Cash App, Apple Pay and Chime, subject to what suits the size of the order. Large amounts are best handled with a quote, because some methods have transfer limits, and because we want to confirm the total before you send it. Cryptocurrency handles large amounts well, and stablecoins give an exact figure. Read [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/) and [how to pay with Bitcoin](/blog/how-to-pay-with-bitcoin/) to choose.

## Shipping
Bulk orders ship under the same adult-signature rules as any other order. A parcel or pallet needs an adult aged 21 or older to sign and show photo ID. Our regional carriers deliver according to the estimates in the [shipping policy](/shipping/): 3 to 7 business days for the West Coast and 11 to 18 business days for the eastern half of the US, after 24 to 72 business hours of processing. Large orders may be reviewed for accuracy and compliance before shipping, which can add a little time. Plan your ordering around those lead times so that you do not run out of stock.

## Planning your first order
- **Start with your best sellers.** Look at what your customers buy most, and order enough for a few weeks.
- **Mix a few new products.** Adding a few new flavors lets you test demand without a large commitment.
- **Balance size and freshness.** E-liquid and pouches keep best in cool, dark storage, and large stocks should be rotated. See [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/) and [how to store nicotine pouches](/blog/how-to-store-nicotine-pouches/).
- **Check your local rules** on flavors and listings before you order, because some products may not be lawful to sell in your area.
- **Allow for lead times,** especially if you are in the eastern half of the country.

## Your responsibilities as a reseller
As a retailer, you are responsible for your own licensing, taxes and age checks. Verify the age of every customer, display required warnings, store products responsibly and follow local rules on flavors, packaging and advertising. We supply products to registered businesses, but we cannot take responsibility for how they are sold. Read [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/), [the PACT Act explained](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/) and [what 21+ age verification means](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/).

## Returns and problems
Our returns policy applies to wholesale orders as well: returns must be arranged within 30 days, with an RMA, and opened or used items cannot be returned. A 15% restocking fee applies to refunds, and shipping fees are not refunded. Puffco products do not qualify for refunds or exchanges. For wholesale orders, check the quote for any terms that differ, and ask us if you are unsure before you pay. If a parcel arrives damaged, photograph it and email us immediately. See [refund and return policy explained](/blog/refund-and-return-policy-explained/) and [damaged or missing items](/blog/damaged-or-missing-items-what-to-do/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is there a minimum wholesale order?
Minimums depend on the products and the pricing we offer. Tell us your target volume and we will confirm what applies.

### Can I place wholesale orders through the website?
Smaller trade orders can use the cart. Larger orders are best arranged with our team so that we can quote them. We will tell you which route suits your order.

### Do you offer recurring orders?
We can discuss regular supply once you have placed a first order. Tell us your expected monthly volume.

### Can you ship to several store locations?
Each parcel ships to one address, so multiple locations are handled as separate shipments. Tell us what you need.

### Do you supply customers who sell online?
We supply registered retailers who sell lawfully. Online sellers must comply with the rules for remote sales, including age verification and signature on delivery. Ask us if you are unsure.

## Next steps
Read [how to become a wholesale customer](/blog/how-to-become-a-wholesale-customer/) and [bulk buying tips](/blog/bulk-buying-vapes-save-money/), then send your application through the [wholesale page](/wholesale/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A worked example of a first wholesale order
A small vape shop in Nevada wants to stock disposables, a few bottles of salt e-liquid and nicotine pouches. The owner submits the form with the company name, resale ID, a copy of the state retail license and a list: three disposable brands in eight flavors each, two e-liquid brands and two pouch brands, with quantities. We reply within a few business days confirming that the documents are in order and send a quote with unit prices and a total. The owner asks to swap two flavors, we update the quote and confirm in writing. The owner pays with USDC on Solana, and the payment is matched automatically. After 24 to 72 business hours of processing, the order ships to the shop address, where the owner signs with photo ID. Because the shop is on the West Coast, transit is 3 to 7 business days. The owner checks the delivery against the invoice, photographs one dented box and emails us, and we sort it out.

## Questions to ask yourself before ordering
How fast do these products sell in my shop? How much shelf and storage space do I have? How long can I hold stock before it goes stale? What do local rules allow me to sell? How will I verify the age of every customer? Answering these before you order helps you choose quantities that match demand, rather than tying up money in stock you cannot move.

## Keeping a steady ordering rhythm
Wholesale works best as a rhythm rather than a one-off. Many retailers place a larger order every few weeks, topping up fast sellers and adding a few new products each time. Tell us what sold and what did not, and we can suggest changes. Keep notes of lead times for your region, and reorder before you run low, so that a delay in transit does not leave shelves empty.

title: How to Become a Wholesale Customer: Application Steps
summary: From first form to first order, here is what happens when you apply for wholesale and what we need from your business.
body:
Applying for a wholesale account with One Stop Vape Store is straightforward, and the process usually takes a short exchange of emails. This guide walks through each step from the first form to your first delivery, explains what we check and why, what documents help, how quotes and ordering work, how payment is handled, what to expect with shipping and what your responsibilities are once you become a customer. It is written for adults aged 21 and over and for registered retailers. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Before you apply
Make sure you have the basics in order. You should have a registered business, a tax or resale ID and, where your state requires one, a retail license for vapor products. You should sell only to adults aged 21 and over and have a way to verify age. You should have a delivery address that can accept adult-signature parcels and a person who will be there to sign. If any of these is missing, sort it out first, because it will save time and avoid a refusal. Our [wholesale ordering guide](/blog/wholesale-ordering-guide/) lists what to prepare.

## Step 1: submit the form
Fill in the form on the [wholesale page](/wholesale/) with your company name, tax or resale ID, contact details, volume estimate and requirements. Say which brands and categories you are interested in, such as disposables, e-liquids, pods or pouches, and roughly how much you expect to buy each month. A saved copy goes to our dashboard, and you receive a confirmation. If you prefer not to use the form, contact us by email, phone or WhatsApp with the same information. See [how to contact support](/blog/how-to-contact-support/).

## Step 2: we review
We check your details and may ask for a copy of your business license or proof of age-restricted retail status. This helps us comply with the rules for shipping vape products, and it protects both of us. We may also ask about your location, the products you plan to sell and how you verify age. A review is routine, and most applications that are complete are handled promptly. If we cannot supply a business, for example because we cannot ship lawfully to its location, we explain why.

### Documents that help
- **Business license or registration.**
- **Tax or resale certificate.**
- **State or local tobacco or vapor retail license,** where one applies.
- **Proof of the shop address,** such as a utility bill or a lease.
- **A contact who can sign for deliveries.**

## Step 3: receive a quote
We reply with product availability and volume pricing for the items you listed. You can negotiate quantities and mix products. The quote states the products, options such as strength and pack size, quantities, unit prices, total, shipping and any discounts that apply. Check it carefully, and ask us to change anything that is not right. Do not pay until you have a quote you are happy with, in writing.

## Step 4: place the order
Place the order through the website cart or by agreement with our team, depending on size. Smaller trade orders often work through the cart, with options chosen on each product page. Larger orders are arranged with us, and we confirm the details in writing. Large orders may be reviewed for accuracy and compliance before shipping, which is routine for wholesale volumes. We confirm the order, the total and the expected processing time.

## Step 5: pay
Choose a payment method with our team. See [payment methods compared](/blog/payment-methods-compared/) for fees and speed. Cryptocurrency, especially stablecoins, handles large payments well and is matched automatically on most networks. Gift cards and app payments suit smaller amounts because of limits. We confirm which method is best for the size of your order. Follow the matching guide, for example [paying with USDC on Solana](/blog/pay-with-usdc-on-solana/) or [USDT ERC20 vs TRC20](/blog/usdt-erc20-vs-trc20-which-network/), and send your proof if we ask. Orders begin processing once payment is confirmed.

## Step 6: receive and resell responsibly
Parcels arrive with adult-signature delivery, and the carrier checks government-issued photo ID. Plan for someone to be present. Check the delivery against your invoice as soon as it arrives, photograph any damage and tell us the same day. You are responsible for local licensing and age checks on your own sales. Learn more in [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/), [the PACT Act explained](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/) and [what 21+ age verification means](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/).

## How long does it take?
A complete application can be reviewed within a few business days, and a quote follows soon after. The longest delays come from missing documents, so send everything with your first message. After you pay, orders process within 24 to 72 business hours, and carriers take 3 to 7 business days to the West Coast or 11 to 18 business days to the eastern half of the US. Plan your first order with those lead times in mind.

## After your first order
Once you are set up, reordering is quicker, because we already have your details. Tell us how your first order sold, and we can suggest quantities for next time. If you want to add products, send a list. If you want regular deliveries, tell us your schedule. Keep records of your purchases and invoices for your own bookkeeping and for any inspection you may face as a retailer.

## Common questions
### Do I need a physical shop?
We supply registered retailers. If you sell online or through another lawful channel, tell us how, and we will say whether we can supply you. Remote sellers must follow the rules for remote sales.

### Can individuals buy wholesale?
Wholesale is for businesses. Individuals can use the regular store, where the 10% discount for cryptocurrency and gift cards applies and bulk buying still lowers your cost per item. See [bulk buying tips](/blog/bulk-buying-vapes-save-money/).

### Is there a fee to open an account?
We do not describe any account fee. Pricing is in the quote, and we confirm everything before you pay.

### What if my application is declined?
We explain the reason where we can. If it is a documentation issue, you can resubmit with the missing items.

### Can I get samples?
Ask us. Sample availability depends on the products, and sample packs cannot be partially returned if opened.

## Staying in touch
Keep your contact details current, and tell us if your address, license or business details change. Contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with any question. Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) to build your list. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Common reasons applications are delayed
- **Missing tax or resale ID.** Include it in the first message.
- **No retail license where one is required.** Check your state's rules and attach it.
- **An address that cannot accept signature deliveries.** Give a street address with staff present.
- **An unclear product list.** List brands, flavors and quantities, even roughly.
- **Mismatched names.** Use the same business name on the form, the documents and the delivery address.

Fixing these before you apply saves days. A short checklist next to the form helps you remember everything.

## A sample first message
"Hello, I run [shop name] in [city, state]. Our business is registered as [legal name], resale ID [number], and I have attached our retail license. We would like to stock disposables from [brands], e-liquid from [brands] and pouches from [brands]. Our expected monthly volume is about [amount]. Our delivery address is [address], and [name] will sign for deliveries with ID. Please send availability and volume pricing." A message like this answers almost every question we would ask.

## Building the relationship
The best wholesale relationships are built on clear communication. Tell us early if your needs change, flag problems promptly and keep your documents current. We, in turn, tell you about availability, changes that affect your area and anything we need from you. Treat it as a partnership: the smoother it runs, the easier it is to scale your orders as your shop grows.

## Frequently asked questions about onboarding
### What happens to my documents?
They are used only to confirm that your business can lawfully buy and resell vapor products, and they are handled under our [privacy policy](/privacy/). Send copies, not originals, and tell us if you would like us to delete them after review, subject to legal record-keeping requirements.

### Can several people from my business order?
Yes. Tell us who is authorized to place orders and who will receive deliveries, and we will note it against the account so there is no confusion.

### What if I run more than one shop?
Tell us the details of each, because licenses, addresses and tax IDs may differ. Each location receives its own deliveries, and we can discuss how to organize orders.

## A short checklist before you press submit
1. Business name matches your documents.
2. Tax or resale ID included.
3. Retail license attached where required.
4. Delivery address can accept adult-signature parcels.
5. Product list and rough quantities included.
6. A contact name, email and phone number that you answer.

With those six items in your first message, a review is usually quick, and you can move on to the quote.

title: Why We Ask for Your Email and Phone Number at Checkout
summary: Email and phone are required for orders. See what we use them for, what we never do with them and how they speed up delivery.
body:
Checkout asks for an email address and a phone number, and some customers wonder why. Both are needed for good reasons: your email is where your order confirmation, payment details and tracking arrive, and your phone number lets carriers and our team reach you when a delivery or a payment needs attention. This guide explains the reason for each, what we do and do not do with them, how they relate to our privacy policy, how to keep them accurate, how marketing is handled, what choices you have and what to do if you do not want to share a particular detail. It is written for adults aged 21 and over.

## Email: confirmations and payment details
Your email address receives your order confirmation, which includes your order ID and your private link. It also receives payment details for methods like Cash App, Apple Pay, Chime and gift cards, proof upload links, your payment confirmation and your tracking number. Without a valid email, you would not receive these, and the order could stall. Email also gives you a written record that you can search later. See [how ordering works](/blog/how-ordering-works/) and [how payment details reach you](/blog/how-payment-details-reach-you/).

### Why we do not use a different channel only
Some customers ask whether we could use only a phone number. Email is the best place for long, detailed messages with links, and it works on every device. Phone and chat complement it. We keep email as the main channel because it provides a reliable record for both of us.

## Phone: delivery and urgent issues
Carriers sometimes need to reach the recipient to arrange an adult-signature delivery, because the driver cannot leave the parcel. We may also call about payment mismatches, address questions or an order that needs a quick decision. If you choose WhatsApp, we use the same number for chat. Giving us a number that you answer, with the correct area code, avoids missed deliveries. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) and [shipping address tips](/blog/shipping-address-tips/).

## Why both?
Email and phone serve different needs. Email is for records and instructions. Phone is for urgency. Having both means that if one fails, such as an email that lands in spam, we can reach you another way. That is especially useful with payments, where time matters, and with deliveries, where a missed call can lead to a returned parcel.

## What we do with your information
We use it to fulfill your order, process payments, provide support and meet legal obligations. We do not sell personal data. We share it only with service providers who help us run the store, such as hosting, order storage, email and carriers, and only as needed. The full details are in our [privacy policy](/privacy/) and, for California residents, the [California privacy notice](/california-privacy/). If live chat is enabled, messages you type there are handled by the chat provider under its own policy.

## Your email and phone are not shown publicly
Your details are not published on the site, and the private order page is available only to people who have its link. Staff who handle your order can see them, and only for the purposes above. Carriers see your name, address and phone number, because they need them to deliver.

## Keeping it accurate
Typos cause missed emails and missed calls. Double-check your email address and your phone number before you submit. Use an address you check often, and add our address to your contacts. If something went wrong, see [what to do if the confirmation email does not arrive](/blog/order-confirmation-email-not-arriving/). If you change your number or email while an order is open, tell us, quoting your order ID.

## Marketing
We do not use your order information for marketing without your consent. Messages we send about your order are service messages, such as confirmations and tracking, and are not marketing. If we ever offer news or offers, you will be asked, and you will be able to opt out.

## Your choices
You can ask us to update or delete your information, subject to legal requirements. Use the [contact page](/contact/) and write from the address on your order. We may need to keep some records for tax, accounting and legal reasons, as explained in the privacy policy. California residents have additional rights described in the [California privacy notice](/california-privacy/).

## What if I do not want to share a phone number?
A phone number is required for checkout because of the delivery and payment reasons above. If you have a concern, contact us before you order, and we will tell you what is possible. Some customers use a number that they answer rather than a personal mobile, such as a work line, where that suits them.

## What we never ask for
We never ask for your passwords, card numbers, PINs, private keys or recovery phrases by email or phone. If a message claiming to be from us asks for them, do not respond, and tell us. See [gift card code security tips](/blog/gift-card-code-security-tips/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Will you call me without warning?
We call only about your order, such as a delivery or a payment question. We will not call to sell you something. If you prefer messages, tell us, and we will use WhatsApp or email where we can.

### Can I use a work email or phone?
Yes, if you check it regularly and it accepts messages from us. Work filters can block commercial email, so a personal address is often more reliable.

### Do you share my number with the carrier?
Yes, because the carrier may need to contact you to arrange delivery. It is shared for that purpose only.

### How long do you keep my details?
For as long as needed for your order, returns, tax, accounting and legal requirements, after which we delete or anonymize them. See the [privacy policy](/privacy/).

### What if I used someone else's email by mistake?
Contact us with your order ID. We will confirm your identity and update the order.

Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What each piece of information is used for, in one table of sentences
Your name appears on the order, the invoice and the shipping label so the carrier knows who the parcel is for. Your address is used for delivery and to check that we can lawfully ship to that place. Your email receives confirmations, payment details, proof links and tracking. Your phone number is used by the carrier and by us for delivery and urgent order questions. Your order details, such as items and totals, are used to fulfil the order and to answer questions about it. Your payment proof, such as a screenshot, is used only to confirm your payment. Nothing is collected without a purpose, and each item is described in the privacy policy.

## Good practice for protecting your own information
Use a strong, unique password for your email account, because email is where your order links and tracking arrive. Be wary of messages that imitate us and ask for sensitive information. Do not share your private order link. Keep your devices up to date and avoid entering personal details on networks you do not trust. These habits protect you with every online shop, not just ours.

## What happens to your data over time
After your order is complete, the records are kept for as long as needed for returns, tax, accounting and legal obligations. After that, they are deleted or anonymized. If you ask us to delete your information, we do so unless the law requires us to keep it, and we tell you what we have kept and why. You can ask at any time through the [contact page](/contact/).

## Special situations
### If you share a device or email
If someone else can see your email or phone, they can see our messages. Use an address and number that you control, and tell us if privacy is a concern, so we can send only what is needed.

### If you travel
If you are away from your usual email or phone, keep access to them through your phone or another device, so that you do not miss a delivery call or a payment message.

### If you have two numbers
Give the one you answer most. If you want us to use WhatsApp, give the number linked to your WhatsApp account.

## Frequently asked questions about contact details
### Can I change my email after I order?
Yes. Contact us from the address on the order, or give us the details of the order, and we will confirm your identity and update it. Do this before payment details are sent if you can.

### Why does the carrier call instead of leaving a note?
Because an adult must sign, the driver may call to arrange a time. Answering helps the delivery succeed on the first attempt.

### Do you ever contact me after the order is delivered?
Only if there is a reason connected with the order, such as a return, a question about a problem you reported or a reply to your message.

title: Shipping Address Tips: Avoid Missed and Returned Deliveries
summary: A good address and a plan for signature prevent most delivery problems. Use these tips for apartments, workplaces and gated buildings.
body:
Most delivery problems come from two causes: a small mistake in the address, or no one being available to sign. Both are easy to avoid if you know what to check, and avoiding them can save you weeks of delay and the cost of a returned parcel. This guide explains how to enter your address exactly, how to choose a place where an adult will be, how to handle apartments, gated communities and workplaces, why P.O. boxes do not work, how the name on the package matters, what to do if you will be away and how to fix a mistake. It follows our published [shipping policy](/shipping/) and is written for adults aged 21 and over.

## Use the exact address
Enter your address as it appears on your mail. Include the apartment, suite or unit number in the second address line, the full five-digit ZIP code and the correct city and state. Mismatches cause delays and returns. If the street name has a direction, such as North or SW, include it. If your address has changed recently, use the new one and check that the carrier will recognize it. Copy it from a recent bill or a mail label if you are unsure.

### Common address mistakes
- **Missing apartment or unit number,** which leaves the carrier unable to find the right door.
- **Wrong ZIP code,** which can send the parcel to the wrong facility.
- **Abbreviations that the carrier cannot read,** such as an unusual street suffix.
- **A different name on the mailbox,** so the carrier cannot match the recipient.
- **An old address,** especially after a move.

## Choose a place where an adult will be
Every package needs an adult aged 21 or older to sign with photo ID. A home address where someone is present during the day, or a workplace that allows personal deliveries, usually works best. If you are rarely home during the day, consider whether a trusted adult, a neighbor you know well or your workplace can receive it. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) for how the signing works.

## Gated communities and apartment buildings
Add gate codes, buzzer numbers and building notes in the order notes. Tell your building staff or neighbors to expect a delivery that needs a signature, because the carrier cannot leave the parcel at the door. If a front desk accepts packages, ask whether staff can sign for an adult-signature parcel, since many cannot. If they cannot, the carrier will need to reach you, so keep your phone number accurate and your phone on.

## Avoid P.O. boxes
Carriers cannot obtain a signature at a P.O. box. Use a street address instead. For the same reason, parcel lockers and some mailbox stores may not work for adult-signature deliveries. If you are unsure whether an address will work, ask us before you order.

## Name on the package
Use the name on your ID. Some carriers require the recipient's name to match the ID when they check it, and a mismatch can lead to a refused delivery. If another adult will receive the parcel, tell us in the order notes and check with the carrier. Use the same name on the order and on the doorbell or mailbox where you can, so the carrier is not confused.

## Phone number and email
Your phone number lets the carrier reach you if the address needs clarifying or a delivery needs rescheduling. Enter it with the area code, and keep it on during the delivery window. Your email receives our confirmations, tracking and your private link, so check it carefully. See [why we need your email and phone](/blog/why-we-need-your-email-and-phone/).

## Where we do not ship
Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands and military addresses are excluded from free shipping, and we do not ship internationally. Some states and cities restrict certain products, and we cannot ship where the law does not allow it. See [where we ship and where we do not](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/).

## If you will be away
If you will be away when the parcel is likely to arrive, tell us right away through the [contact page](/contact/), and consider delaying payment so the order does not process until you are back, or arranging for a trusted adult to receive it. A parcel that cannot be signed for is returned, and the refund is minus the 15% restocking fee and the shipping cost. Planning avoids that loss. See [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/).

## After you order
Watch for the tracking email, and open the carrier's tracking page when it arrives. Many carriers let you set up delivery alerts or choose a delivery window. Keep your ID ready, and make sure someone is available. If you see a delivery notice, follow the instructions at once. See [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/) and [what to do if your package is delayed](/blog/what-to-do-if-your-package-is-delayed/).

## A pre-order checklist
1. Is the street address complete and spelled correctly?
2. Is the apartment or unit number in the second line?
3. Is the ZIP code correct?
4. Is the name the same as on my ID?
5. Will an adult aged 21 or older be there to sign?
6. Is my phone number correct, and will my phone be on?
7. Have I added gate codes or building notes?
8. Is my email correct?

## Fixing a mistake
If you notice a mistake after you order, contact us immediately with your order ID and the corrected address, and wait for our written confirmation. Before the parcel is handed to the carrier, we can usually correct it. After that, we cannot change the address, and the carrier may return the parcel. See [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I use a work address?
Often yes, if your employer allows personal deliveries and an adult will be available to sign. Check your workplace rules first.

### What if my building has a package room?
A package room cannot take adult-signature parcels unless a staff member can sign. Ask your building staff, and give the carrier a way to reach you.

### What if I live in a rural area?
Delivery to rural addresses can take longer, and some carriers have limited coverage. Contact us with your address if you are unsure, and we will tell you what customers there typically see.

### What if my name is long or has special characters?
Enter it as it appears on your ID, and use plain letters where the form requires. If a carrier cannot read it, it may cause delays.

Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A worked example: a missed signature
A customer in an apartment building orders a parcel and enters the street address but forgets the unit number. The carrier arrives, cannot find the right door and cannot reach the customer, because the phone number has a typo. After two attempts the parcel is returned. The customer receives a refund minus the 15% restocking fee and the shipping cost, and has to order again and wait another two weeks. Two small errors, a missing unit number and a mistyped phone number, caused the whole delay. A thirty-second check before submitting would have prevented it.

## Habits that prevent most problems
Read the address back before you submit, preferably aloud. Compare it with a recent piece of mail. Check the phone number digit by digit. Tell anyone who lives with you or works nearby to expect a delivery that needs a signature. And save the tracking email so you can follow the parcel. These habits take a minute, and they make the difference between a smooth delivery and a returned one.

## Frequently asked questions about delivery windows
### Can I choose a delivery time?
That depends on the carrier. Some carriers let you pick a window or request a redelivery through their tracking page. Adult-signature parcels sometimes have fewer options, so check the carrier's page as soon as your tracking email arrives.

### Can I pick up the parcel from the carrier?
Some carriers hold a parcel at a facility after a missed delivery, and you can collect it with your ID. Follow the instructions on the delivery notice, and do it quickly, because holds are limited in time.

### What if I have a dog or a locked gate?
Make sure the carrier can reach the door, and add instructions in the order notes. A dog that prevents access can lead to a failed delivery attempt. Secure pets before the likely delivery window.

### Should I tell my neighbors?
If you share a building or a street with people who might sign, let them know a delivery is coming, and remind them that a parcel needing an adult signature should be handed to you, not left. Better still, be there yourself.

## Special cases
**Dormitories and shared houses.** Use the full building and room details, and make sure a resident aged 21 or older will sign. Some campuses restrict deliveries of age-restricted products, so check the rules first.

**Businesses with reception desks.** Ask whether the front desk may sign for an adult-signature parcel. If not, arrange for you or a colleague to receive it in person.

**Recently built addresses.** If your street is new, check that the carrier recognizes it, and add a note with the nearest cross street if needed.

faq.q: Where do I put the apartment number?
faq.a: In the second address line, together with the full ZIP code, so the carrier can find the exact door.

faq.q: Why can't I ship to a P.O. box?
faq.a: Adult signature is required, and a carrier cannot obtain a signature at a P.O. box.

faq.q: Whose name should be on the package?
faq.a: The name on the ID of the adult who will sign. Some carriers require the names to match.

faq.q: What if I live in an apartment building?
faq.a: Add gate codes, buzzer numbers and building notes in the order notes, and ask whether staff can sign for adult-signature parcels.

faq.q: What if I will be away?
faq.a: Tell us right away, consider delaying payment or arrange for a trusted adult to receive it. A parcel nobody signs for is returned.

faq.q: What if I made a mistake in the address?
faq.a: Contact us immediately with your order ID and the corrected address. We can usually fix it before the parcel is handed to the carrier.

title: Where We Ship and Where We Do Not
summary: We ship across the contiguous United States. Learn about the exclusions, state-by-state differences and why some orders may be reviewed.
body:
We ship from our Stock Warehouse in Phoenix, Arizona to customers across the United States, with some exceptions that are worth knowing before you order. This guide explains where free shipping applies, which areas are excluded, why we do not ship internationally, how state and local laws affect what we can deliver, how order review works and how to check whether we can ship to you. It follows our published [shipping policy](/shipping/) and is written for adults aged 21 and over. It is general information, and you are responsible for following the laws where you live.

## Where we ship
We deliver within the United States using regional carriers, with adult signature confirmation required on every parcel. Delivery times depend on your region: our published estimates are 3 to 7 business days in transit for the West Coast (Arizona, Nevada, Washington and Idaho) and 11 to 18 business days for the eastern half of the US. Places between those regions fall in between. See [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/).

## Where free shipping applies
Free domestic shipping on orders of $200 or more after discount and before tax is valid for most of the 48 contiguous states. It does not apply to Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, Hawaii, Alaska or APO, DPO, FPO and other U.S. military addresses. Orders to those places are subject to the standard shipping terms, and some may not be possible. If you live in one of those areas, contact us before you order and we will tell you what is available. See [minimum order and free shipping explained](/blog/minimum-order-and-free-shipping-explained/).

## International shipping
We do not offer international shipping. Orders placed with international addresses will be cancelled and refunded. International customers can call us for help finding a local distributor. We do not ship to freight forwarders or reshippers who would send the parcel abroad, because that would also be international shipping. This is not a preference but a limit of what we can lawfully and practically do: vapor products are regulated differently in each country, and exporting them involves rules we do not handle.

## State and local law
Some states and cities restrict or ban certain vaping products, require licensing or tax stamps, limit flavors or restrict nicotine strengths. We cannot ship where the law does not allow it, and we may cancel orders that cannot be delivered lawfully. Because rules change and differ widely, it is your responsibility to check the rules for your area before you order. Read [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/) and [vape taxes by state](/blog/vape-taxes-by-state-overview/) for background, and the [PACT Act overview](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/) for the federal framework.

### What we may do if an order cannot be delivered lawfully
If we find that an order cannot lawfully be delivered to your address, we will contact you. In most cases we cancel the order and refund it through the payment method used, and we tell you why. We do this to protect you and us, because a parcel that cannot be delivered lawfully may be seized or returned.

## Order review
Orders may be reviewed to ensure security and accuracy. A review checks that the details are consistent and that the order can be delivered. If an order is under review, we contact you the same day. A review is routine and not a sign of a problem, and it may add a short delay to processing. See [how ordering works](/blog/how-ordering-works/).

## Age and signature
Every delivery requires an adult aged 21 or older to sign, with government-issued photo ID. This applies in every state, to every parcel containing vapor products. The signature rule is part of federal law covered in our [PACT Act overview](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/), and it is explained in [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/). Choose an address where an adult can sign, and avoid P.O. boxes, because a carrier cannot obtain a signature at one. See [shipping address tips](/blog/shipping-address-tips/).

## Before you order
Check your local rules and make sure your address is within our shipping area. If you are unsure whether we can ship to you, ask via the [contact page](/contact/) before you pay. Give us your state and the type of product you plan to order, and we will tell you what we can do. Review the [shipping policy](/shipping/) for the latest terms. If your address is in an excluded area, tell us so we can advise on your options.

## Common questions about addresses
### Can I ship to a workplace?
Often yes, if your employer allows personal deliveries and someone aged 21 or older will be available to sign. Check your workplace's rules first.

### Can I ship to a friend or relative?
Yes, within the United States, provided an adult aged 21 or older will sign with ID. Tell us in the order notes if the recipient's name differs from yours.

### Can I ship to a hotel?
It is possible, but risky, because hotel staff often cannot sign for adult-signature parcels. A private address is more reliable.

### Can I ship to a P.O. box?
No. A carrier cannot obtain a signature at a P.O. box, so use a street address.

### Can I ship to a military address?
APO, DPO and FPO addresses are excluded from free shipping, and delivery to them may not be possible. Contact us before you order.

## Why these limits exist
Our limits come from three sources: federal law, which requires adult signature and tax compliance; state and local law, which varies; and practical limits of regional carriers, which do not serve every area equally. Staying inside those limits protects customers from seized parcels and protects us from violations, and it is why we are clear about them up front.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Will you ship to my state?
Most states, yes, subject to local rules. If your state or city restricts a product, we cannot ship it. Ask us if you are unsure.

### Does shipping outside the 48 contiguous states cost more?
Free shipping does not apply there, and costs and availability vary. Contact us before you order.

### What happens if I order from outside the US?
The order will be cancelled and refunded. International customers can call us for help finding a local distributor.

Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A worked example: checking whether we can ship to you
You live in a city that has recently introduced a flavor restriction. You are not sure whether the product you want is covered. You message us with your state, your city and the product page link. We check the rules we know of, tell you whether we can ship that product to your address and, if not, suggest products that are not affected. You decide what to order with the facts in front of you, and you avoid an order that has to be cancelled. This kind of question costs nothing and saves time, so ask whenever you are in doubt.

## Rules change, so check again
Laws on vapor products change often, and a product that could be shipped last year may be restricted this year. If you are a regular customer and your local rules change, tell us, and we will update how we handle your orders. If we learn of a change that affects your area, we will tell you before we ship. Keeping each other informed is the surest way to avoid a cancelled order.

## Frequently asked questions about restrictions
### Does the flavor of a product affect whether you can ship it?
In some places, yes. Certain states and cities restrict flavored products, so a flavor that is fine in one place may not be allowed in another. If you are not sure, ask before you order.

### Does nicotine strength affect shipping?
Some jurisdictions limit nicotine strengths or require specific labeling. If your area has such a rule, tell us and we will advise what we can ship.

### What if my area bans online sales of vapor products?
We cannot ship where the law prohibits it. If we learn that an order is going to such an area, we will cancel it and refund it through the payment method used.

### Do I have to prove where I live?
We confirm your age through the age gate and checkout, and the carrier confirms ID at delivery. We may contact you if something about an order needs clarification.

### What if I move?
Update your address on any new order, and tell us if you have a pending order that needs to change. Keep in mind that rules differ by place, so a move can change what we can ship to you.

## A note for travelers and people who move often
If you are traveling or between addresses, do not use a temporary location that you cannot be sure of, because a missed signature leads to a returned parcel. Order when you will be at an address for at least two to three weeks, or use an address where a trusted adult will be present. If you are moving soon, wait until you have settled, so that the parcel and the signature line up with your plans.

title: What 21+ Age Verification Means When You Buy Vapes Online
summary: Federal law sets 21 as the minimum age to buy tobacco and vaping products. Here is how age checks work from checkout to your doorstep.
body:
Since December 2019, the federal minimum age to buy tobacco products, including e-cigarettes, has been 21 across the United States. For anyone buying vapor products online, that single number shapes everything from the age gate on the website to the signature on the doorstep. This guide explains what 21+ age verification means in practice at One Stop Vape Store: what you confirm when you arrive, what checkout asks, what happens at delivery, why the rules are strict, how higher age limits and local rules can apply, why we never sell to anyone under 21 and what to do if you are buying for someone else. It is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live.

## The federal minimum age
In December 2019, federal law raised the minimum age of sale for tobacco products, including e-cigarettes and other vapor products, to 21 nationwide. The change is often called Tobacco 21. It applies to sales in stores and online, and it applies regardless of any older state or local age. Some states and cities also have their own rules, which can be stricter. Whatever the local rule, no one under 21 may lawfully buy these products from us.

## At our age gate
Our site shows an age confirmation when you arrive. You confirm that you are 21 or older to enter the store. The gate also shows the nicotine warning and a link to our terms. This is a first step and a reminder, not the only check, because a click cannot prove age on its own. If you are under 21, you should choose the option that says so, and you will not be able to browse the shop.

## At checkout
When you place an order, you confirm again that you are 21 or older, and you provide your name and shipping address. We check the order for consistency, and orders may be reviewed. We can refuse or cancel any order that we cannot verify, or that we believe may be for a minor, and we will tell you why where we can. Providing false information is not just against our terms: it can be unlawful. See our [terms](/terms/) and [FDA disclaimer](/fda-disclaimer/).

## At delivery
This is the check that matters most. The carrier requires an adult aged 21 or older to sign for the package and to show valid government-issued photo ID. The ID must show the person's date of birth and be current. The delivery employee compares the ID with the delivery and records the details according to the carrier's procedures. A parcel is not left unattended, and it is not handed to a minor. If no adult is available, the carrier retries and then returns the parcel, and a refund minus the 15% restocking fee and shipping cost applies. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/).

## Why the rules are strict
Federal and state rules for remote vape sales require adult signature confirmation, and the aim is to keep age-restricted products away from minors. Online sales are especially sensitive, because the seller cannot see the buyer. That is why the law puts the final check on the delivery employee, who can see the person and the ID. The [PACT Act overview](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/) explains the rule, and our [shipping policy](/shipping/) describes how we apply it.

## Higher age limits and other rules
Some places set rules that go beyond federal law. A state or city may set a higher minimum age, limit flavors, restrict quantities or require specific delivery arrangements. Others ban online sales of certain products altogether. Where a local rule is stricter than the federal one, the stricter rule applies. It is your responsibility to know the rules where you live. See [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/) and [where we ship and where we do not](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/).

## Never buy for minors
Buying vapor products for anyone under 21 is illegal, even if the buyer is an adult. If you buy for someone under 21, you may be breaking the law, and the consequences can be serious. Keep products out of reach of children, teenagers and pets, and do not share them with anyone underage. See [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/). If you are under 21, you should not use this site.

## What if my ID looks different?
Carriers accept current, valid government-issued photo ID that shows your date of birth, such as a driver's license, a state ID or a passport. If your ID is expired or damaged, get a replacement before delivery. If your name differs from the one on the order, tell us in the order notes so that the carrier can match them. A delivery employee cannot waive the ID check.

## What if I am an adult buying for an adult?
You can ship to another adult's address, provided that adult is 21 or older and will sign with ID. Tell us in the order notes if the recipient's name differs from yours. Do not use our service to buy for anyone under 21 or for resale to minors.

## How we handle your information
We use the age confirmation and the order details for the purposes in our [privacy policy](/privacy/): fulfilling your order, meeting legal obligations and preventing fraud. We do not sell your information. The carrier checks your ID at the door, and we do not receive a copy of it. If we ever need further verification, we will explain why and how.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is clicking the age gate enough?
It is a first step. The checks at checkout and at delivery are what meet the legal requirements.

### What if I turn 21 next week?
Wait until you are 21. A purchase before then is not lawful, even if delivery would be after your birthday, because the sale takes place when you order.

### Do older states' rules, such as 18, still apply?
No. The federal minimum is 21 in every state. A state rule can be higher, but it cannot be lower.

### What if someone else signs for my parcel?
Only an adult aged 21 or older may sign, and they must show ID. If you are unsure of the rules for your carrier, check before delivery.

### Do you ever ask for a copy of my ID?
We confirm age through the age gate and checkout, and the carrier checks ID at delivery. If we need more, we will explain why and ask only through our official channels.

## Our policies
Read the [terms](/terms/) and the [FDA disclaimer](/fda-disclaimer/), and the [PACT Act FAQ](/pact-act/). Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) only if you are 21 or older. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A short history of the minimum age
Before December 2019, the federal minimum age to buy tobacco products was 18, and many states and cities had already raised it to 21. The federal change made 21 the national minimum, so that the rule is the same everywhere in the country. Retailers and online sellers had to update their processes, and carriers had to apply it to deliveries. If you remember a time when the age was 18, that is no longer the rule, and an older state rule that is lower than 21 no longer applies.

## What age verification does and does not do
Age verification is a set of checks, not a single step. The age gate and checkout confirmations are declarations by you, the delivery check is a verification by a person looking at your ID, and the law together aims at keeping products away from minors. No single step is perfect, which is why they are layered. If you are an adult, the process is a minor inconvenience, and it is part of what lets online sales of these products exist under the law.

## Being a responsible adult buyer
If you are 21 or older and buy these products, you are also responsible for what happens to them afterward. Store them where children and pets cannot reach them, do not give or sell them to anyone under 21 and dispose of devices and batteries responsibly. If you suspect that someone is buying for minors, do not take part. If you are worried about a young person using these products, support is available from healthcare professionals and from public health services.

## Frequently asked questions about the process
### Does the age gate store my date of birth?
No. The age gate records only that you confirmed you are 21 or older, in your own browser, so that it does not ask again each time. It does not ask for your date of birth.

### What if I clear my browser data?
The age gate will appear again the next time you visit, and your cart will be empty. Confirm your age again to continue.

### Can I be refused at delivery even if the order was accepted?
Yes. The carrier's check is separate. If the signer cannot show valid ID that confirms they are 21 or older, the carrier will not hand over the parcel.

### Does the age check apply to every product?
Yes. Every product on the site, including pouches, accessories and devices, is for adults aged 21 and over, and every delivery requires adult signature.

faq.q: What if no adult is available to sign?
faq.a: The carrier retries and may return the parcel. A refund minus the 15% restocking fee and the shipping cost applies.

title: The PACT Act Explained for Vape Buyers
summary: The PACT Act changed how vape products are shipped, taxed and delivered. Here is a plain summary of what it means for online buyers.
body:
The Prevent All Cigarette Trafficking Act, usually called the PACT Act, was amended by legislation signed in December 2020. Its provisions covering e-cigarettes and vaping products took effect on March 27, 2021. For anyone buying vapor products online, the law explains several things that can seem strange at first: why parcels need an adult signature, why they carry a special label, why some carriers do not handle them and why sellers must follow tax and licensing rules. This guide explains what the PACT Act covers, how it affects shipping, signatures, labels and taxes, what it means for you as a buyer and where to find more. It is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so confirm requirements with official sources.

## What it is
The PACT Act was first passed in 2009 to address the illegal trafficking of cigarettes and to make remote sales of tobacco products subject to similar rules as sales in stores. The December 2020 amendments extended its provisions to e-cigarettes and vaping products, with a start date of March 27, 2021. The law treats vaping products similarly to cigarettes for remote sales. That includes how they are shipped, taxed and delivered.

## Shipping limits
One of the best-known effects is that the U.S. Postal Service may not carry vaping products, so sellers use other carriers. Some carriers have also limited what they accept, and rules and carrier policies can change, which can lead to interruptions in some areas. We use regional carriers that handle vapor shipments. That is part of why delivery times vary by region and why our shipping policy gives ranges. See [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/) and our [shipping policy](/shipping/).

## Adult signature
Every delivery must be signed for by an adult aged 21 or older, who must show valid government-issued photo ID. This applies in every state to every parcel containing vapor products. It is the single feature of the law that customers notice most, because it means the parcel cannot be left at the door. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) and [what 21+ age verification means](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/).

## Labeling
Parcels must carry a label stating that federal law requires payment of applicable excise taxes and compliance with licensing and tax-stamping obligations. The label is small and factual. It does not name the products inside, and it is a legal requirement for remote vape shipments. See [discreet packaging](/blog/discreet-packaging-what-to-expect/) for what your parcel looks like.

## Taxes and licensing
Sellers must register and comply with state and local licensing and tax rules. Some states tax vape products, in different ways, and sellers may collect those taxes. The law also requires sellers to report certain sales to state tax authorities in some cases. The details are complex, and they differ by state, which is why a seller may be unable to ship certain products to certain places. See [vape taxes by state](/blog/vape-taxes-by-state-overview/) and [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## What it means for you
You may see delivery rules and restrictions that did not exist for older orders. You may need to be present to sign, and you may find that some products cannot be shipped to your area. Our own summary is on the [PACT Act FAQ](/pact-act/) page, and details on shipping are in the [shipping policy](/shipping/). You are responsible for knowing the rules where you live, and for making sure that buying, receiving and using these products is lawful for you.

## What it means for sellers
A seller that ships vapor products must verify age, use adult-signature delivery, label parcels, register with the relevant authorities and comply with tax and licensing rules. A seller that does not may face serious penalties. That is why you should be cautious of any seller that offers to skip the signature or the label, or to ship without age checks. A seller that ignores these rules is ignoring the law, and your purchase may be at risk.

## Common questions about the law
### Why can't the Postal Service deliver vapes?
The law restricts the mailing of vaping products, with limited exceptions, so sellers use private carriers. Policies of some private carriers have also changed over time.

### Why do I need to show ID?
The law requires adult signature confirmation. Showing government-issued photo ID is how the delivery employee confirms that the signer is 21 or older.

### Why is there a warning label on the parcel?
The law requires parcels containing vaping products to carry a statement about excise taxes and licensing and tax-stamping obligations.

### Does the law apply to me as a buyer?
It applies mainly to sellers and carriers, but it shapes what you experience: signature, labels, delivery restrictions and availability.

### Will the rules change?
They can. Carriers, states and regulators update their rules, so check official sources and our policies for the latest.

## How this connects with our service
We follow the rules that apply to us, and we expect customers to follow theirs. That means adult signature on every parcel, compliant labels, delivery with carriers that handle vapor shipments, and cancelling orders that cannot be delivered lawfully. See [where we ship and where we do not](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/) and our [terms](/terms/).

## Not legal advice
This article summarizes publicly known features of the law in plain language. It is not legal advice, and it may not cover every detail or recent change. Rules differ by state and city, and they change. Confirm requirements with official sources, such as federal and state agencies, and ask a qualified professional about your own situation. If you have a question about how a rule affects an order with us, ask through the [contact page](/contact/).

## Related reading
Read [the FDA and vaping products](/blog/fda-and-vaping-products-what-adults-should-know/), [how ordering works](/blog/how-ordering-works/) and [how to become a wholesale customer](/blog/how-to-become-a-wholesale-customer/) if you run a shop. Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A brief timeline
The PACT Act became law in 2009 and targeted illegal cigarette trafficking. It was amended by a law signed in December 2020, which brought e-cigarettes and vaping products within its remote-sale provisions, effective March 27, 2021. After that date, carriers and sellers had to adjust: the Postal Service could no longer carry vaping products, adult signature became a requirement for deliveries of vapor products and sellers had to meet the registration, reporting and tax obligations that apply to remote sellers. Many sellers changed how they ship, and some customers noticed longer delivery times as a result of new routes and carriers.

## What this looks like from the customer's side
You place an order, and the seller ships it with a carrier that handles vapor shipments. The parcel carries the required label. When it arrives, an adult signs and shows ID. If you are not available, the carrier tries again and may return the parcel. If the seller cannot lawfully ship to your area, it cancels the order. At each step, the law is at work, even if the process feels slower than an ordinary online purchase.

## Questions to ask any online seller
- Do you require adult signature on delivery?
- Do you label parcels as the law requires?
- Do you verify age and cancel orders that cannot be delivered lawfully?
- Do you make health or regulatory claims that you cannot support?
- Do you explain your shipping, returns and compliance clearly?

A seller that answers yes to the first four and clearly to the last is likely taking the rules seriously. A seller that is vague or dismissive is a warning sign.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does the PACT Act mean I pay extra taxes?
The law requires sellers to meet tax and licensing obligations. Any tax that applies to your order is shown in your order summary before you pay. Rates and rules differ by state.

### Can a seller ignore the PACT Act?
A seller that ships vapor products must follow it. A seller that ignores it may face penalties, and a parcel from such a seller may be refused by carriers or seized. That is a good reason to buy from a seller that explains its compliance.

### Why did delivery change after 2021?
After the law took effect, sellers moved to carriers that handle vapor shipments, and routes and times changed. That is one reason delivery to some regions takes longer than it once did.

### Do I have to do anything under the PACT Act as a buyer?
You need to be 21 or older, be available to sign with ID and follow the laws where you live. You do not file anything yourself.

### Where can I read the law itself?
Official sources, such as federal agencies and government publications, publish the text and guidance. Use them if you need the exact wording for a decision.

### Why this matters when you compare sellers
Sellers that follow the PACT Act spend time and money on compliance, which can show up as longer delivery estimates, adult-signature requirements and parcel labels. Sellers that skip these steps may seem faster and simpler, but they take risks that can end up with you, such as seized parcels or cancelled orders. When you compare sellers, a clear explanation of how they ship, label and verify age is a good sign. See our [shipping policy](/shipping/) and [PACT Act FAQ](/pact-act/) for how we handle it.

faq.a: The law restricts mailing vaping products, so sellers use other carriers.

faq.a: Taxes, licensing and state rules can limit what can be shipped to some places.

faq.a: No. It is general information. Confirm requirements with official sources.

title: The FDA and Vaping Products: What Adult Buyers Should Know
summary: The FDA regulates e-cigarettes as tobacco products. Learn what marketing authorization means and why you should check product and local rules.
body:
In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration, usually called the FDA, regulates e-cigarettes and other electronic nicotine delivery systems as tobacco products. That regulation shapes which products can be sold, how they are labelled and what sellers may say about them. This guide explains in plain language what the FDA's role is, what marketing authorization means, how availability can change, what warning statements must appear, why we make no health or regulatory-endorsement claims, how our own FDA disclaimer fits in and how to stay informed. It is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live. Everything we sell is for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## The FDA's role
The FDA gained authority over e-cigarettes and other products that deliver nicotine under federal law, treating them as tobacco products. The agency sets standards for manufacturing, labelling and marketing, and it can take enforcement action against products and sellers that do not comply. It does not approve vaping products in the way that it approves medicines. When people say a product is FDA authorized, they mean that it has gone through a specific premarket review process, which is not the same as being endorsed.

## Marketing authorization
New tobacco products generally need FDA marketing authorization before they can be legally sold. The process is called premarket review, and a manufacturer submits an application showing that marketing the product would meet the legal standard. Only some vaping products have received authorization. Many products on the market have not, and enforcement actions against unauthorized products can change what retailers may sell. Whether a product has been authorized is a regulatory status, not a quality rating, and we do not claim that any product is authorized, approved or endorsed by the FDA.

## What this means for buyers
Availability can change quickly. Products you could buy last year may become restricted, and some states restrict sales to authorized products only. A product may be available in one place and not in another. That is one reason we cannot ship every product everywhere, and why we may cancel orders that cannot be delivered lawfully. Check your local rules before you order, and ask us if you are unsure. See [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/) and [where we ship and where we do not](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/).

## Warning statements
Packaging and advertising must carry the FDA nicotine warning: "WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical." The statement must be clear and prominent. You will see it on our site and on product packaging. The warning exists because nicotine is addictive, and it is a reminder that these products are for adults only. See [what the nicotine warning label means](/blog/what-the-nicotine-warning-label-means/).

## No health claims
We make no health or regulatory-endorsement claims about any product, and you should be cautious of any seller that does. Regulations restrict claims that a product carries health benefits, reduces risk or helps people stop using tobacco, unless the FDA has authorized such a claim. We do not describe any product as treating, preventing or curing any condition, and we do not suggest that any product is a substitute for medical advice. If you have questions about nicotine and your health, speak to a licensed healthcare professional.

## Why you may see "FDA" in different places
You may see the FDA mentioned in several places: on warning labels, in news about enforcement, in our disclaimer and in product pages that discuss compliance. Each has a different purpose. A warning label is a legal requirement. News about enforcement is about what the agency does. Our disclaimer explains our position. None of them implies that a particular product has been approved or endorsed.

## Our disclaimer
Our [FDA disclaimer](/fda-disclaimer/) page explains our position in detail. It states that statements on this site have not been evaluated by the FDA, that the products are for adults and that we make no health claims. If you have questions about a specific product, ask us via the [contact page](/contact/). We will tell you what we know, and we will not make claims we cannot support.

## What responsible sellers do
A responsible seller follows the law on age verification and delivery, labels products correctly, avoids unsupported health claims, complies with tax and licensing rules and is transparent about what it does and does not claim. When you evaluate a seller, look for those signs. Be wary of a seller that promises federal approval of a product, offers to skip age checks or makes medical claims.

## How to stay informed
Visit the FDA's tobacco products pages and your state's regulator for current lists and rules. News about enforcement and authorization changes regularly, and official sources are more reliable than social media. Also read [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/) and [the PACT Act explained](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/), which cover the rules for shipping and selling.

## Common questions
### Does "not evaluated by the FDA" mean the product is bad?
No. It is a standard statement that the agency has not evaluated the statements made about a product. It does not say anything positive or negative about the product itself.

### Can I check whether a product is authorized?
The FDA publishes information about authorized products on its website. Check there, and ask us if you want to know what we know about a listing.

### Why do some products disappear from sale?
Enforcement and regulatory changes can remove products from the market, and manufacturers also discontinue products. If a product you like is unavailable, check related products, and ask us.

### Do you sell authorized products only?
We make no claim that any product is authorized, approved or endorsed by the FDA. Availability depends on what manufacturers supply and what the law allows where you live.

### Does vaping carry health benefits?
We make no health claims. Nicotine is addictive, and these products are for adults aged 21 and over. If you have a health question, speak to a professional.

## Browse responsibly
Adults 21+ only. See [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) when you are ready, and read [what 21+ age verification means](/blog/what-21-plus-age-verification-means/) and our [terms](/terms/).

## A short glossary
- **Premarket review:** the FDA process for deciding whether a new tobacco product may be marketed.
- **Marketing authorization:** the result of that process when it is favorable, which allows a specific product to be sold in the United States.
- **Enforcement action:** a step the agency takes against products or sellers that do not comply, such as warning letters or seizures.
- **Warning statement:** the required nicotine warning on packaging and advertising.
- **Unauthorized product:** one that has not received marketing authorization and may be subject to enforcement.

Knowing these terms makes news about regulation easier to follow, and it helps you judge claims that a seller makes.

## How regulation can affect your choices
If a product you use is affected by enforcement, it may become harder to find. If your state restricts sales to authorized products, your options narrow. If a flavor is restricted where you live, you may need a different flavor or a different product type. These changes are decided by regulators and legislators, not by sellers, and they can happen with little notice. The best response is to stay informed, check the rules where you live and ask us what is available.

## What we will and will not say about a product
We will tell you what we know about a listing: the brand, the flavor, the strength, the size and the specifications. We will not tell you that a product is authorized, approved or endorsed by the FDA, and we will not make claims about health benefits. If you ask a question that we cannot answer, we will say so, and we will point you to official sources. That approach protects you from misleading claims, and it is how a responsible seller behaves.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does your site include a disclaimer?
Regulations restrict what sellers may say about these products, and a clear disclaimer helps you understand our position. It states that the statements on this site have not been evaluated by the FDA, that the products are for adults and that we make no health claims.

### Can I rely on product descriptions for medical decisions?
No. Descriptions explain what a product is and how it works. They are not medical advice, and they do not make health claims. Speak to a licensed healthcare professional about health questions.

### What should I do if I see a seller making health claims?
Be cautious. Claims that a product treats or prevents a condition, or carries no risk, are not supported and may not be lawful. Compare with sellers that explain products plainly and follow the rules.

### A note on language
Words matter in this area. We avoid terms such as approved, certified or endorsed when we describe products, because they suggest a level of regulatory review that we cannot claim. We describe what a product is, what it contains where the manufacturer lists it and how it is used. If you see stronger language elsewhere, check what it is based on. Plain descriptions and honest disclaimers are signs of a seller that takes the rules seriously.

faq.a: Yes. The FDA regulates e-cigarettes and other electronic nicotine delivery systems as tobacco products.

faq.q: What is marketing authorization?
faq.a: Generally, new tobacco products need FDA authorization after a premarket review before they can be legally sold. Many products on the market have not received it.

faq.q: Do you claim your products are approved by a federal agency?
faq.a: No. We make no health or regulatory-endorsement claims about any product.

faq.q: What warning must appear on packaging?
faq.a: WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical.

faq.a: Enforcement actions, regulatory changes and state rules can restrict products, and manufacturers also discontinue them.

faq.a: The FDA's tobacco products pages and your state's regulator.
