title: California Privacy Rights Explained for Our Customers
summary: California residents have rights to know, delete and limit the use of personal information. Here is a plain summary and how to use them.
body:
If you live in California, state privacy law gives you certain rights over the personal information that businesses collect about you. At One Stop Vape Store we collect only what we need to run the store, we do not sell your personal information, and we respond to requests to exercise your rights. This guide explains the rights in plain language, what personal information we collect, what we do not do, why we may need to keep some records, how to make a request, how we verify who you are, how long we take and where the details are in our policies. It is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live. Everything we sell is for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## The law in brief
The California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act, gives California residents rights over their personal information and places duties on businesses that meet certain thresholds. The rights apply to personal information that identifies, relates to or could reasonably be linked with you or your household. The law aims to give you more visibility and control over how your information is used. Our [California privacy notice](/california-privacy/) sets out how it applies to us.

## Your rights
- **Know:** ask what personal information a business collects, uses and shares, and for what purposes.
- **Access:** ask for the specific pieces of personal information a business holds about you.
- **Delete:** ask a business to delete personal information, subject to exceptions.
- **Correct:** ask for inaccurate information to be fixed.
- **Opt out:** of the sale or sharing of personal information, where a business does either.
- **Limit:** the use of sensitive personal information in certain cases.
- **Non-discrimination:** you cannot be penalized for using these rights.

## What we collect
For orders: name, email, phone, shipping address, items ordered, order notes, payment method and payment confirmation details, including any proof you upload. For enquiries: the details in your message. For site operation: technical data such as IP address and pages requested, used for security and to limit abuse, plus items stored in your browser such as your age confirmation, your cart and your wishlist. Our [privacy policy](/privacy/) and [California privacy notice](/california-privacy/) provide the full list. We do not collect precise geolocation, biometric data or the other kinds of sensitive information the law lists.

## What we do not do
We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. We use it to fulfill orders, provide support, process payments and meet legal obligations. We share it with service providers who help us run the store, such as hosting, order storage, email and delivery carriers, only as needed and under their own obligations. We do not knowingly sell or share the personal information of anyone under 16, and our products are for adults aged 21 and over.

## Why we keep some records
We may need to retain order information for tax, legal and compliance reasons even after a deletion request. For example, financial records may need to be kept for a number of years, and records connected with age-restricted sales may be needed to show that we complied with the law. When we keep something for these reasons, we tell you, and we limit how it is used. We delete or anonymize records when the reasons for keeping them end.

## How to make a request
Contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) or by email with your name, the email address used on your order and the request you are making. For access or deletion requests, mention the order or orders concerned if you can. You can also call during business hours. If you are using an authorized agent, tell us, and we will ask for your written permission. We will confirm that we have received your request.

## How we verify your identity
To protect your data, we may ask you to verify your identity before we act. In most cases we do this by matching details on the order, such as the email, name and order ID. We will not ask for more than we need. We will not ask for your passwords, PINs, private keys or recovery phrases. If we cannot verify your identity, we will explain why we cannot act on the request, and what you can do.

## How long it takes
We respond within 45 days of receiving a verifiable request. If we need more time, we can extend once by a further 45 days, and we will tell you why. Simple requests are often handled sooner. If we cannot do something, we will explain the reason.

## What you get back
For a request to know or access, we give you the categories and specific pieces of information we hold, in a readable format. For a deletion request, we delete the information we are not required to keep and tell you what we kept and why. For a correction request, we update the record and confirm. For opt-out requests, we confirm that we do not sell or share your information, and note your preference.

## Related reading
Read [why we ask for your email and phone](/blog/why-we-need-your-email-and-phone/) and [how to use the private order page](/blog/how-to-use-the-order-payment-page/). If you are curious about how long we keep things, see the privacy policy.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do I have to be a customer to make a request?
No. If you have contacted us or visited the site, you can ask what we hold. If we hold nothing identifiable, we will tell you.

### Will deleting my information cancel my order?
If an order is open, deleting the information needed to fulfil it would stop us delivering it. We will explain the effect before we act, and we may need to keep some records.

### Do you sell data to advertisers?
No. We do not sell personal information, and we do not run advertising tracking on the site.

### Can I make a request for someone else?
An authorized agent can make a request for you with your written permission, and we may confirm with you directly.

### What if I am not in California?
Other states have their own privacy laws, and our privacy policy applies to everyone. Contact us with your question and we will explain what we can do.

## Browse
Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A worked example: a deletion request
A customer in California writes to us from the email on their order, asking us to delete their personal information. We reply to confirm receipt and ask them to confirm the order ID to verify their identity. They do. We review the records: the order is complete and past the return window, so we delete the shipping address, the phone number and the uploaded payment images, keeping only the minimum order and payment record that we need for tax and accounting. We tell the customer what we deleted and what we kept and why, and we confirm that the information we kept is used only for those purposes. The whole process takes a few days, well within the 45-day limit.

## A worked example: an access request
Another customer asks what we hold about them. After verification, we send a summary of the categories, such as identifiers, order details and payment confirmation, and the specific items, such as the name, email, address and order history, along with the purposes and the service providers that process them. We also confirm that we do not sell or share the information. If the customer then wants a correction, we update the record.

## Good habits for your own privacy
Use an email address that you control, keep your devices updated, avoid sharing your private order link and be cautious of messages that ask for personal information. If you want to see or change what a business holds about you, do not hesitate to ask: the law exists to give you that right.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does the law apply to all businesses?
It applies to businesses that meet certain thresholds. We apply the same standards of care to every customer, whether or not the law strictly applies, and we respond to requests from California residents as described in our notice.

### Can I opt out of marketing?
We do not use your order information for marketing without your consent. If we ever offer news or offers, you can opt out at any time through the contact page.

### What if I think my information was misused?
Contact us with the details. We will look into it and respond. You can also contact the relevant state authority.

## Where to read the full details
Our [privacy policy](/privacy/) explains what we collect, why, who we share it with, how long we keep it and what choices you have. Our [California privacy notice](/california-privacy/) adds the categories of personal information and the rights specific to California residents. If something in this guide is unclear, those pages are the reference, and you can always contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) for help. We would rather answer a question than have you guess.

## A final reminder
Privacy rights are most useful when you use them. If you have ever wondered what a business knows about you, ask. If you spot a mistake in your details, ask for a correction. If you no longer want us to hold your information, ask for deletion. We will explain what we can do, and we will do it within the time the law allows.

faq.q: What rights do California residents have?
faq.a: To know and access what is collected, delete, correct, opt out of sale or sharing, limit use of sensitive information and not be penalized for using these rights.

faq.q: Do you sell my personal information?
faq.a: No. We do not sell it or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising.

faq.q: Why might you keep some records after a deletion request?
faq.a: For tax, legal and compliance reasons, such as financial records and records connected with age-restricted sales.

faq.q: How do I make a request?
faq.a: Contact us through the contact page or by email with your name, the email on your order and your request.

faq.q: How do you verify my identity?
faq.a: Usually by matching details on the order, such as your email, name and order ID. We never ask for passwords, PINs or recovery phrases.

faq.q: How long do you take?
faq.a: We respond within 45 days, and may extend once by a further 45 days with notice.

title: How to Spot a Counterfeit Vape: Warning Signs for Buyers
summary: Counterfeit disposables and liquids are common. Use these checks on packaging, codes, price and seller before you buy.
body:
Popular brands are widely imitated. Fake devices and liquids look convincing in photos, can sell for tempting prices and may perform poorly, leak or have unreliable battery and coil quality. For you as a buyer, the risk is not only wasted money: an imitation product may not meet the rules, may carry no proper warnings and may be built with unknown components. This guide explains the warning signs of a counterfeit, how to check packaging, how verification codes work, why required warnings matter, what to look for in weight and feel, how to judge a seller, what to do if you suspect a fake and how to reduce your risk when you shop. It is general information for adults aged 21 and over, not legal advice. Nicotine is addictive.

## Why counterfeits exist
Brands that sell well attract imitators. A convincing copy can be made cheaply and sold at a discount, or at the normal price to buyers who cannot tell the difference. Counterfeits are most common with high-demand disposables, because they are cheap to copy and sell fast. Imitation is not limited to unknown sellers: it can appear in marketplaces, on social media and sometimes in shops that do not check their supply. The best protection is knowing what to look for and buying from sellers who explain where their products come from.

## Price that is too good
A price far below the usual market range is a red flag. Compare across reputable retailers and see [how to compare vape prices](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/). A genuine product has a cost floor, and a seller cannot sell much below it for long without a reason. If a device sells for a fraction of its usual price, ask why. A discount that looks too good is often a sign of a copy, stolen stock or old stock that has expired.

## Packaging details
Look for sharp printing, correct spelling, consistent fonts and clean seals. Compare with images on the brand's official site. Poor printing, color mismatches, typos, blurry logos or glue marks suggest a fake. Check that the box closes neatly, that the plastic wrap is applied evenly and that the information on the box matches the device. Look at details such as batch numbers and dates, which should be clear and consistent. A genuine product's packaging is usually uniform from one unit to the next.

## Verification codes
Many brands include a code or QR on the package that links to a verification page. Use the brand's official domain, typed yourself, not a link from a message or an unfamiliar site, because scammers copy verification pages too. A code that does not work, that has been used many times or that leads to a page that does not look official is a concern. Some brands do not offer verification, so the absence of a code is not proof of a fake, but the presence of one that fails is a warning.

## Required warnings
U.S. packaging should carry the FDA nicotine warning: "WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical." Missing or incorrectly worded warnings are a concern. So is packaging in another language only, with no English labeling. A product that does not meet labeling rules may not have been made for the U.S. market, and it may have been imported illegally. See [what the nicotine warning label means](/blog/what-the-nicotine-warning-label-means/).

## Weight and feel
Fakes may feel lighter, because they use smaller batteries or less liquid, or heavier because of cheaper parts. They may have rough seams, loose parts, an uneven finish or buttons that feel wrong. Check for flavor or nicotine strength inconsistent with the label, a harsh or chemical taste, leaking out of the box, or a battery that dies far sooner than the specification suggests. If you have used a genuine unit of the same product, compare them. These signs are not proof on their own, but several together are a strong indication.

### Performance clues
- **Battery that drains in a fraction of the expected time.**
- **Flavor that is weak, odd or inconsistent with the label.**
- **Leaking when new,** which can mean a poor seal.
- **A device that fails or flickers** soon after first use.
- **A heat or smell that is unusual.**

If you see any of these, stop using the device and contact the seller.

## The seller
Buy from a retailer with clear contact details, published [shipping](/shipping/) and [refund](/refunds/) policies and a real business address. Look for an explanation of how it sources products, adult-signature delivery, and age checks. Avoid social-media sellers with no history, sellers that will not tell you where they are, sellers that skip age verification and sellers that offer prices that do not make sense. A seller that follows the rules for remote sales is more likely to deal in genuine products, because it has more to lose.

### What we do
We source from manufacturer and authorized distribution channels, we list products with their brand, strength and specifications, we publish our shipping and returns policies and we require adult signature on every parcel. If you have a doubt about a product you received from us, contact us with photos and your order ID, and we will look into it. See [how to contact support](/blog/how-to-contact-support/).

## What to do if you suspect a fake
Stop using it, keep the packaging and contact the seller. Take clear photos of the packaging, the label, any codes and the device. Note where and when you bought it, and keep your receipt. If the product was bought from us, email with your order ID, and we will review it. If it was bought elsewhere, contact that seller, and consider reporting a suspected counterfeit to the brand through its official channels. Learn about [disposal](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/) if the device is damaged.

## Reducing your risk
- **Buy from sellers you can identify,** with clear policies.
- **Compare prices** before you buy, and be wary of big discounts.
- **Check the packaging** against the brand's official images.
- **Use official verification pages,** typing the address yourself.
- **Keep your order records** so you can report a problem.
- **Do not use a device that looks or behaves oddly.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can a counterfeit be dangerous?
Imitations may use unknown components and may not meet the standards of the genuine product. A damaged or poorly made battery is a particular concern. Stop using a suspect device, and follow the guidance in [lithium battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

### Is every cheap product fake?
No. Sales and clearance exist. But a price far below the usual range, with no explanation, deserves a second look.

### Can I check a product myself?
Compare it with the brand's official images, check the warning and the labeling, use any official verification page and note the weight and finish. If you are unsure, ask the seller.

### What if the seller will not respond?
Keep your records, contact your payment provider if appropriate and report the product to the brand. Be more careful with that seller in future.

### Do you guarantee that products are genuine?
We make no absolute claims, but we source from manufacturer and authorized distribution channels and will review any product you doubt.

## Browse
See our [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A worked example: comparing two listings
You see the same disposable listed at two prices: $19.99 at a retailer with a business address, a clear returns policy and adult-signature delivery, and $9.99 on a social media account with no address and no policy. The cheaper listing has photos with a different font on the box. You check the brand's official site and see that the font on the box differs from the official images. You decide not to buy from the cheaper seller, because the price, the lack of information and the packaging all point the same way. A few minutes of comparison save you from a poor product and a lost payment.

## Keeping evidence
If you buy a product you later suspect is not genuine, keep the box, the device, any inserts, the receipt and the tracking information. Photograph everything from several angles, including batch numbers and codes. Evidence helps the seller investigate, helps the brand identify counterfeits and helps you if you need to dispute a payment. Do not throw the packaging away until the matter is resolved.

## Helping others
If you spot a counterfeit, tell the brand through its official channels, and warn friends who buy the same product. Counterfeit sellers rely on people not noticing or not speaking up, and every report makes their job harder. Be careful not to accuse a specific seller publicly without evidence, and stick to facts.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I tell a counterfeit from a photo alone?
Sometimes, but photos can be copied, and fakes can look identical online. Check how the seller describes the product, whether it explains its sourcing and whether its policies look real. The physical product tells you more when it arrives.

### Does a missing QR code mean a fake?
Not always. Some brands do not include codes. But a code that fails, or leads to an unfamiliar site, is a warning.

### What if I bought it from a shop in person?
The same checks apply. Reputable shops can be deceived by bad supply, so check the packaging and warnings, keep your receipt and tell the shop if something looks wrong.

faq.q: How can I tell a counterfeit vape?
faq.a: Look for prices far below the market, poor printing or typos, missing or wrong warnings, verification codes that fail, unusual weight and feel and unreliable performance.

faq.q: Should I use the QR or code on the box?
faq.a: Yes, if the brand offers one, but use the brand's official domain typed yourself, not a link from a message.

faq.q: Which warning should be on the packaging?
faq.a: The FDA nicotine warning: WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical.

faq.q: Where should I buy?
faq.a: From a retailer with clear contact details, published shipping and refund policies, a real business address and adult-signature delivery.

faq.q: What if I suspect a fake?
faq.a: Stop using it, keep the packaging and contact the seller with photos and your order details.

faq.q: Can a counterfeit be a battery risk?
faq.a: Yes. A poorly made battery is a particular concern. Stop using a suspect device.

title: How Does a Vape Work? Battery, Coil, Wick and Liquid
summary: A vape is a battery that heats a coil to turn liquid into vapor. Here is how each part works together in plain language.
body:
Every vape, from a tiny disposable to a large box mod, works on the same basic principle: a battery powers a small heater that turns liquid into an inhalable vapor. Once you understand that chain of events, everything else about vaping starts to make sense, including why different devices feel different, why some liquids suit some hardware, why a coil wears out and why a device that is not looked after can taste burnt or leak. This guide explains the four key parts, what happens in the second after you inhale, why liquid and airflow must balance, how the main types of device differ, how nicotine and flavor fit in, what goes wrong and how to look after a device. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## The four key parts
- **Battery:** stores energy and supplies power to the heater. In most devices it is a rechargeable lithium-ion cell.
- **Coil:** a small heating element, made from wire or mesh. When electric current passes through it, it heats up.
- **Wick:** usually cotton or another absorbent material that soaks up liquid and holds it against the coil.
- **E-liquid:** a mixture of propylene glycol, vegetable glycerin, flavoring and usually nicotine. It is the substance that becomes vapor.

Around those four parts sit a mouthpiece, an airflow path and some electronics that control the power. A small circuit board switches the coil on and off, and in many devices it includes protections against short circuits, overheating and low battery.

## What happens when you inhale
When you draw on the mouthpiece, an airflow sensor detects the change in pressure and sends power to the coil, or you press a button to do the same. The coil heats up in a fraction of a second. The liquid in the wick that touches the coil reaches a temperature at which it turns from liquid into vapor, which is a mixture of tiny droplets and gas. Air flows past the coil, carries the vapor through the mouthpiece and into your mouth. When you stop drawing, the sensor releases the circuit, the coil cools and the wick starts to refill with liquid from the reservoir.

That whole cycle takes a few seconds, and it repeats with every puff. The speed of each step is what makes vaping feel immediate: unlike older heating methods, a small coil can reach working temperature almost instantly, because there is very little material to heat.

### Auto-draw and button-fire
Devices fire in one of two ways. Auto-draw devices have a sensor that starts the coil when you inhale, so there is nothing to press. Button-fire devices heat the coil only while you hold a button. Auto-draw is simpler and is standard on disposables and most pods, while button-fire gives you more control and is common on box mods. See [auto-draw vs button-fire vapes](/blog/auto-draw-vs-button-fire-vapes/).

## Why liquid and airflow must balance
A vape works well only when three things stay in balance: power, liquid supply and airflow. If the wick is dry, the coil can scorch the cotton and taste burnt, because there is no liquid to carry the heat away. If there is too much liquid, it can flood the coil and gurgle or leak. If the airflow is too tight, vapor builds up and the draw feels hot. If it is too loose, the vapor is thin and the flavor weak. Each device is designed around a particular balance, which is why using the recommended liquid and power matters. See [fixing a gurgling vape](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/) and [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/).

## Device types
Disposables are sealed units that come pre-filled and pre-charged and are replaced when finished. Pods have a replaceable pod that holds liquid and often the coil, which clicks into a rechargeable battery. Box mods and tank systems use a refillable tank with replaceable coils and a larger battery with adjustable power. Each type makes different trade-offs between simplicity, control and cost. Compare them in [disposable vs pod vs box mod](/blog/disposable-vs-pod-vs-box-mod/).

### How the types differ in practice
- **Disposable:** nothing to fill or charge in many cases, a fixed flavor and a fixed lifespan.
- **Pod system:** a reusable battery with swappable pods, so you can change flavors without changing devices.
- **Tank and mod:** the most control over power, airflow and liquid, and the most maintenance.

## Nicotine and flavor
Nicotine strength and type are set by the liquid, while flavor comes from the recipe. In a disposable, both are chosen by the maker. In a refillable device, you choose them with your bottle. Nicotine salts and freebase behave differently, and the ratio of PG to VG changes how the vapor feels and how well it wicks. Learn about [PG and VG](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/) and [nicotine salts vs freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/).

## What controls how a puff feels
Several things shape the experience, and you can adjust some of them:

- **Power:** more power means more heat and more vapor.
- **Coil resistance and type:** lower resistance draws more current. Mesh coils heat more evenly.
- **Airflow:** tighter airflow feels like a cigarette draw, and open airflow feels like a larger breath.
- **Liquid:** thickness, flavor and strength.
- **How you draw:** a slow, gentle draw gives a different result from a fast one.

## Wear and tear
A coil is the part that wears out first. Over time, residue from liquid builds up on it, and flavor fades or a burnt taste appears. That is normal, and it is the reason pods and coils are sold as replaceable parts. Batteries wear too, losing capacity after many charge cycles. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/) and [lithium battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

## Common problems and what they mean
- **Weak vapor or flavor:** a worn coil, low battery, empty liquid or blocked airflow.
- **Burnt taste:** a dry wick, too much power or a worn coil.
- **Gurgling or leaking:** too much liquid in the coil chamber or a poor seal.
- **Does not fire:** a dead battery, a loose connection or a blocked sensor.

Our guides on [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/) and [troubleshooting a vape that will not charge](/blog/vape-wont-charge-fixes/) walk through fixes.

## Looking after a device
Keep it clean and dry, charge it with a suitable charger, store it upright at room temperature and replace pods and coils when flavor fades. Do not open or modify sealed devices. Dispose of finished devices at a hazardous waste or electronics recycling site; see [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is vapor the same as smoke?
No. Vapor is produced by heating liquid, not by burning plant material. This article describes how devices work and makes no comparison of health effects.

### Why do different devices feel so different?
Because power, coil, airflow and liquid all differ. A small pod and a large tank can use the same liquid and still feel very different.

### Can I use any liquid in any device?
No. Match the nicotine type and the PG/VG ratio to the hardware, as the manufacturer recommends.

### Why does a new coil taste different?
A new coil needs a few minutes to soak and a few puffs to settle. Priming it correctly avoids a harsh first taste. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).

### What is the difference between wattage and voltage?
Voltage is the electrical pressure and wattage is the power delivered to the coil. See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## Next steps
See [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) for starter hardware and the [first vape kit guide](/blog/first-vape-kit-guide/) for how to choose. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A second-by-second walkthrough of one puff
Second zero: the device is idle. The battery holds its charge, the coil is cool and the wick is saturated with liquid. Second one: you draw. Air rushes in through the intake, and the sensor notices the drop in pressure. The circuit closes, and current flows through the coil. A fraction of a second later, the coil is hot. Second two: the liquid in the wick turns into vapor, and the airflow carries it through the channel to the mouthpiece. You inhale. Second three: you stop. The sensor releases, the coil cools within moments and capillary action pulls fresh liquid from the reservoir into the wick. The device is ready for the next puff. The cycle is simple, but every part of it must work for the result to feel right.

## Why disposables, pods and tanks feel different
The same physical principle runs through all of them, but the engineering choices differ. A disposable is tuned at the factory: the coil, the airflow, the liquid and the battery are matched, and nothing can be changed. A pod device lets you swap the liquid and the pod, so you can change flavor, but the power is usually fixed. A tank and mod lets you change almost everything, including the coil, the power and the airflow, which gives control but also more ways to get it wrong. Which one suits you depends on whether you value simplicity or control.

## What a good device does well
- **Heats quickly and evenly,** so the first puff is as good as the tenth.
- **Wicks reliably,** so the coil is never starved or flooded.
- **Seals well,** so it does not leak in a pocket or a bag.
- **Manages the battery,** with protections against overheating and short circuits.
- **Is comfortable to use,** with a mouthpiece and weight that suit you.

If you are choosing hardware, those are the qualities to look for. Product pages rarely say them outright, but reviews, specifications and the maker's reputation hint at them.

## Common myths
- **"More power is always better."** Power must match the coil and the liquid. Too much burns the cotton.
- **"A bigger battery means better flavor."** Flavor comes from the coil, the liquid and the airflow, not from battery size.
- **"All liquids work in all devices."** The nicotine type and the PG/VG ratio must suit the hardware.
- **"A burnt taste means the liquid is bad."** It is usually a coil, wick or power problem.

faq.q: How does a vape work in one sentence?
faq.a: A battery powers a small coil that heats liquid held in a wick until it turns into vapor, which you inhale through the mouthpiece.

faq.q: What are the main parts?
faq.a: A battery, a coil, a wick and e-liquid, plus a mouthpiece, airflow path and a circuit that controls the power.

faq.q: What is the difference between auto-draw and button-fire?
faq.a: Auto-draw starts the coil when you inhale. Button-fire heats the coil only while you hold a button.

faq.q: Why does a vape taste burnt?
faq.a: Usually a dry wick, too much power or a worn coil.

faq.q: Why do coils wear out?
faq.a: Residue from liquid builds up on the coil over time, which dulls flavor and can cause a burnt taste.

faq.q: Can I use any e-liquid in any device?
faq.a: No. Match the nicotine type and PG/VG ratio to the hardware's recommendations.

title: Parts of a Vape: A Labeled Guide for Beginners
summary: Mouthpiece, tank, pod, coil, wick, battery and more. Learn what each component does so you can shop and troubleshoot with confidence.
body:
Shopping for vape hardware means meeting a lot of unfamiliar words: drip tip, 510 connector, atomizer, pod, airflow ring. This labeled guide walks through every part you are likely to see on a device or a product page, what it does, how it differs between device types, which parts wear out, which parts are interchangeable and how to match replacements to your exact device. It is written for beginners aged 21 and over, with plain explanations and practical tips. Nicotine is addictive.

## How to use this guide
Read it once to learn the vocabulary, then come back to it when you compare products. Each section names a part, says what it does and notes what to look for when you buy. If a word on a product page is not here, check our [vape glossary of terms](/blog/vape-glossary-terms-a-to-z/).

## Mouthpiece (drip tip)
The part you draw from. On tanks, mouthpieces are often interchangeable, and they come in different widths and materials, such as plastic, resin or metal. A narrow mouthpiece suits a tight, cigarette-style draw, and a wide one suits an open draw. On disposables and many pods, the mouthpiece is fixed. If you share devices, a replaceable mouthpiece is easier to keep clean. Keep it dry and wipe it regularly.

## Tank or pod
Holds the e-liquid. Tanks are larger and refilled through a fill port, which is usually a sliding or screw-off cover. Pods are compact cartridges that snap into the battery, either pre-filled or refillable. Pre-filled pods are replaced when empty, and refillable pods are topped up. See [what a pod vape is](/blog/what-is-a-pod-vape-and-how-to-choose/). Capacity is listed in milliliters, and a larger capacity means fewer refills but a bulkier device.

### Fill port and seal
The fill port is where you add liquid. A good seal keeps it from leaking, so check that the cover is fully closed. Overfilling is a common cause of leaks, and our guide to [filling a pod without leaks](/blog/how-to-fill-a-pod-without-leaks/) explains how to avoid it.

## Coil
The heating element, usually mesh or wire. It heats the liquid and wears out over time, so it needs replacing. In many pods, the coil is built into the pod. In tanks, it is a separate part that screws in. Coils have a resistance, measured in ohms, and a recommended power range. Learn [mesh versus standard coils](/blog/dual-mesh-vs-single-mesh-coils/) and [what a mesh coil is](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/).

## Wick
Cotton or another absorbent material inside the coil that carries liquid to the heating surface. You do not see it, but its condition decides how well the device works. A wick that is dry or burnt gives a harsh taste, and a wick that is flooded gives gurgling and leaks. Priming a new coil lets the wick soak properly. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).

## Battery
Powers the heater. Capacity is measured in mAh, and in many devices the battery is built in and recharged through a port. In box mods, it may be one or two removable cells. Larger capacity usually means longer life between charges, but power use also matters. See [mAh, puffs and battery life](/blog/mah-puffs-and-battery-life-how-they-relate/) and [lithium battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

## Airflow control
A ring or slider that adjusts air intake. Open airflow gives a looser, cooler draw and more vapor. Tight airflow gives a restricted draw that suits mouth-to-lung inhaling. Not every device has it. See [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).

## 510 connector
A standard threaded connection, named for its thread pattern, that lets many tanks fit many mods. It is the reason you can pair a tank from one brand with a mod from another. Pods and disposables do not use it. If you buy a tank for a mod, check that both use a 510 thread, and that the tank's recommended power matches the mod.

## Charging port
Modern devices use USB-C. Older devices use micro-USB or proprietary connectors. USB-C is reversible and common, so cables are easy to find. A charging port can collect lint and residue, so keep it clean and dry. See [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/).

## Fire button and sensor
Devices fire on inhale (auto-draw) or when you press a button. The sensor that detects your draw is a small component near the airflow path. If it gets blocked by liquid, the device may stop firing. See [auto-draw vs button-fire](/blog/auto-draw-vs-button-fire-vapes/).

## Display and indicator lights
Some devices have a screen that shows battery, power or liquid levels, and others have a light that changes color or blinks to signal status. See [understanding vape device indicator lights](/blog/understanding-vape-device-indicator-lights/) and [screen vs no-screen disposables](/blog/screen-vs-no-screen-disposable-vapes/).

## Other parts you may see
- **O-rings and seals:** rubber rings that keep the tank sealed.
- **Base and deck:** the bottom of a tank, where the coil sits.
- **Glass or tube:** the clear section of a tank that shows the liquid level.
- **Chimney or center tube:** the channel that carries vapor to the mouthpiece.
- **Lanyard or case:** accessories for carrying.

## Which parts wear out
- **Coils and pods:** wear first, and are replaced regularly.
- **O-rings:** harden over time and may need replacing if a tank leaks.
- **Mouthpieces:** can crack or stain.
- **Batteries:** lose capacity after many cycles.

See [how to pick replacement coils and pods](/blog/how-to-pick-replacement-coils-and-pods/).

## Matching replacements to your device
Replacement parts must match your exact device. Check the product name and model, the thread type for tanks, the coil resistance and the recommended power. Pods and coils are not interchangeable between brands or often between models. If you are unsure, ask us with your device name. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Which part should I replace first when flavor fades?
The coil or pod. It is the most common cause, and replacing it is the simplest fix.

### Can I use a different brand's pod?
Usually not. Pods are designed for a specific device, and a mismatch can leak or not fit.

### What does 510 mean?
It is the name of a standard thread size that lets tanks and mods from different makers connect.

### How do I clean the parts?
Wipe the outside with a dry cloth. Rinse refillable tanks with warm water, dry them fully and reassemble. Do not wet the battery or the electronics. See [how to clean a vape device](/blog/how-to-clean-a-vape-device/).

## Shopping
Match replacement parts to your exact device. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Putting the parts together: three example devices
### A disposable
A disposable has a body, a built-in battery, a pre-filled liquid reservoir, a coil with a wick, an airflow sensor, a mouthpiece and often a USB-C port. You cannot separate the parts, and you do not need to. The parts you can affect are the charging and the way you use it. When the liquid or the battery is finished, you replace the whole thing.

### A pod system
A pod system has a battery section with a sensor and a port, and a pod that clicks into it. The pod contains the liquid, the wick and often the coil. When the pod is empty or the coil wears out, you replace the pod. The battery stays. If the pod is refillable, you can add liquid through a fill port until the coil wears out.

### A tank and mod
A tank and mod has a mod with one or two batteries, a screen and buttons, and a tank that screws onto the 510 connector. The tank has a mouthpiece, a glass section, a fill port, an airflow ring and a replaceable coil. You can change the coil, the mouthpiece, the glass and sometimes the airflow. This type has the most parts, and the most to look after.

## A quick buying checklist by part
- **Mouthpiece:** comfortable, and easy to keep clean.
- **Tank or pod:** a capacity that suits your use, and a seal that does not leak.
- **Coil:** the right resistance and type for your style, and replacements that are easy to find.
- **Battery:** a capacity and charging port that suit you, with a reputable maker.
- **Airflow:** adjustable if you want to tune the draw.
- **Connector:** standard if you want to mix and match.
- **Display:** useful if you want to see battery and power at a glance.

## Cleaning and care by part
Wipe mouthpieces regularly. Rinse refillable tanks and glass sections with warm water, and let them dry fully before use. Never wet the battery or the electronics. Check O-rings for wear, and replace them if they harden or crack. Replace coils and pods when flavor fades. Check the charging port for lint, and clear it gently with a dry tool if needed. A few minutes of care keeps parts working for longer.

## Where parts come from
Parts are made by the device maker or by third parties. Original parts fit best and follow the maker's specifications. Third-party parts can be a good value but vary in quality, so choose carefully. For sealed devices, there are no user-serviceable parts, and the whole device is replaced.

### Frequently asked questions about parts
**Can I swap the mouthpiece on a pod?** Usually not, because it is built into the pod. On a tank, many mouthpieces can be swapped if they use the same standard fitting.

**Why does my tank leak around the base?** Often an O-ring has worn, the coil is loose or the tank is overfilled. Check each in turn.

faq.q: What is a drip tip?
faq.a: The mouthpiece you draw from. On tanks it is often interchangeable, and on disposables it is fixed.

faq.q: What is a 510 connector?
faq.a: A standard threaded connection that lets many tanks fit many mods.

faq.q: What wears out first?
faq.a: The coil or pod, followed by O-rings, mouthpieces and eventually the battery.

faq.q: What does the coil do?
faq.a: It is the heating element that turns liquid into vapor. It wears out over time and needs replacing.

faq.q: What is the wick?
faq.a: Cotton inside the coil that carries liquid to the heating surface.

faq.q: How do I match replacement parts?
faq.a: Check the exact product name and model, thread type, coil resistance and recommended power, because parts are not interchangeable between brands.

title: Vape Glossary: Common Terms Every Shopper Should Know
summary: Understand the jargon on product pages, from MTL and DTL to mAh, ohm, shortfill and nic salts, all in one quick reference.
body:
Product pages and reviews use a great deal of shorthand, and it can feel like a different language when you first start shopping. This glossary groups the terms you will meet most often into device terms, electrical terms, style terms, liquid terms, experience terms and shopping terms, with a plain explanation of each and links to our fuller guides. It is written for adults aged 21 and over, and it describes how products work without making any health claims. Nicotine is addictive.

## How to use this glossary
Skim the sections that match what you are shopping for, and come back when a term on a product page is unfamiliar. Terms are grouped by topic so that related ideas sit together. Where a term has a full guide, we link to it.

## Device terms
- **Disposable:** a pre-filled, ready-to-use device that is replaced when finished. See [how to choose one](/blog/how-to-choose-a-disposable-vape/).
- **Pod:** a compact, replaceable liquid cartridge that clicks into a battery.
- **Pod system:** a device that uses pods, usually small and simple.
- **Mod:** a battery unit, often with adjustable power. Short for modification, from the days when users modified devices.
- **Box mod:** a mod in a rectangular body, often with removable batteries.
- **Tank:** a refillable container with a coil that screws onto a mod.
- **Atomizer:** the part that heats and vaporizes liquid, often used to mean the coil and its housing.
- **Starter kit:** a bundle that includes a device and what you need to start.
- **Open system:** a device that you refill yourself.
- **Closed system:** a device with pre-filled, sealed pods or cartridges.

## Electrical terms
- **mAh:** battery capacity, in milliamp hours. See [mAh, puffs and battery life](/blog/mah-puffs-and-battery-life-how-they-relate/).
- **Ohm (Ω):** coil resistance. Lower resistance draws more current.
- **Watt (W):** power delivered to the coil.
- **Volt (V):** electrical pressure.
- **Amp (A):** current. A battery's amp rating shows how much current it can supply.
- **USB-C:** a common charging connector.
- **Pass-through:** the ability to use a device while it charges.

See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/) for how they relate.

## Coil terms
- **Mesh coil:** a coil made from a thin metal sheet that lines the wick. See [what is a mesh coil](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/).
- **Wire coil:** a coil made from wound wire.
- **Dual coil:** a design with two coils for more vapor.
- **Priming:** soaking a new coil with liquid before use. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).
- **Wicking:** the way liquid travels through the cotton to the coil.

## Style terms
- **MTL:** mouth-to-lung inhale, a tight draw into the mouth before inhaling.
- **DTL / sub-ohm:** direct-to-lung inhale with a low-resistance coil, usually with open airflow. See [the difference](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/).
- **Auto-draw:** a device that fires when you inhale.
- **Button-fire:** a device that fires when you press a button.
- **Boost mode:** a setting that increases power for a stronger draw.

## Liquid terms
- **E-liquid or vape juice:** the liquid that becomes vapor.
- **PG / VG:** propylene glycol and vegetable glycerin, the liquid base. See [PG and VG](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).
- **Nic salts:** a smoother type of nicotine for low-power devices. See [nicotine salts vs freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/).
- **Freebase:** the traditional form of nicotine.
- **Shortfill:** a bottle with spare room for nicotine shots.
- **Nic shot:** a bottle of concentrated nicotine for mixing.
- **Steeping:** letting liquid rest so flavors blend. See [what is steeping](/blog/what-is-steeping-and-does-it-matter/).
- **Strength:** the nicotine concentration, in mg/mL or percent. See the [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/).

## Experience terms
- **Throat hit:** the sensation of vapor on the throat. See [throat hit explained](/blog/throat-hit-explained/).
- **Ghosting:** a lingering flavor from a previous liquid.
- **Dry hit:** a harsh, burnt draw from a dry wick. See [dry hits explained](/blog/dry-hits-explained/).
- **Spitback:** hot droplets that reach your mouth.
- **Gurgling:** a bubbling sound caused by excess liquid.
- **Cloud chasing:** vaping for the largest vapor volume. See [cloud chasing vs flavor chasing](/blog/cloud-chasing-vs-flavor-chasing/).
- **Flavor chasing:** vaping for the fullest flavor.

## Shopping terms
- **Puffs:** the estimated number of draws a disposable provides; see [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/).
- **Bundle:** a pack of several items sold together.
- **Pack size:** how many units come in a listing, such as single or 5-pack.
- **SKU:** a product's unique code.
- **Nixodine:** a newer nicotine alternative used in some devices. See [what is Nixodine](/blog/what-is-nixodine/).
- **Nicotine pouch:** a small tobacco-free pouch placed between lip and gum. See [nicotine pouches beginner's guide](/blog/nicotine-pouches-beginners-guide/).

## Compliance terms
- **PACT Act:** a federal law covering remote sales of vapor products. See [the PACT Act explained](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/).
- **Adult signature:** delivery that requires a 21+ signature with ID. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/).
- **RMA:** a return authorization form used in our returns process.

## Abbreviations at a glance
MTL: mouth to lung. DTL: direct to lung. PG: propylene glycol. VG: vegetable glycerin. mAh: milliamp hours. W: watts. V: volts. Ω: ohms. USB-C: Universal Serial Bus type C. FDA: Food and Drug Administration. PACT: Prevent All Cigarette Trafficking.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do I need to know all these terms?
No. Learn the few that matter for the device you are buying, and use the rest as a reference.

### Why are there so many words for the same thing?
The vaping community developed its own vocabulary over time, and different brands use different names. Where terms overlap, this guide notes it.

### Where do I find the strength on a product?
On the product page and the packaging, as mg/mL or a percentage. See [how to read a vape product page](/blog/how-to-read-a-vape-product-page/).

## Shop
Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Terms you will see on product pages, explained with examples
### "50K puffs, 5% nicotine, USB-C, mesh coil"
This tells you that the manufacturer estimates about 50,000 puffs, that the liquid contains 50 mg/mL of nicotine (5%), that the battery charges through a USB-C port and that the coil is made of mesh. Together, these describe a large, rechargeable disposable with a modern coil.

### "30 mL, 50/50, 35 mg salt"
This describes a 30-milliliter bottle of e-liquid with equal parts PG and VG and a nicotine-salt strength of 35 mg/mL. It suits a low-power pod.

### "100 mL shortfill, 70VG/30PG, 0 mg"
This is a 100-milliliter bottle with higher VG and no nicotine, usually sold with room to add nicotine shots in some markets. It suits a sub-ohm tank.

### "Kit, 1.2 ohm pod, 18 W, 1000 mAh"
This describes a starter kit with a 1.2 ohm pod, a power of 18 watts and a battery of 1,000 mAh. It suits mouth-to-lung inhaling.

## Words that mean different things in different places
Some terms are used loosely. "Mod" can mean any battery unit or a box device. "Atomizer" can mean the coil or the whole tank. "Cartridge" can mean a pre-filled pod or a replaceable coil head. "Juice" and "e-liquid" mean the same thing. If a term is unclear, check the product description, and ask us if you are unsure.

## Terms from the shop and the law
- **Age gate:** the confirmation that you are 21 or older when you enter a site.
- **Adult signature:** a delivery requirement. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/).
- **Warning statement:** the required nicotine warning. See [what the nicotine warning label means](/blog/what-the-nicotine-warning-label-means/).
- **Batch code:** a code printed on packaging that identifies a production run.
- **Counterfeit:** a fake product that imitates a brand. See [how to spot counterfeit vapes](/blog/how-to-spot-counterfeit-vapes/).

## Terms about use and care
- **Priming:** soaking a new coil before use.
- **Chain vaping:** taking puffs in quick succession, which can dry the wick.
- **Charge cycle:** one full discharge and recharge of a battery.
- **Pass-through:** using a device while it charges.
- **Leak:** liquid escaping from the tank or pod.

## Terms you can ignore for now
If you use a disposable, you can skip most electrical and coil terms. If you use a pod, learn pod, coil and strength. If you use a tank and mod, learn ohms, watts, airflow and PG/VG. Start with the words that match your device, and add more as you need them.

## Quick pronunciation and spelling notes
Ohm is written with the symbol Ω. Mod is short for modification. MTL and DTL are usually said as letters. Nic salts is pronounced as written. Sub-ohm is said "sub-ohm". These small points help when you read reviews and talk to other users.

## Tips for reading unfamiliar listings
Read the specifications first, because they are the least ambiguous part of a listing. Compare the same details across products, such as strength, volume, puffs and battery. Be cautious of listings that use many technical terms but give few concrete numbers. If you cannot tell what a product is, ask us before you buy.

## Terms about money and value
- **Cost per puff:** price divided by puffs, used to compare disposables. See [how to compare vape prices per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/).
- **Cost per milliliter:** price divided by volume, used to compare bottles.
- **Bulk or wholesale:** buying larger quantities at lower unit prices. See [bulk buying tips](/blog/bulk-buying-vapes-save-money/).
- **Restocking fee:** a charge on some refunds that covers handling returned items.

## Terms about nicotine pouches
- **Pouch strength:** nicotine per pouch, in milligrams. See [nicotine pouch strengths explained](/blog/nicotine-pouch-strengths-explained/).
- **Slim, mini and regular:** pouch sizes.
- **Can:** the container, which usually holds around 15 to 20 pouches.

## Terms about devices you may meet less often
- **Rebuildable:** devices where you build your own coils. They need more skill.
- **Squonk mod:** a mod that feeds liquid from a bottle in the body. It is a niche device.
- **Pen style:** a slim device shaped like a pen.
- **Cartridge:** a pre-filled liquid container, used in some closed systems.

faq.q: What does MTL mean?
faq.a: Mouth to lung, an inhale style where you draw into your mouth first and then inhale, usually with a tight airflow and a higher-resistance coil.

faq.q: What is a sub-ohm coil?
faq.a: A coil with resistance below one ohm, used with open airflow for direct-to-lung inhaling.

faq.q: What are nic salts?
faq.a: A smoother type of nicotine used in low-power devices such as pods and disposables.

faq.q: What is a dry hit?
faq.a: A harsh, burnt draw caused by a dry wick.

faq.q: What does mAh mean?
faq.a: Milliamp hours, a measure of battery capacity.

faq.q: What is ghosting?
faq.a: A lingering flavor from a previous liquid.

title: mAh, Puffs and Battery Life: How They Relate
summary: A bigger battery does not always mean more puffs. See how mAh, power mode and coil design combine to decide how long a vape lasts.
body:
Battery capacity, measured in milliamp hours, or mAh, is the number that product pages put in bold, and it is easy to assume that a bigger number always means a longer-lasting device. It is one factor, but it is not the whole story. How long a vape runs depends on how much energy the battery holds, how much energy each puff uses, how efficiently the device uses power and how you use it. This guide explains what mAh tells you, why power use matters, how puff counts relate to batteries, what real-world factors change battery life, how to read product pages, with a worked example you can follow, and how to look after a battery. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive.

## What mAh tells you
mAh measures how much charge a battery holds. A 1,000 mAh battery holds twice the charge of a 500 mAh one, all else equal. It is like the size of a fuel tank. A bigger tank can go further, but how far depends on how thirsty the engine is. Capacity is usually quoted at the battery's nominal voltage, which for most lithium-ion cells is 3.7 volts.

## From mAh to energy
To compare batteries properly, it helps to turn mAh into watt-hours, which is a measure of energy. Multiply the capacity in amp hours by the voltage. A 1,000 mAh battery is 1 amp hour. At 3.7 volts, that is 3.7 watt-hours. A 500 mAh battery is 1.85 watt-hours. A 2,000 mAh battery is 7.4 watt-hours. Energy is what is actually spent when you puff.

## Power use matters
A device that runs at low power uses less energy per puff than a high-wattage one. Boost modes drain the battery faster. So a smaller battery on an efficient device can last as long as a bigger one on a power-hungry device. Energy per puff is power multiplied by time, so a 10-watt device taking a 2-second puff uses 20 joules, and a 25-watt device taking the same puff uses 50 joules, two and a half times as much.

### A worked example
Take a 1,000 mAh battery at 3.7 volts, which holds 3.7 watt-hours, or about 13,300 joules. At 10 watts for a 2-second puff, each puff uses about 20 joules, so the battery could in theory supply about 660 puffs. At 25 watts for a 3-second puff, each puff uses 75 joules, so you would get about 177 puffs. The same battery gives very different results, which shows why mAh alone does not predict battery life. Real results are lower, because of conversion losses and the battery not being fully drained, but the comparison holds.

## Puff counts and batteries
Puff counts on disposables are set mostly by liquid volume, with the battery sized to match. A larger liquid reservoir needs a larger battery to vaporize it all, so high puff counts and large batteries go together. See [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/). Rechargeable models can add extra puffs by charging, which is why many large devices have USB-C ports. For a non-rechargeable device, the battery is sized to last about as long as the liquid, and whichever runs out first ends the device.

## Real-world factors
- **Draw length and frequency:** longer, more frequent draws use more energy.
- **Temperature:** batteries lose capacity when cold, and very high heat shortens their life.
- **Age:** capacity falls after many charge cycles. A battery that is a year old can hold noticeably less than when new.
- **Coil resistance:** lower resistance coils draw more current at the same voltage.
- **Power setting:** higher wattage uses more energy per second.
- **Standby drain:** some devices use a small amount of power when idle.

## Why bigger is not always better
A larger battery adds weight and size, takes longer to charge and may not suit a small device. Some small, efficient devices are designed around a modest battery and give long life. A large battery in a device that uses lots of power may still run out quickly. The sensible comparison is between devices of the same type and power level.

## Reading product pages
Look for mAh and for any mention of USB-C charging or pass-through. Check whether the battery is rechargeable and how long charging takes. If puff counts are listed, compare them with the battery size, because a very high puff count with a very small battery is a sign to read carefully. Our [rechargeable versus non-rechargeable article](/blog/rechargeable-vs-non-rechargeable-disposables/) shows what to check.

## Charging time
Charging time depends on the battery size and the charger. A rough guide is that a small battery charges in under an hour, and a large one in one to two hours. Using a reputable charger and a standard cable helps. See [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/).

## Looking after it
Care extends life. Avoid heat and cold, charge before the battery is fully empty when you can, unplug when full and do not leave a device charging unattended. See [battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/) and [extending battery life](/blog/how-to-extend-vape-battery-life/). A battery that is looked after can serve for many months.

## Signs of a wearing battery
- It drains faster than it used to.
- It takes longer to charge, or does not reach full.
- It feels warm when idle.
- The device shuts off with charge remaining.

If you see these signs, retire the device, and dispose of it properly.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does a higher mAh mean more puffs?
Generally more energy, but puff counts depend on liquid and power too. Compare devices of the same type.

### Can I replace the battery in a disposable?
No. Disposable batteries are sealed. Do not try to open the device.

### Why does my device run out faster in winter?
Cold reduces battery capacity temporarily. Keep the device warm in an inside pocket, and let it warm to room temperature before charging.

### Is it a problem to charge a half-empty battery?
No. Partial top-ups are fine, and often better for a battery than running it to empty.

### What does pass-through mean?
It means that the device can be used while charging. It is convenient, but using a device while it charges makes it warmer, so do it sparingly.

## Shop
Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Comparing two devices with numbers
Device A is a pod kit with a 500 mAh battery, a 1.0 ohm coil and a fixed 12 watts. Device B is a pod kit with a 1,000 mAh battery, a 0.6 ohm coil and a fixed 25 watts. Device A holds 1.85 watt-hours, about 6,660 joules, and uses about 24 joules for a 2-second puff, so in theory it supplies about 277 puffs. Device B holds 3.7 watt-hours, about 13,320 joules, and uses about 50 joules for a 2-second puff, so it supplies about 266 puffs. The second battery is twice the size, but because the device uses more than twice the power, it gives about the same number of puffs. The size of the battery alone would have misled you.

## What to look for when you shop
- **mAh and watts together,** not either on its own.
- **Whether the battery can be recharged,** and how.
- **Reviews of real-world battery life** from users with a similar style.
- **Charging speed,** especially for large batteries.
- **Battery protections,** such as overheating and short-circuit protection.

## Charging habits that help
Charge when you notice the battery getting low, instead of letting it hit zero. Use a reputable charger. Unplug when full. Avoid charging in heat or direct sun. If you will not use a device for a while, store it partly charged. These habits slow the natural loss of capacity and keep the battery in good shape.

## What changes as a battery ages
A new battery delivers its full rated capacity. After a few hundred charge cycles, it may hold 80 percent or less. You will notice shorter life between charges, and possibly slower charging. That is normal, and it is the reason batteries are consumables. When a device no longer lasts as long as you need, it is time to replace it, and to dispose of the old one responsibly. See [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

## How disposables hide the maths
In a disposable, the maker matches battery, coil and liquid, so that the puff count is a reasonable estimate. You do not have to do any calculation. The numbers matter when you compare devices: a 50,000-puff device needs far more energy than a 5,000-puff device, and the battery and liquid are sized accordingly. If you see a very high puff count with a very small battery listed, read carefully, and compare it with similar devices.

### Frequently asked questions about batteries and puffs
**Why does a device with a screen drain faster?** The screen and electronics use a small amount of power, so devices with displays can run through a battery a little faster.

**Does a bigger battery take longer to charge?** Yes, usually, unless the charger and device support faster charging. Allow more time for larger batteries.

**Can I use a power bank to charge?** Yes, with a standard cable, as long as the power bank is reputable and the device accepts it. Avoid leaving it charging unattended.

faq.q: What does mAh mean?
faq.a: Milliamp hours, a measure of how much charge a battery holds. Higher means a larger charge, all else equal.

faq.q: Does more mAh always mean longer battery life?
faq.a: No. Power use matters as much. A device at higher wattage uses more energy per puff.

faq.q: How can I compare batteries properly?
faq.a: Convert mAh to watt-hours by multiplying amp hours by the voltage, about 3.7 volts for most lithium-ion cells.

faq.q: How do puff counts relate to batteries?
faq.a: Puff counts are set mostly by liquid volume, with the battery sized to match. Rechargeable models can add extra puffs by charging.

faq.q: Why does cold weather shorten battery life?
faq.a: Batteries lose capacity when cold. The effect is temporary and reverses as the battery warms.

faq.q: How can I make a battery last?
faq.a: Avoid heat and cold, charge before it is fully empty when you can, unplug when full and use a suitable charger.

title: What Is a Mesh Coil, and Why Do So Many Vapes Use One?
summary: Mesh coils use a thin metal sheet instead of a wire wrap. Learn how that changes heating, flavor and why it became popular.
body:
If you have shopped for vapes recently, you have seen "mesh coil" on almost every listing, often with words like dual mesh, triple mesh or full mesh. It is one of the most common selling points in modern devices, and it is worth understanding what it actually is, how it differs from the older wire coils and what it does for flavor and vapor. This guide explains the change from wire to mesh, why mesh heats differently, what users notice, how mesh coils are used in disposables and pods, what the drawbacks are, how to look after them and how to replace them. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## From wire to mesh
Traditional coils wrap a thin wire around a cotton wick, like a spring around a rope. The wire heats when current passes through it, and the liquid in the cotton touching the wire turns to vapor. A mesh coil replaces the wire with a thin sheet of woven or perforated metal that lines the wick, often rolled into a cylinder or laid flat against the cotton. Because the sheet is full of tiny holes or a fine weave, liquid can pass through it easily, and it touches a large area of cotton.

## Why it heats differently
A mesh sheet has a large surface area touching the cotton. That means liquid is heated across a wide area rather than in a few hot spots. The result is quicker heating and more even vaporization. A wire coil concentrates its heat in a thin line, so the liquid right next to it can get very hot while liquid further away stays cooler. Mesh spreads the heat, which tends to give a more uniform result from puff to puff.

### The surface area idea
Imagine heating a pan of water with a thin hot wire versus with a wide hot plate. The plate heats the water more evenly and faster. A mesh coil is closer to the plate. That is why the same power can feel different, and why mesh coils often work well at modest power, which suits small devices.

## What users notice
- **Smoother, fuller flavor,** because more of the liquid is vaporized at a consistent temperature.
- **Consistent vapor from puff to puff,** with fewer weak or harsh puffs.
- **Less chance of local scorching,** because heat is spread out.
- **Quick response,** with little delay between inhaling and vapor.
- **Often a longer period of good flavor,** though results vary.

These are general tendencies. The quality of the design, the liquid and the power all matter as well.

## Coils in disposables
Most modern disposables use mesh coils to deliver consistent flavor for thousands of puffs. Because a disposable has a fixed liquid and a fixed coil, consistency over its whole life is important, and mesh helps. Dual-mesh designs use two mesh sections, and some use an extra heating zone, aiming at more vapor and more even heating. See [mesh versus standard coils](/blog/dual-mesh-vs-single-mesh-coils/) for the differences.

## Coils in pods and tanks
Pods and tanks use mesh too, especially in sub-ohm tanks where a wide mesh surface supports high power. Mesh coils come in different resistances: lower resistances suit direct-to-lung tanks with open airflow, and higher ones suit mouth-to-lung pods. The coil's rating tells you the power range it works best in. See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## Drawbacks
Mesh coils can cost more to make and can be affected by thick or sweet liquids, which leave residue in the fine holes. Residue can reduce flavor over time, which is why coils eventually wear out. Using the recommended liquid and power helps, and a very high power on a small mesh can burn the cotton. Mesh coils also need to be primed properly so that the cotton is fully saturated, otherwise the first puffs can taste burnt.

## Mesh versus wire: a quick comparison
- **Heating:** mesh is more even, wire is more concentrated.
- **Flavor:** mesh is often smoother, wire can taste sharper.
- **Cost:** mesh is often more expensive to make.
- **Lifespan:** both wear out, and results vary with liquid and use.
- **Use:** mesh is common in modern pods and disposables, wire is common in rebuildable and older designs.

## How to look after a mesh coil
- **Prime it:** add a few drops of liquid and let it soak for a few minutes before use. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).
- **Use the right power:** stay within the recommended range.
- **Take gentle puffs:** avoid chain use that dries the wick.
- **Use suitable liquid:** a liquid that is too thick or too sweet can clog the mesh. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).
- **Replace it when flavor fades:** do not push a worn coil.

## Signs a mesh coil is worn
A muted or flat taste, a burnt taste even with fresh liquid, weaker vapor and a darker or crusty appearance on the coil. If you see these, replace it. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/) and [picking replacements](/blog/how-to-pick-replacement-coils-and-pods/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does mesh make a device more powerful?
Not by itself. It spreads the heat, which changes how the vapor feels and tastes. Power comes from the battery and the settings.

### Is dual mesh better than single mesh?
Dual mesh can offer more vapor and even heating, but it is a design choice. The best coil is the one that suits your device and your style.

### Can I clean a mesh coil?
In most cases, no. They are not designed to be cleaned, and the fine holes are easy to damage. Replace them.

### Are mesh coils in all disposables?
Many, but not all. Check the product page for the coil type.

### Why does my mesh coil taste burnt?
It may be unprimed, dry, worn or run at too high a power. Prime a new coil, check the liquid level and lower the power.

## Replacing mesh coils
Mesh coils still wear out. Match the replacement to your device and the recommended power. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A closer look at how a mesh coil is made
A mesh coil starts with a thin sheet of metal, such as stainless steel or a nickel alloy, that has been woven or etched with a pattern of tiny holes. The sheet is cut, shaped and rolled or folded, then attached to electrical contacts and wrapped around or laid against a wick, usually cotton. The fine structure gives it a high surface area for its size. In a disposable, the mesh and wick are sealed inside the device with the liquid. In a pod or tank, they are in a replaceable head.

## Why surface area matters for flavor
Flavor depends on how completely and evenly liquid is vaporized. If part of the liquid is overheated, some flavor compounds break down and taste harsh. If part is underheated, it does not vaporize and the flavor is flat. A coil that spreads heat evenly keeps more of the liquid in the right temperature range, which is why mesh often tastes smoother and fuller. It is not magic, but it is a real advantage of the design.

## Dual mesh and other variations
Manufacturers market many variations: dual mesh, triple mesh, quad mesh, full mesh and so on. In general, more mesh surface or more heating zones mean even heating and more vapor, at the cost of more power use. A well-designed single mesh can still outperform a poorly designed multi-mesh. Use the descriptions as a guide, not a guarantee, and read reviews of real performance.

## Choosing a device with a mesh coil
- **Check the resistance and the recommended power,** and make sure they suit your style.
- **Look at the liquid it is designed for,** usually salts for low-power pods.
- **Consider how long the coil should last,** and how easy replacements are.
- **Look at the overall device,** because a good coil in a poorly sealed pod still leaks.

## How to get the most from a mesh coil
Prime it properly, take steady puffs without chaining, and keep the power in range. Let the wick refill between puffs, especially with thick liquid. Store the device upright so liquid does not pool. And replace the coil when flavor drops, instead of pushing on with a worn one. Treating a mesh coil gently extends the time it tastes its best.

### Frequently asked questions about mesh
**Will a mesh coil make my liquid last longer?** Not necessarily. Efficient vaporization can use liquid at a steady rate, and the amount you use depends mainly on how you puff and at what power.

**Is mesh quieter?** Mesh coils can crackle less than some wire builds, but sound depends on the whole design.

**Does mesh work with every liquid?** It works with most, but very thick or very sweet liquids can clog it faster, so use the liquid the maker recommends.

### Mesh coils and your buying decision
When two devices look similar, the coil type can break the tie. If you value consistent flavor over the life of a device, mesh is a sensible choice. If you like to build or tinker, wire coils offer more variety. If you simply want something that works, choose a device with a reputable mesh design and follow its instructions. Either way, remember that the coil is only part of the system, and the liquid and power matter as much.

faq.q: What is a mesh coil?
faq.a: A coil that uses a thin sheet of woven or perforated metal lining the wick, instead of a wire wrapped around it.

faq.q: Why do mesh coils heat differently?
faq.a: The sheet has a large surface area touching the cotton, so liquid is heated across a wide area and more evenly.

faq.q: What do users notice?
faq.a: Smoother, fuller flavor, consistent vapor from puff to puff and less chance of local scorching.

faq.q: What are the drawbacks?
faq.a: They can cost more to make and can be affected by thick or sweet liquids that leave residue.

faq.q: Can I clean a mesh coil?
faq.a: Usually not. They are not designed to be cleaned, so replace them when flavor fades.

faq.q: How do I prime a mesh coil?
faq.a: Add a few drops of liquid and let it soak for a few minutes before the first puff.
