title: Ohms, Watts and Volts in Vaping: A Beginner's Explanation
summary: Resistance, power and voltage control how a coil performs. This guide explains them without the math headache.
body:
You do not need an engineering degree to vape, but a little electrical knowledge helps you choose hardware, set it up sensibly and understand what product pages mean. Ohms, watts and volts are the three words you will meet most often, and they describe how electricity behaves in your device. This guide explains each one in plain language, how they relate through two simple formulas, worked examples with real numbers, typical ranges for different styles, how to set up and adjust power, what goes wrong when settings are off and how to use the right battery. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and this is general information, not a manual for any specific device. Always follow the manufacturer's instructions.

## Ohms: resistance
Ohms, written with the Greek letter omega (Ω), measure how much a coil resists the flow of current. Low-resistance coils draw more current and heat faster. High-resistance coils heat more gently. Think of a water pipe: a wide pipe lets a lot of water through and a narrow one restricts it. Resistance is the narrowness of the pipe. A coil's resistance is printed on the coil or the pod, for example 0.6 Ω or 1.2 Ω.

## Volts: electrical pressure
Volts (V) describe the electrical pressure that pushes current through the coil. A fully charged lithium-ion battery is about 4.2 volts and a discharged one about 3.0, with 3.7 volts as the nominal value. Some devices let you set voltage directly, but many convert it for you to deliver a chosen wattage. Think of volts as the water pressure in the pipe.

## Watts: power
Watts (W) measure the power the device sends to the coil. More watts means more heat, more vapor and faster liquid use. Every coil has a recommended wattage range, and staying within it protects both flavor and lifespan. Too low and the vapor is weak and cool. Too high and the liquid can scorch and the coil can burn out. Think of watts as how much water per second comes out of the pipe, which is the useful work.

## How they relate
Two formulas tie them together. Power in watts equals voltage squared divided by resistance in ohms (P = V² / R). And current in amps equals voltage divided by resistance (I = V / R). In practice, you pick a coil with a resistance suited to your style and set the wattage within its range, and the device works out the voltage it needs.

### Worked examples
- **3.7 V across a 0.5 Ω coil:** power is 3.7 × 3.7 / 0.5 = 27.4 W, and current is 3.7 / 0.5 = 7.4 A. That is a lot of current, so the battery must be able to supply it.
- **3.7 V across a 1.0 Ω coil:** power is 13.7 W, and current is 3.7 A.
- **3.7 V across a 1.5 Ω coil:** power is about 9.1 W, and current is about 2.5 A.
- **To get 15 W from a 0.8 Ω coil:** voltage needed is the square root of (15 × 0.8), which is the square root of 12, about 3.46 V.

You do not have to do these sums, because the device does them, but they show why a low-resistance coil needs a battery that can supply high current, and why higher resistance coils suit smaller batteries.

## Typical ranges
- **MTL coils:** about 1 ohm or higher, at lower wattage, commonly 8 to 20 watts. They give a tighter draw, and suit nicotine salts and pods.
- **Sub-ohm coils:** below 1 ohm, at higher wattage, commonly 20 to 80 watts or more. They give a more open draw and a lot of vapor, and suit low-strength freebase liquids.

See [sub-ohm versus mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/) for how the two styles compare.

## Start low
Begin at the lower end of the recommended range and increase gradually. If the vapor tastes harsh or burnt, lower the power. If it feels cool or weak, raise it in small steps, such as a watt or two at a time. Most coils list a range, such as 15 to 25 watts, and the best setting is often near the middle for a new coil. A new coil also needs priming before you vape. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).

## Why the wrong settings cause problems
- **Too much power for the coil:** the liquid scorches, the cotton burns and the coil wears quickly. You get a burnt taste.
- **Too little power:** the coil does not heat enough, so vapor is thin and the liquid may pool, causing gurgling.
- **Liquid too thick for the power:** the coil dries out because it cannot wick fast enough.
- **Liquid too thin for the power:** the coil floods and leaks.

See [dry hits explained](/blog/dry-hits-explained/) and [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/).

## Battery and current
A low-resistance coil at high power draws a lot of current, so the battery must be rated to supply it. Batteries have a continuous discharge rating, in amps, and using a battery with too low a rating for your setup can make it overheat. That is why removable batteries must be matched to the device and bought from reputable sources. See [lithium battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/). If you use a sealed device or a pod, the maker has already matched battery and coil, and you do not need to calculate anything.

## Common mistakes
- **Ignoring the coil's recommended range.**
- **Setting power by the highest number the device allows.**
- **Using a coil with the wrong resistance for your style.**
- **Mixing battery types or ages in a multi-battery device.**
- **Assuming that more watts is always better.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do I need to know this for a disposable?
No. A disposable has everything matched by the maker. This knowledge matters for refillable and adjustable devices.

### What is a smart or temperature-control device?
Some devices adjust power automatically or limit temperature. They still depend on the same electrical relationships, and you should follow the manufacturer's instructions.

### Why do pods not show watts?
Many pods run at a fixed output chosen by the maker, so there is nothing to set.

### Can I use any coil in any tank?
No. Coils fit specific tanks and have specific ranges. Match the model.

### Why does my device show a different resistance from the coil?
Small differences come from measurement and the connection. A large difference can mean a poor connection or a damaged coil.

## Shop
Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A step-by-step setup example
You have a tank with a 0.4 ohm mesh coil rated for 40 to 70 watts, and a mod that lets you set watts. Start at 45 watts, near the low end. Prime the coil by adding liquid, letting it soak for several minutes and taking a few gentle puffs at a lower power, such as 30 watts. Then set 45 watts, and take a few puffs. If the vapor feels cool or thin, raise the power by 2 or 3 watts and try again. If it tastes harsh, lower it. After a few adjustments, you will find a setting that suits your taste, usually well within the range. Write it down, or use the device's memory, so you can return to it.

## Safety margins for batteries
Removable cells have a continuous discharge rating. For a 0.4 ohm coil at 3.7 volts, current is about 9.25 amps, so a battery rated at 15 amps or more gives a comfortable margin. A battery rated at 8 amps would be pushed beyond its limit. Using a battery with too low a rating is one of the most common causes of problems in advanced devices. If you are not sure, choose a higher rating, from a reputable source, and follow the manufacturer's guidance.

## Understanding the numbers on a coil
A coil may be printed with something like "0.4 Ω, 40 to 70 W". The first number is the resistance. The second is the recommended power range. Some coils also state the type, such as mesh, and the maker's suggested liquid. These details tell you how it is meant to be used. A coil used outside its range wears quickly or performs badly.

## Keeping the electrical side simple
If you find all of this daunting, choose a pod device or a disposable, where the maker has set everything. You can enjoy vaping without ever thinking about ohms. If you later move to an adjustable device, the ideas here will make the transition easier, and the formulas will help you check that a setup makes sense.

## A quick reference table in words
A 0.3 ohm coil usually works around 50 to 100 watts and suits a large tank with open airflow. A 0.6 ohm coil often runs around 25 to 50 watts. A 1.0 ohm coil often runs around 12 to 25 watts and suits a tighter draw. A 1.5 ohm or higher coil often runs around 8 to 15 watts and suits pods. These are rough, and the coil's own rating is what counts, but they show how resistance and power go together.

faq.q: What are ohms?
faq.a: A measure of a coil's resistance. Low-resistance coils draw more current and heat faster.

faq.q: What are watts?
faq.a: A measure of the power sent to the coil. More watts means more heat, more vapor and faster liquid use.

faq.q: What are volts?
faq.a: The electrical pressure that pushes current through the coil. A lithium-ion cell is about 3.7 volts nominal.

faq.q: How do they relate?
faq.a: Power equals voltage squared divided by resistance, and current equals voltage divided by resistance.

faq.q: Where should I set the power?
faq.a: Start at the lower end of the coil's recommended range and increase gradually.

faq.q: Why do I need the right battery?
faq.a: Low-resistance coils at high power draw a lot of current, so the battery must be rated to supply it.

title: What Is in E-Liquid? PG, VG, Flavoring and Nicotine Explained
summary: E-liquid has four main components. Learn what each one does, what to look for on a label and what is meant by food-grade flavoring.
body:
E-liquid is a short list of ingredients, but the details differ between brands, and many people are curious about what they are actually inhaling. This guide explains the main ingredients in plain language: propylene glycol, vegetable glycerin, flavoring and nicotine, plus the optional extras you may see, how to read a label, how ingredients affect the experience, what we can and cannot say about them, how to store liquid and what to do if you think an ingredient does not suit you. It is general information for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive. We make no health claims about any ingredient, and nothing here is medical advice.

## The basic recipe
Most e-liquids contain four things: a base made of propylene glycol and vegetable glycerin, flavoring, and nicotine in most cases. The proportions vary between products, and the base is usually the largest part by volume. The ratio of the two base liquids is printed on many labels, and it affects how the liquid wicks, how the vapor feels and which hardware it suits.

## Propylene glycol (PG)
A thin, odorless liquid that carries flavor and gives throat feel. It is used widely in food and personal care products, which is one reason it is common in e-liquid. In e-liquid, it is thin and wicks quickly, so it suits small coils and pods. Higher-PG liquids tend to taste crisp and give more throat hit. We make no claims about how it affects your body. If you are sensitive to it, stop using the product and speak to a healthcare professional.

## Vegetable glycerin (VG)
A thicker, slightly sweet liquid made from plant oils, which produces denser vapor. Because it is thick, it wicks slowly and needs coils with large wicking channels. Higher-VG liquids give a smoother feel and bigger clouds, and they suit sub-ohm tanks. See [PG and VG ratios explained](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## Flavoring
Flavor concentrates give each liquid its character: fruit, dessert, mint, tobacco and many others. Brands often describe them as food-grade, meaning they are commonly used in foods. Being edible is not the same as being suitable to inhale, and we make no health claims about flavorings. The formulas are the maker's own, and brands do not always list every component. If a flavor does not agree with you, try a different one or a different brand. See [vape flavor profiles explained](/blog/vape-flavor-profiles-explained/).

### Sweeteners and cooling agents
Some liquids add sweeteners to round out a flavor, and cooling agents to produce a fresh, icy sensation without changing the taste. These are used in small amounts. Cooling agents are why "ice" versions of flavors feel different. See [how cooling ice flavors work](/blog/how-cooling-ice-flavors-work/). Sweeteners can leave residue on coils, which shortens their life.

## Nicotine
Present in most liquids, as freebase or nicotine salts, in a stated strength. Nicotine is addictive. Strength is shown in milligrams per milliliter or as a percentage. Freebase is the traditional form, used at lower strengths. Salts are smoother at higher strengths and common in pods and disposables. See the [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/) and [nicotine salts vs freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/). Zero-nicotine liquids exist for adults who want flavor without nicotine.

## Optional extras
Some liquids add water to thin them, or other components for specific effects. Not all are listed in detail, so check the brand's information. We list what the manufacturer provides on the product page. If you want to know more about a specific product, ask us, and we will tell you what we know.

## Reading the label
Look for ratios, strength, volume and the warning statement. The label should also show the manufacturer's details and, in many cases, a batch or date code. Our guide to [reading an e-liquid label](/blog/how-to-read-an-e-liquid-label/) walks through each element. A label that is missing key information, or that has no nicotine warning, is a concern. See [what the nicotine warning label means](/blog/what-the-nicotine-warning-label-means/).

## How ingredients affect the experience
- **More PG:** crisper flavor, more throat hit, thinner vapor.
- **More VG:** smoother feel, denser vapor, slower wicking.
- **Higher nicotine:** stronger sensation, and a need to match the device.
- **Flavor and sweeteners:** taste, and how quickly a coil wears.
- **Cooling agents:** a fresh sensation.

## What we can and cannot say
We can tell you what a product is, what the manufacturer lists and how it is used. We cannot tell you that any ingredient is good or bad for your body, because we make no health claims, and regulators restrict them. If you have a health question, speak to a licensed healthcare professional. See [the FDA and vaping products](/blog/fda-and-vaping-products-what-adults-should-know/).

## Storage
Keep liquid cool, dark and away from children and pets; see [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/) and [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/). Heat and light degrade flavor and darken the liquid. Keep caps tight. Check the date, and use older bottles first. See also [e-liquid shelf life and expiry](/blog/e-liquid-shelf-life-and-expiry/).

## Allergies and sensitivities
If you suspect a reaction to an ingredient, stop using the product and talk to a healthcare professional. Some people notice irritation, a dry mouth or a cough with certain bases or flavors. It is a good idea to change one thing at a time, such as the flavor or the ratio, so that you can tell what causes it.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Are all e-liquids made the same way?
The basic approach is similar, but recipes, ratios and quality differ. Reading the label and buying from a reputable seller helps.

### Why do some liquids list more than the four ingredients?
Because flavor systems can be complex, and some products add extras. The label shows what the maker lists.

### What does "food-grade" mean?
It refers to ingredients commonly used in food. It does not mean the product is suitable for inhalation or free of risk, and we make no such claim.

### Why is my liquid darker than before?
Nicotine liquid darkens over time with air and light. A little color change is usual. See [what is steeping](/blog/what-is-steeping-and-does-it-matter/).

### Can I mix liquids?
It changes ratio, strength and flavor in ways that are hard to predict. It is simpler to buy the product you want.

## Shop
Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## How to compare two liquids using the label
Imagine two bottles of 30 milliliters. Bottle A lists 50/50 PG/VG, 35 mg/mL nicotine salt and a fruit flavor. Bottle B lists 70/30 VG/PG, 3 mg/mL freebase nicotine and a dessert flavor. From the label alone you can tell that A suits a low-power pod with a high-strength salt, while B suits a sub-ohm tank with a low-strength freebase. The ratios and strengths point to different hardware. If you used A in a sub-ohm tank, the vapor would be harsh, and if you used B in a small pod, it would be too thick to wick. Reading the label tells you where each belongs.

## Why ingredient lists are short
Labels list the main components and the nicotine, but flavor formulas are often proprietary, and makers do not always list every component. The rules on labeling differ by place. If you want more detail, ask the brand or the seller, and be aware that you may get a general answer. We share what the manufacturer provides on the product page.

## Questions to ask before you buy a new liquid
- What is the PG/VG ratio, and does it suit my device?
- What is the nicotine type and strength?
- What is the bottle size, and will I use it before it ages?
- Does the label show the nicotine warning and the maker's details?
- Is the seller clear about where the product comes from?

If the answers are all clear, you can buy with confidence. If any is missing, ask first.

## When ingredients change
Brands sometimes change recipes, and a liquid you like may taste different after a change. If that happens, tell the seller, because it may be a new batch. Keep the bottle's batch code. If you are very particular about a flavor, buy what you need within a reasonable window, not a huge stock, because liquids age.

### Frequently asked questions about ingredients
**Why do some liquids contain water?** A small amount of water thins the liquid slightly, which can help wicking in some recipes.

**Does a clear liquid differ from a colored one?** Some liquids are clear and some are tinted, depending on the flavoring and age. Color is not a reliable guide to quality.

**Can I check ingredients myself?** You can read the label and the maker's information. Detailed testing is a matter for manufacturers and regulators, not something we can do for you.

**What if I want a liquid without a certain ingredient?** Tell us what you want to avoid, and we will tell you what the maker lists. If the information is not available, we will say so.

### Choosing liquids with ingredients in mind
If you know that you prefer a crisper feel, look for balanced or PG-leaning ratios. If you want smoother vapor and bigger clouds, look for higher VG, with hardware that suits it. If you want to avoid nicotine, choose a zero-strength liquid. If you are new to a brand, start with one bottle, judge it over several days and then decide whether to buy more. Taking a measured approach lets you learn what suits you without wasting liquid.

faq.a: It is thin, carries flavor and gives throat feel. It wicks quickly, so it suits small coils and pods.

faq.a: It is thicker and slightly sweet, producing denser vapor. It suits sub-ohm tanks with large coils.

faq.a: No. We describe what manufacturers list and how products are used. We make no health claims.

faq.a: On the label and product page. Look for ratios, strength, volume and the nicotine warning.

faq.q: What if I think I react to an ingredient?
faq.a: Stop using the product and talk to a healthcare professional.

title: What Is Steeping, and Does It Matter for E-Liquid?
summary: Steeping lets flavors blend over days or weeks. Learn when it helps, when it does not and how to do it properly.
body:
Steeping is the practice of letting e-liquid rest, usually in a cool, dark place, so that flavors blend and mellow. It is a term borrowed from tea and wine, and it comes up often in vaping forums and reviews, usually with strong opinions. This guide explains why people steep, what actually changes in a bottle over time, which kinds of liquid benefit most, whether commercial liquids need it, how to steep properly, what to avoid, what a color change means and how to tell when a liquid is simply old. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## What steeping means
Steeping is storing a freshly mixed liquid for a period, often days or weeks, before using it. During that time, the ingredients settle together. The idea is that the flavors, which are made of many components, spread evenly through the base, and that the nicotine and flavor mellow. People also use the word for the simple act of letting a new bottle rest for a few days, with the cap loosened briefly to let air out, which is also called breathing.

## Why people steep
Fresh mixed liquid can taste sharp or uneven. Over time, flavor molecules disperse and the nicotine mellows, which can make the liquid taste rounder. Some flavors, especially complex or creamy ones, change noticeably as they rest. Others hardly change. People who mix their own liquid steep because the effect is most obvious on a bottle that was mixed only hours before. If you buy bottled liquid, the maker usually did this for you.

## What actually changes
Several things happen as a bottle rests:

- **Mixing:** flavor concentrates, which are thick, disperse evenly through the base.
- **Oxidation:** a small amount of air in the bottle slowly reacts with the contents, which can mellow harshness and also darken the liquid.
- **Settling:** tiny air bubbles escape, and the mixture becomes uniform.
- **Flavor development:** some flavor compounds change slowly, which is why certain recipes taste different after a week or two.

The size of these effects depends on the recipe, the temperature and the storage.

## Which liquids benefit
- **Dessert and custard recipes** often improve with a week or two, because creamy flavors take time to blend.
- **Tobacco flavors** often benefit from longer, sometimes several weeks.
- **Complex blends** with many components can change noticeably.
- **Fruit and menthol** recipes usually taste good fresh and need less.
- **Simple single-flavor liquids** rarely change much.

## Do commercial liquids need it
Most commercial liquids are ready to use, and many brands steep before bottling. A few extra days rarely hurts, but it is not required. If you buy a bottle and the first taste seems a little sharp, giving it a few days with the cap closed and the bottle in a cool, dark place may help. If it tastes right, just use it. There is no need to wait weeks for a product that is sold as ready to use.

## How to steep
1. Cap the bottle tightly.
2. Shake it, then open the cap briefly to release air. This is called breathing.
3. Store it in a cool, dark place away from direct sunlight.
4. Shake occasionally and wait several days.
5. Taste a small amount in your device and decide whether it has improved.

### The speed-up methods
Some people use warm water baths or gentle shaking to speed up the process. These can have mixed results, and heat can darken and degrade a liquid. If you try them, be careful: never use a flame or a microwave, and do not overheat. For most people, time is the simplest way.

## What to avoid
Do not store liquid in a hot car or on a windowsill, and do not leave caps loose. Heat and light can darken liquid and change flavor. Keep bottles upright and capped, away from children and pets. See [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/) and [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/).

## Dark color is normal
Nicotine liquid darkens with time and oxygen. A little color change is usual and is often cited as a sign of steeping. A liquid that goes very dark, smells odd or tastes harsh may be past its best. See [e-liquid shelf life and expiry](/blog/e-liquid-shelf-life-and-expiry/).

## Steeping versus aging
Steeping is the short period in which a new liquid settles. Aging is what happens over months and years, when flavors can fade and the liquid can degrade. A bottle that sits for a long time will eventually decline. Use older bottles first, and check dates where they are printed.

## A worked example
You buy a creamy dessert liquid, and the first taste is a little sharp. You cap the bottle, shake it, open the cap for a moment to release air and put it in a cupboard away from light. After five days you try it again. The sharpness has softened, and the creamy notes are fuller. You decide to leave it for a week next time you buy something similar. By comparison, you buy a fresh fruit and ice liquid and it tastes good from the first puff, so you use it straight away.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Does steeping change nicotine strength?
Not meaningfully. The strength stays the same, though the sensation can seem smoother as flavors blend.

### Can I steep a liquid in a tank?
It is better to steep in the bottle. Liquid in a tank is exposed to air and heat and should be used soon.

### How long should I steep?
There is no fixed answer. A few days is common for ready-made liquids, and weeks for some recipes. Taste and decide.

### Does steeping matter for nicotine salts?
Salts and freebase can both change with time, but many salt liquids are designed to be used as bought.

### Is steeping a myth?
Not entirely, but it is often overstated. The effect is real for some recipes and small for others.

## Shop
Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/), or read about [bottle sizes](/blog/e-liquid-bottle-sizes-30ml-60ml-100ml/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Steeping in practice: a simple routine
If you like to steep, build a small routine. When a new bottle arrives, write the date on it. Cap it, shake it and open the cap briefly. Put it in a drawer or a box away from light and heat. Check it after a few days, and try a small amount. Keep notes about which flavors improved and which did not, so that next time you know what to expect. Rotating bottles by date means you always have one ready to use, while the next rests.

## Why some people say steeping makes no difference
Many commercial liquids are made in large batches and rested at the factory, so by the time you buy them they have already had the time they need. Some recipes also change little with time. And tastes differ: a difference one person notices, another does not. If you cannot tell the difference, there is no need to steep. If you can, and you enjoy the result, it is a pleasant habit.

## Steeping and nicotine salts
Nicotine salts are made by combining nicotine with an acid, and some recipes benefit from a few days of rest after mixing. For bottled salts, the maker has handled this. A few days of rest in a cool, dark place does no harm, and may smooth a very sharp first taste. See [nicotine salts vs freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/).

## What not to expect
Steeping will not rescue a liquid that is stale, badly made or past its best. It will not change the nicotine strength. It will not make a flavor you dislike taste good. It is a small refinement, not a transformation. Use it where it helps, and skip it where it does not.

## Signs a liquid has gone past its best
A very dark color, a sour or harsh smell, a flat or off taste or separation in the bottle can mean that a liquid is old or has been stored badly. If you see these signs, do not use it. Dispose of it responsibly, as explained in [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). Fresh storage habits prevent most of these problems.

### Related reading and shopping
If you are choosing liquids to try, read [vape flavor profiles explained](/blog/vape-flavor-profiles-explained/) and [how to read an e-liquid label](/blog/how-to-read-an-e-liquid-label/). Buy bottle sizes you will finish in a reasonable time, so that you are not left with old liquid. See [e-liquid bottle sizes](/blog/e-liquid-bottle-sizes-30ml-60ml-100ml/). When you are ready, browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and our guide on [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/) so that the bottles you buy keep their flavor.

### Frequently asked questions about timing
**Should I steep a refill bottle that arrived in cold weather?** Let it come to room temperature first. Cold liquid is thick and may taste different until it warms.

**Can I steep a liquid in the fridge?** It is not needed. A cool, dark cupboard is enough, and fridge storage can make liquid thick.

**Does a darker bottle mean a better steep?** Not necessarily. Color shows age and oxygen, not quality. Judge by taste.

faq.q: What is steeping?
faq.a: Letting e-liquid rest, usually in a cool, dark place, so flavors blend and mellow.

faq.q: Which liquids benefit most?
faq.a: Dessert and custard recipes and tobacco flavors often improve with time. Fruit and menthol recipes usually taste good fresh.

faq.q: Do commercial liquids need steeping?
faq.a: Most are ready to use, and many brands steep before bottling. A few extra days rarely hurts, but it is not required.

faq.q: How do I steep a bottle?
faq.a: Cap it tightly, shake it, open the cap briefly to release air, store it in a cool, dark place and wait several days.

faq.q: Why does liquid darken?
faq.a: Nicotine liquid darkens with time and oxygen. A little color change is usual.

faq.q: What should I avoid?
faq.a: Heat, direct sunlight and loose caps. Do not store liquid in a hot car or on a windowsill.

title: What Is Throat Hit, and What Affects It?
summary: Throat hit is the sensation vapor creates in your throat. See what increases or softens it, from nicotine type to PG ratio and temperature.
body:
Throat hit is the feeling of vapor at the back of the throat when you inhale. It is a major part of why people choose certain liquids and devices.

## What creates it
- **Nicotine strength:** higher strength gives a stronger sensation.
- **Nicotine type:** freebase feels sharper; salts feel smoother. See [salts versus freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/).
- **PG content:** high-PG liquids feel crisper than high-VG ones.
- **Temperature:** hotter vapor feels harsher.
- **Airflow:** tighter airflow concentrates the sensation.

## Cooling agents
Menthol-type cooling can add a sensation distinct from nicotine throat hit. Read about [ice flavors](/blog/ice-vape-flavors-guide/).

## How to soften it
- Lower the strength.
- Choose a higher-VG liquid.
- Open the airflow or lower the wattage.
- Try nicotine salts if you want a smooth feel at higher strength.

## How to increase it
Choose a higher PG ratio, tighter airflow or a slightly higher strength, within what is comfortable. Nicotine is addictive, and increasing intake is not advisable for everyone.

## Everyone is different
There is no right level. Experiment sensibly and stop if you feel unwell.

## Related
See [PG and VG](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/) and [adjustable airflow](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/). Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Is stronger throat hit better?
faq.a: It is a preference, not a measure of quality.

faq.q: Why do salts feel smooth at high strength?
faq.a: The acid in the salt changes how nicotine is delivered, which softens the sensation.

title: How Cooling 'Ice' Flavors Work (and Who Likes Them)
summary: Ice versions add a chill to fruit and candy flavors. Learn what creates the sensation, how strong it can be and how to pick the right level.
body:
Many flavor names include "ice", "freeze" or "chill". These versions add a cooling sensation to the original flavor.

## What creates the cooling
Cooling comes from compounds that trigger the cold-sensing receptors in your mouth and throat, similar to the effect of mint. They do not change the temperature of the vapor; they change how it feels.

## Levels of cooling
Some recipes add a light cool finish, while others are a strong, icy blast. Names like "extra ice" usually signal more.

## Why people like it
Cooling can brighten fruit flavors and make sweeter profiles feel fresher. Some find it also softens the heat of vapor.

## Who may prefer no ice
If you are sensitive to menthol or find cooling harsh, choose a non-ice version. Our [ice flavors guide](/blog/ice-vape-flavors-guide/) lists options.

## How to compare
Try the same flavor with and without ice to learn your preference. Rotating can also keep flavors interesting; see [best disposables for flavor lovers](/blog/best-disposable-vapes-for-flavor-lovers/).

## Impact on hardware
Cooling agents can leave residue on coils over time. Keep to the recommended power and replace parts on schedule; see [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/).

## Shop
Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Does ice mean menthol?
faq.a: Often it means a menthol-type cooling agent, though recipes vary.

faq.q: Can I get a cooling flavor without mint?
faq.a: Yes. Many fruit-and-ice flavors use cooling without a strong mint taste.

title: A Short History of Vaping: From Early Patents to Pod Systems
summary: Electronic cigarettes have evolved over decades, from early patents to cig-a-likes, tanks, box mods and today's pods and disposables.
body:
Modern vaping has a surprisingly long backstory. Here is a short timeline of how devices developed.

## Early ideas
Patents for smokeless electronic devices appeared in the 1960s, but the concept did not reach consumers at the time.

## The first commercial e-cigarette
In 2003, a Chinese pharmacist named Hon Lik designed a modern electronic cigarette that used an ultrasonic atomizer. Commercial products reached the market in the mid-2000s and spread to Europe and the United States.

## Cig-a-likes
First-generation devices looked like cigarettes and used small batteries and cartomizers. They were simple but limited in battery life and vapor.

## Tanks and box mods
Around 2010, refillable tanks and larger battery devices let users customize power, airflow and flavor. Sub-ohm vaping emerged, producing larger vapor clouds.

## The pod era
Compact, easy pod systems appeared in the mid-2010s, using nicotine salts to deliver smoother, stronger hits from low-power hardware.

## Disposables
Pre-filled disposables grew in popularity because they need no setup. Recent models include mesh coils, rechargeable batteries and screens. See [how to choose a disposable](/blog/how-to-choose-a-disposable-vape/).

## Regulation
Governments have steadily regulated vaping, from age limits to the [PACT Act](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/) and FDA oversight. See [FDA and vaping products](/blog/fda-and-vaping-products-what-adults-should-know/).

## Today
Hardware is more compact and easier than ever. Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) to see current options. Adults 21+ only; nicotine is addictive.

faq.q: Who invented the modern e-cigarette?
faq.a: Hon Lik, a Chinese pharmacist, designed a modern electronic cigarette in 2003.

faq.q: Why did pods become popular?
faq.a: They are small, simple and work well with nicotine salts.

title: Vapes, Pouches and Other Nicotine Products: How They Differ
summary: A neutral comparison of how vapes and nicotine pouches work, what each requires and what adults should consider before using them.
body:
Nicotine products come in several forms. This overview describes how they differ in use, without health claims or recommendations.

## Vapes
A vape heats liquid to create vapor that you inhale. They need a charged battery, and refillable ones need liquid and coils. See [how a vape works](/blog/how-does-a-vape-work/).

## Nicotine pouches
Pouches are small tobacco-free pouches placed between the lip and gum. Nicotine is absorbed in the mouth, and there is no vapor, device or charging. See [pouches for beginners](/blog/nicotine-pouches-beginners-guide/).

## Practical differences
- **Equipment:** vapes need hardware; pouches need none.
- **Discretion:** pouches produce no vapor.
- **Cost:** vary by brand and use.
- **Rules:** laws for vaping and pouches differ by place.

## What they have in common
All contain nicotine, which is addictive, and are for adults 21 and over. None come without risks, and we make no health claims.

## Choosing
Think about where you will use it, how much effort you want to spend and local rules. Many adults try one form and stay with it.

## Browse
See [nicotine pouches](/shop/nic-pouches/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). Read [state and local vape laws](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## Not medical advice
If you want advice on nicotine use, consult a healthcare professional. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Do pouches contain tobacco?
faq.a: Modern pouches are described as tobacco-free, though they contain nicotine.

faq.q: Which one is right for me?
faq.a: That depends on your preferences and local rules. Neither comes without risk.

title: What Is a Box Mod? Features, Benefits and Who Needs One
summary: Box mods are larger, adjustable devices for experienced users. Learn what they offer over pods and what to know before buying one.
body:
A box mod is a battery-powered device that holds one or more batteries and powers a separate tank. They are the larger, more adjustable end of vape hardware.

## What makes them different
Box mods offer adjustable wattage, temperature or voltage settings, bigger batteries and compatibility with many tanks via a 510 thread. Many include a screen and menu.

## Benefits
- **Power range:** support for sub-ohm tanks and big vapor.
- **Battery life:** larger cells last longer.
- **Customization:** swap tanks and coils to suit your taste.

## Drawbacks
- **Size and weight:** bulkier than pods.
- **Complexity:** more settings and more to learn.
- **Safety considerations:** removable batteries need correct handling. See [battery care](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

## Who should consider one
Experienced adult vapers who want to tune their device and use high-power tanks. Beginners are usually better served by pods; see [disposable vs pod vs box mod](/blog/disposable-vs-pod-vs-box-mod/).

## Coils and liquid
Pair a box mod with a sub-ohm tank and a lower-strength, higher-VG liquid. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/) and [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## Shop
Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). Adults 21+ only; nicotine is addictive.

faq.q: Do box mods need special batteries?
faq.a: Many use removable 18650 or 21700 cells. Use cells rated for the device and never mix them.

faq.q: Can a beginner use a box mod?
faq.a: Possible, but a simpler pod kit is usually easier to start with.

title: E-Liquid Shelf Life: How Long Does It Last?
summary: Unopened e-liquid usually lasts a year or two when stored well. See what shortens shelf life and how to tell when liquid has gone off.
body:
E-liquid does not last forever, but with good storage it stays usable for a long time.

## Typical shelf life
Most bottles carry a best-by date about one to two years after manufacture. Unopened liquid stored properly generally stays fine until then.

## What shortens it
- **Heat:** warm places accelerate chemical changes.
- **Light:** sunlight darkens liquid and degrades flavor.
- **Air:** every opening introduces oxygen. Keep caps tight.
- **Contamination:** dirty tips or fingers.

## Signs of aging
Liquid darkens, flavor weakens, or it smells or tastes off. Darkening alone is usual with nicotine, but a sour or flat taste means it is past its best.

## Nicotine and flavor
Nicotine slowly oxidizes, which changes color. Flavors, especially delicate fruits, can fade over time.

## How to extend life
Store in a cool, dark place, such as a drawer. Keep it upright, and tighten the cap after use. See [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/).

## Buying in bulk
Only buy more than you will use before the date. See [bottle sizes](/blog/e-liquid-bottle-sizes-30ml-60ml-100ml/).

## What to do with old liquid
Dispose of expired or off-tasting liquid responsibly; see [disposal guidance](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

## Shop
Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). Adults 21+ only.

faq.a: Not always. Nicotine liquids darken over time, but check the smell and taste as well.

summary: Some adults want big vapor, others want the best taste. Compare the hardware and settings for each style.

This guide explains what clouds tastes like in vapes, how it is usually blended, where to find it, which brands make it and how to choose the right product, using the live catalog so the numbers match the shop.

## What clouds tastes like in a vape
Vapers tend to favor either large vapor clouds or concentrated flavor. The hardware and settings differ for each. Most flavors are blended with a supporting note: a cooling finish for freshness, a sweet fruit for balance or a creamy base for body. Flavor is personal, so treat any description as a guide: the same recipe can taste sweeter, sharper or fuller depending on the device, how you draw and what you vaped before.

If you are choosing clouds for the first time, try one product from a brand you already trust before stocking up, and compare two or three variations (plain, iced and blended) so you learn which style you prefer. Our [vape flavor profiles guide](/blog/vape-flavor-profiles-explained/) explains how the main flavor families work, and [best disposable vapes for flavor lovers](/blog/best-disposable-vapes-for-flavor-lovers/) is a good next read.

Reading the product names in our catalog, clouds is most often combined with berry, cooling and ice, orchard and stone fruit, citrus and tropical notes:

- **Berry:** 31 products. Berry flavors balance sweetness and tartness. Blue raspberry, strawberry and mixed-berry blends are among the most reliable crowd-pleasers in vaping.

Pairings like these are how makers keep a familiar flavor interesting: the second note changes the sweetness, acidity or finish without hiding the main flavor. clouds also appears with a cooling finish, which is covered in [how cooling ice flavors work](/blog/how-cooling-ice-flavors-work/).

title: Vape Indicator Lights: What Blinking and Color Changes Mean
summary: LED lights tell you about charge, faults and activation. Learn the common patterns and what to do when a vape blinks at you.
body:
Many devices use an LED instead of a screen. Patterns differ between makers, so check your manual, but several signals are common.

## Charging
A light while plugged in usually shows charging, changing color or turning off when full. On many devices a red light means charging and green or off means done.

## Low battery
Blinking when you inhale often means the battery is low. Charge the device if it is rechargeable. Non-rechargeable devices that blink at the end of life are done.

## Fault or protection mode
Rapid blinking can mean a short circuit, overheating or a coil problem. Stop using it and let it cool. If it continues, it may need replacement. See [how to fix a vape that will not charge](/blog/vape-wont-charge-fixes/).

## Activation
A light that flashes when you draw is normal, indicating it is firing. A fast blink on press may be a lock or cut-off.

## Modes
Devices with power modes use colors to show the mode. Check the product description.

## When the light does nothing
No light and no vapor could mean a flat battery or an empty device. See [why my vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/).

## Know your device
Keep the packaging or product page. Compare options in [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) that note light and screen features. Adults 21+ only.

faq.q: Why does my vape blink when I inhale?
faq.a: It can mean low battery, a fault or a protection feature. Check your manual.

faq.q: Is a charging light always red?
faq.a: No. Colors vary by manufacturer.

title: Auto-Draw vs Button-Fire: Which Activation Style Is Better?
summary: Some vapes fire when you inhale, others when you press a button. Compare control, convenience and typical use for each style.
body:
The way a device turns on affects how it feels and what it suits.

## Auto-draw (inhale-activated)
A sensor detects airflow and fires the coil as you draw. It is simple and intuitive. Almost all disposables and many pod systems work this way. Downsides: accidental activation if you squeeze the device, and less control over timing.

## Button-fire
You press a button to activate the coil before or while inhaling. It gives you control over when the coil heats and prevents accidental firing. Box mods and many pod kits offer it. The downside is an extra action with each puff.

## Some devices do both
A few pod kits support both modes, letting you choose.

## Which suits you
- **Simplicity:** auto-draw.
- **Control:** button-fire.
- **Travel:** button-fire, if it has a lock, reduces accidental firing in a bag.

## Considerations
Auto-draw sensors can be sensitive to blocked airflow. Keep air holes clear. See [vape not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/) for related fixes.

## Choosing hardware
Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/), and read [disposable vs pod vs box mod](/blog/disposable-vs-pod-vs-box-mod/). Adults 21+ only; nicotine is addictive.

faq.q: Is auto-draw more convenient?
faq.a: Yes, because you just inhale. The trade-off is less control.

faq.q: Can button-fire prevent leaks?
faq.a: It can reduce accidental firing, which helps in bags.

summary: Vaporizers come in several designs. Compare pens, portables and desktop units so you can see which style fits how you plan to use one.
body:
The word "vaporizer" covers a range of devices that heat material or liquid without burning. Here are the main types.

## Vape pens
Slim, battery-powered pens heat a cartridge or a small chamber. They are discreet and easy to carry, and are suited to people who want simplicity.

## Portable vaporizers
Larger handheld devices have a heating chamber, adjustable temperature and bigger batteries. They give more control than a pen at the cost of size.

## Desktop vaporizers
Plug-in units are designed for home use. They offer precise temperature control and excellent consistency but are not portable.

## Dab and concentrate devices
Some vaporizers are designed for concentrates with specific heating elements. These are specialist products, and their legality depends on your local laws.

## Choosing
Consider portability, battery life, how easy it is to clean and the cost of replacement parts. Read reviews and manuals, and buy from a reputable seller. See [how to buy a vaporizer wisely](/shop/vaporizers/).

## Legal considerations
Products and uses are regulated differently by state, and some materials remain restricted or illegal in places. Check [state and local laws](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## Care
Clean regularly and handle batteries carefully; see [battery care](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

## Browse
See our [vaporizers](/shop/vaporizers/) category. Adults 21+ only.

title: Vape Flavor Profiles Explained: Fruit, Dessert, Menthol and Tobacco
summary: Understand the main flavor families so you can find what suits you, from bright fruit to rich dessert and classic tobacco.
body:
Flavor names can be confusing, but most vapes fall into a handful of families.

## Fruit
The biggest group. It includes single fruits like watermelon, mango and peach and blends like berry mixes and tropical punches. Fruit flavors are bright, sweet and often tart. Our flavor guides cover [watermelon](/blog/watermelon-vape-flavors-guide/) and [blue razz](/blog/blue-razz-vape-flavors-guide/).

## Menthol and mint
Cooling, crisp flavors. Mint is herbal and sweet, menthol is sharper and cooler. Some recipes mix them with fruit.

## Dessert and bakery
Creamy, sweet and rich: custards, pastries, cakes and ice cream. They tend to have dense vapor and can leave residue on coils.

## Tobacco
Earthy, nutty or smoky profiles that aim to mimic traditional tobacco, from light to robust.

## Beverage
Cola, lemonade, coffee and tea flavors, often with citrus or cooling notes.

## Candy
Cotton candy, gummy and sour flavors. They are very sweet and popular with those who like bold taste.

## Choosing a flavor
Start with a family you like in food or drink. If you want a chill, try an [ice flavor](/blog/ice-vape-flavors-guide/). Read [best disposables for flavor lovers](/blog/best-disposable-vapes-for-flavor-lovers/).

## Browse

title: Why Is My Vape Not Hitting? 8 Causes and Quick Fixes
summary: No vapor or a weak draw is usually a simple fix. Work through these eight checks before assuming the device is dead.
body:
When a vape stops producing vapor, or the puffs turn weak, thin or cool, it is rarely a mystery for long. The cause is usually one of a short list: a flat battery, no liquid, blocked airflow, a loose connection, a flooded or worn coil, extreme temperature or a locked device. This guide walks through the checks in the order that finds the problem fastest, explains what each symptom means, shows how to fix the cause for each type of device, covers disposables, pods and tanks separately, lists what not to do and explains when a device has simply reached the end of its life. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive.

## Start with what the device is telling you
Before you take anything apart, notice how it behaves. Does it fire at all? Does a light blink, and in what pattern? Is the vapor weak, or absent, or harsh? Does the problem happen on every puff or only some? Those clues narrow the field. A device that does nothing and shows no light points to power. A device that fires but gives no vapor points to liquid or airflow. A device that gives thin vapor and a flat taste points to a worn coil or low power. Keep those clues in mind as you go through the checks.

## 1. Battery
A flat battery is the most common cause. Charge a rechargeable device for 20 to 30 minutes, then try again. A device with a nearly empty battery may fire weakly before it stops, so a gradual fade is a sign of low charge. Many devices have a light that blinks when the battery is low. See [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/) and [understanding vape device indicator lights](/blog/understanding-vape-device-indicator-lights/). If the device will not charge, see [what to do when a vape will not charge](/blog/vape-wont-charge-fixes/).

## 2. Out of liquid
Check the window or the pod. A dry wick burns and gives weak or harsh vapor, and a device that is out of liquid may still fire and heat the coil. Refill a refillable pod or tank, or replace a pre-filled pod. In a disposable, if you cannot see liquid and the flavor has gone, the device may be finished. Do not keep puffing on an empty device, because it burns the wick and gives an unpleasant taste.

## 3. Blocked airflow
Airflow holes can be covered by fingers or lint, and in some devices the sensor channel can be blocked by condensation. Check that your fingers are not over the intake, and clean the holes gently with a dry cotton bud. If the draw feels very tight, airflow may be blocked. If you have an adjustable airflow ring, check that it is not fully closed. See [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).

## 4. Loose connection
Make sure the pod or tank is seated firmly, with a click if it has one, and that the contacts are clean. Wipe the metal contacts with a dry cotton bud. Liquid residue or lint can stop the electrical connection, so the device will not fire. If a pod has a bent or dirty contact, clean it carefully, and do not bend anything.

## 5. Flooded coil
Too much liquid can drown the coil, so that it cannot heat the liquid properly. Signs are gurgling, weak vapor and sometimes leaking. Blow gently through the mouthpiece, wipe excess liquid from the contacts and wait a few minutes. See [fixing a gurgling vape](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/) and [leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/).

## 6. Worn coil
Coils lose performance with time, as residue builds up on the heating surface. Flavor fades, vapor thins and sometimes a burnt taste appears. Replace the coil or pod. As a rough guide, coils last from several days to a few weeks depending on use, liquid and power. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/).

## 7. Cold or hot temperatures
Batteries struggle in cold, and a device left in a cold car or outdoors may fire weakly or not at all. Warm the device in your hand or an inside pocket, away from heat sources, and let it reach room temperature. Very hot conditions are also a problem: a device that has been in the sun can shut off to protect itself. Let it cool before you try again. Never use a hairdryer or a heater to warm a battery.

## 8. Device lock
Some devices lock after multiple clicks, to prevent accidental firing in a pocket. Check the manual for the unlock sequence, which is often a set number of clicks on the button. If your device has a lock indicator, it may blink in a particular pattern.

## 9. The sensor is stuck
In auto-draw devices, a small sensor detects your inhale. Condensation can make it stick. Blowing gently into the mouthpiece, or tapping the device against your palm, can free it. Wipe away any visible liquid, and let it sit upright for a few minutes.

## 10. Prime the coil
A new coil or pod that has not been primed can seem to give nothing, or taste burnt. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/). Let it soak, and use gentle puffs at first.

## Troubleshooting by device type
### Disposables
You cannot open or repair a disposable. Check the charge, check for liquid, clear the mouthpiece and the airflow, and try holding it upright for a minute. If it still does not work, it may be faulty or finished.

### Pod systems
Remove the pod and check the contacts and the liquid. Try a fresh pod, if you have one, to tell whether the problem is the pod or the battery. Clean the contacts, and make sure the pod clicks fully into place.

### Tank and mod systems
Check the battery level, the connection between tank and mod, the coil and the power setting. Try a different coil, or put the tank on another mod, to isolate the fault. Make sure the coil's resistance is displayed correctly. See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## What not to do
- **Do not open a disposable or a sealed device.** It risks damaging the battery.
- **Do not use metal tools in the charging port or contacts.**
- **Do not keep vaping on a dry or burnt coil.** It tastes bad and wears the coil.
- **Do not heat a battery to warm it up.**
- **Do not force a pod that does not fit.** Check it is the right model.

## A quick diagnostic flow
If nothing happens at all, check the charge and the lock. If it fires but there is no vapor, check the liquid and the airflow. If vapor is thin and flavor is flat, check the coil and the power. If it gurgles, check for flooding. If it tastes burnt, check the liquid level and the coil. Following that order solves most cases within a few minutes.

## When the device has reached its end
Batteries wear and coils wear. A device that has been in use for a long time may simply be finished. If a disposable has run out of liquid or battery, replace it, and dispose of it properly. See [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). If a refillable device has a worn battery, consider a replacement.

## If your device is faulty from new
If a device from us does not work, or stops working very soon, contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your order ID and a description of what you tried. Our [refund policy](/refunds/) explains what applies, and we will tell you the next step. Do not try to repair it.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does my vape work for one puff and then stop?
Often a flooded coil, a low battery or a sensor that is sticking. Wipe, wait and try again.

### Why is the vapor weak even though the battery is full?
A worn coil, low liquid, blocked airflow or too low a power setting.

### Why does my device blink but not fire?
Blinking is a signal. Check the manual or our guide to indicator lights. It can mean low battery, a short circuit or a lock.

### Can a cold device be fixed by warming it?
Usually yes, by letting it return to room temperature. Do not use direct heat.

### Is it normal for a vape to need replacing?
Yes. Coils and batteries are consumables, and devices have a limited life.

## Prevention
Charge before it is empty, keep liquid above the minimum, prime new coils, avoid chain vaping and store devices upright at room temperature. Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) when you need replacements. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Three short case studies
### Case 1: the pocket device
A customer's pod device worked in the morning and stopped by lunchtime. The battery light blinked three times. The cause was a low battery, and a 25-minute charge fixed it. Lesson: a blinking light on a device that suddenly stops is usually a power signal.

### Case 2: the weak vapor
A tank gave thin, cool vapor even with a full battery. The coil had been in use for three weeks, and the cotton looked dark and crusty. A new coil, primed properly, restored full flavor. Lesson: weak vapor with a full battery points to the coil.

### Case 3: the cold morning
A disposable did nothing when taken out of a cold car. After ten minutes in an inside pocket, it worked normally. Lesson: warm the device gently and give it time.

## A small troubleshooting kit
Keep a few simple items to hand: a spare cable, a dry cotton bud, a wooden toothpick, paper towels and a spare pod or coil. With these, you can solve most problems in a few minutes without leaving the house.

title: Why Does My Vape Taste Burnt? Causes and Fixes
summary: A burnt taste usually means a dry or worn coil. Learn the causes, how to fix them and how to prevent it next time.
body:
A burnt taste is unpleasant, and it is a clear sign that something is off in your setup. It happens when the cotton wick or the liquid on the coil gets too hot, and it is almost always preventable. This guide explains what is actually happening inside the device when a vape tastes burnt, the common causes in the order you should check them, how to fix each one, how to avoid damaging a new coil, why chain vaping and thick liquid cause problems, how to tell a burnt coil from a dying battery, what not to do and how to prevent the problem. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## What a burnt taste actually is
When the coil heats, liquid in the wick absorbs the heat and turns to vapor. If there is not enough liquid in the wick, the cotton itself heats, and it scorches, giving a harsh, acrid, sometimes bitter taste. Sugars and sweeteners in the liquid can also caramelize on the coil when they sit on it too long or too hot, leaving a residue that tastes burnt on later puffs. In both cases, the taste is a signal that the coil is not being cooled by liquid as it should be.

## Dry or low liquid
If liquid runs low, the wick dries and burns. Refill or replace before the pod or tank empties, and keep the level above the minimum line. In a device with a window, check it before you use it. In a disposable, a burnt taste late in its life may mean the liquid is nearly finished, and it is time to replace the device.

## An unprimed coil
A new coil needs time to soak. Without priming, the dry cotton scorches on the first puffs, which can ruin a coil in seconds. See [how to prime a coil](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/). Drip a few drops on the cotton, fill the tank or pod and wait, then start with gentle puffs at a low power.

## Chain vaping
Rapid puffs without letting the wick re-saturate can burn it. The wick can only draw liquid in as fast as it can move, and long, repeated puffs use it faster. Take breaks between puffs, and use shorter draws. If you tend to chain vape, a device with better wicking, or a larger coil, may suit you better.

## Wrong liquid for the coil
Thick, sugary or high-VG liquid can struggle to wick through small coils, and sweeteners caramelize on the heating surface. Match liquid to hardware: high-VG liquids suit sub-ohm tanks with large wicking openings, and 50/50 or PG-leaning liquids suit pods. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/). Very sweet dessert liquids are tougher on coils, and they shorten coil life even when used correctly.

## Too much power
Running above the coil's recommended wattage burns cotton fast. If your device lets you set power, lower it to the middle of the coil's range or below. If it is a fixed-power pod, the maker has set it, and a burnt taste points to another cause. See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## A worn coil
Coils that have been in use a while build up residue. Even with good liquid levels, a coil with a caked surface gives a burnt taste. Replace it. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/). A coil that tastes burnt from new, though, may be unprimed or faulty.

## Blocked or tight airflow
Too little airflow can cause the coil to overheat, because there is not enough air to carry heat away. Open the airflow slightly, or check that nothing blocks it. See [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).

## Low battery
As a battery weakens, some devices deliver uneven power, which can cause odd tastes. If the burnt taste appears together with weak vapor at low charge, charge the device and test again.

## How to tell whether the coil is the problem
Try a fresh coil or pod. If the burnt taste goes away, the old coil was the problem. If it stays, check the liquid level, the liquid type and the power. Changing one thing at a time tells you which it is. If you have two devices, try the same liquid in the other, to see if the liquid is the cause.

## A step-by-step fix
1. Stop vaping, because more puffs will make it worse.
2. Check the liquid level and top up if needed.
3. Let the coil rest for a few minutes to re-saturate.
4. Take a gentle puff to test.
5. If it is still burnt, lower the power or open the airflow.
6. If it is still burnt, replace the coil or pod.
7. Prime the new coil properly.

## What not to do
Do not keep vaping through a burnt taste. It will not improve, it can be unpleasant to inhale and it wears out the coil faster. Do not add more power to try to burn off the taste, which makes it worse. Do not rinse a coil with water and reuse it, because water and electrical parts do not mix, and a wet coil can misfire. Do not try to clean a coil with flames or heat.

## Prevention
Prime coils, keep pods filled and use compatible liquid. Take steady puffs with breaks. Keep power in range. Replace coils on a schedule that suits your use. Store devices upright. Keep a spare pod or coil so that a burnt one can be replaced right away. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) for replacements.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does a new coil taste burnt?
Usually it was not primed, or it was used at too high a power before it was soaked. Let it rest and use low power.

### Can a burnt coil recover?
Sometimes a mild case recovers after resting and re-saturating. A truly burnt coil does not, and it should be replaced.

### Why does my disposable taste burnt at the end?
The liquid is probably nearly finished. A burnt taste is a sign that the wick is running dry.

### Do some flavors burn more easily?
Sweet, creamy and dessert flavors leave more residue and can taste burnt sooner. That is a property of the recipe, not a fault.

### Is a burnt taste harmful?
We make no health claims. A burnt taste is unpleasant and a sign that the device is not working as intended, so stop and fix the cause.

## Related
See [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/), [dry hits explained](/blog/dry-hits-explained/) and [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Case studies
### The new coil that tasted burnt
A customer fitted a new coil and fired it straight away. The first puffs tasted burnt, and they carried on. By the end of the day the coil was ruined. Priming for ten minutes and starting at a low power would have prevented it. Lesson: the first minutes of a coil's life decide how long it lasts.

### The sweet liquid that kept burning coils
A customer using a very sweet dessert liquid found that coils lasted only three days. Switching to a less sweet liquid doubled coil life, and lowering the power by a few watts helped too. Lesson: some liquids are hard on coils, and the fix may be the liquid, not the coil.

### The disposable that tasted burnt at the end
A large disposable tasted burnt after several weeks. The liquid window showed it nearly empty. The device had simply reached the end of its liquid. Lesson: a burnt taste late in a device's life often means it is finished.

## A weekly habit check
Check liquid levels before you start vaping each day, give a new coil a proper soak, replace a coil when the taste changes and keep a spare. These four habits prevent most burnt tastes.

## When flavor is the problem, not burning
Not every unpleasant taste is burnt. A flat or muddy taste can mean a worn coil or a flavor you have tired of. A soapy or chemical taste can come from residue after cleaning. A sour taste can come from old liquid. Learn to tell them apart: burnt is sharp and acrid, flat is dull, soapy is smooth and unpleasant, and sour is tangy. See [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/).

## Frequently asked questions about taste
### Can e-liquid itself taste burnt?
Old or overheated liquid can taste off, and a liquid that has darkened a lot may taste harsher. If the same liquid tastes fine in another device, the liquid is not the cause.

### Why does a burnt taste come and go?
It can appear when the wick is drying between puffs, and disappear after a rest. That pattern points to wicking, liquid thickness or chain vaping.

### Should I change liquid flavors to fix it?
A very sweet or very thick flavor may be the cause. Try a thinner or less sweet liquid before you replace the coil again.

### Is it worth switching to a bigger coil?
If you chain vape or use thick liquids, a coil with better wicking can help. Match it to your device and liquid.

faq.a: Usually a dry wick, an unprimed or worn coil, chain vaping, too much power or liquid that is too thick for the coil.

faq.q: How do I fix it?
faq.a: Check the liquid level, let the coil rest, lower the power or open the airflow, and replace the coil if it persists.

faq.q: Can I keep using a burnt coil?
faq.a: No. It will not improve and wears out faster. Replace it.

faq.q: How do I prevent it?
faq.a: Prime new coils, keep liquid above the minimum, avoid chain vaping and use liquid that suits the coil.

faq.q: Why do sweet liquids burn coils faster?
faq.a: Sweeteners caramelize on the heating surface and leave residue that tastes burnt.

faq.q: Should I clean the coil with water?
faq.a: No. Water and electrical parts do not mix. Replace the coil.

title: Vape Leaking? Common Causes and How to Stop It
summary: Leaks come from overfilling, loose seals, pressure changes or damaged parts. Find the cause and fix it with these steps.
body:
A leaking vape is messy, wasteful and unpleasant to carry, and it can damage devices and clothes. Liquid ends up on your fingers, in your pocket or in the charging port, and a device that leaks keeps leaking until the cause is found. The causes are almost always simple: overfilling, loose or damaged seals, cracks, pressure changes, the wrong liquid thickness, too much airflow, a worn coil or poor storage. This guide explains each one, how to recognize it, how to fix it, how to clean up properly, how to carry devices to avoid leaks and what to do with a device that will not stop leaking. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and liquid should be kept away from children and pets.

## How leaks happen
A vape holds liquid in a reservoir and feeds it to the coil through the wick. The system is designed to keep liquid in the right place using seals, small airflow channels and the balance between liquid, air and pressure. A leak happens when liquid finds a way out: through a gap in a seal, through the airflow, through a crack or out of the fill port. Anything that disturbs the balance, such as too much liquid, a pressure change or a damaged part, can start one.

## Overfilling
Filling a pod or tank to the very top leaves no room for air. Air is needed in the reservoir to let liquid flow smoothly and to cushion changes in pressure. Fill below the max line and never over the central tube, and tilt the tank when you fill it so liquid runs down the side instead of splashing into the airflow channel. Close the fill port firmly. Overfilling is the most common cause of leaks.

## Loose or damaged seals
Check that the pod or tank is tightly seated and that silicone seals are in place and not cracked. A seal that has hardened, stretched or shifted lets liquid past. Replace worn seals if the device uses them, and check them when you change a coil. Make sure the tank is screwed together evenly, not cross-threaded. Do not overtighten, because that can damage the seals.

## Cracked tank or pod
Inspect for hairline cracks, especially after a drop. A crack in plastic or glass is not always visible, and liquid can seep along it. Hold the part up to the light and look for lines or stains. If you find one, replace the part. Do not try to glue it, because the glue will not suit liquid or heat.

## Pressure changes
Flights and driving through mountains can push liquid out. As air pressure falls, the air inside the reservoir expands and pushes liquid out. Keep pods nearly empty when traveling, or choose a sealed disposable. Keep the device upright and in a bag. See [choosing a vape for travel](/blog/best-vapes-for-travel/) and [traveling with vapes](/blog/traveling-with-vapes-airline-rules/).

## Wrong liquid thickness
Thin liquid in a large-coil tank can seep through the coil and leak. Thick liquid can cause flooding if the coil cannot take it. Match liquid to hardware: high-PG liquids can leak from big sub-ohm coils, and high-VG liquids can flood small pods. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/). If a particular bottle always leaks in your device, try a different ratio.

## Too much airflow
Very open airflow with a tight coil can cause condensation to pool and run out through the intake. If your device has adjustable airflow, close it a little. Condensation collects in the airflow channel and can drip from the base, which looks like a leak even when the tank is sealed.

## Worn coil
An old coil can flood, because its wicking channels are clogged and liquid builds up around it. Replace it; see [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/). A leak that starts after weeks of normal use often points to the coil.

## Storage position
Store pods and tanks upright. Lying a device on its side lets liquid run toward the airflow and the mouthpiece. In a bag, use a case or a pocket where the device stays upright. Do not leave it in a hot car, because heat thins liquid and expands air.

## Loose connections and threads
If the tank base has a loose thread, liquid can leak through the join. Check the coil is screwed in firmly, and the base is tight. If a thread is damaged, replace the part.

## How to clean up a leak
Wipe the outside with a paper towel while wearing gloves if you can, wash your hands and the surface and dispose of the towels responsibly. Avoid skin contact. Dry the contacts and the charging port before you use or charge the device, because liquid can damage electronics. Keep liquid away from children and pets; see [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/). If liquid has got into the charging port or the electronics, do not charge the device, and let it dry in a warm room, not near heat.

## A step-by-step approach
1. Empty the device and wipe it clean.
2. Inspect the seals, the threads and the body for damage.
3. Check the coil. Replace it if it is worn.
4. Refill below the max line.
5. Seat the pod or tank firmly.
6. Let it rest upright for a few minutes.
7. Test with gentle puffs.
8. If it leaks again, replace the part you suspect, starting with the coil, then the seals, then the pod or tank.

## Disposables that leak
Disposables are sealed, and you cannot open them. A disposable that leaks from the mouthpiece or the base is faulty, or has been damaged or stored badly. Do not use a device that is leaking. Wipe it, keep it upright and contact us with your order ID and photos if it arrived like that. See the [refund policy](/refunds/) and [damaged or missing items](/blog/damaged-or-missing-items-what-to-do/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does my vape leak only when I travel?
Pressure changes push liquid out. Keep pods nearly empty and carry devices upright in a bag.

### Is a little condensation normal?
Yes. A small amount of moisture in the airflow is normal. Wipe it away. A steady drip is a leak.

### Can I use a leaking device?
It is better to fix it first. Liquid on the electronics can damage the device, and you will waste liquid.

### Why does a new pod leak?
It may have been overfilled, not seated properly or have a faulty seal. Remove it, wipe it, refill below the line and seat it firmly.

### Can I stop leaks with tape or glue?
No. Do not modify the device. Replace the faulty part.

## Prevention
Fill carefully, check seals, keep devices upright, avoid heat, match the liquid to the hardware and replace coils on time. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) for replacement parts. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Case studies
### The bag that smelled of fruit
A customer found their bag damp and sweet-smelling after a commute. The pod had been filled to the top and carried on its side. Filling below the line and carrying the device upright stopped it. Lesson: fill level and position decide most leaks.

### The leak after a drop
A tank started leaking two days after it was dropped. A hairline crack had formed in the base, invisible at first. A new tank solved it. Lesson: inspect after a drop, because small cracks cause slow leaks.

### The leak in the cold
A device leaked every winter morning. Cold made the liquid thicker and the seals stiffer. Letting it warm before use, and storing it inside, stopped the leaks. Lesson: temperature changes matter.

## Carrying devices to avoid leaks
Carry devices upright, in a case or a pocket of their own, with the pod nearly empty if you are traveling. Do not put them loose in a bag with keys. Do not leave them in a car. A small silicone sleeve or a case costs little and protects both the device and your belongings.

## A short maintenance routine
Once a week, wipe the outside of the device and check seals and threads. Once a month, rinse refillable tanks and replace worn O-rings. Replace coils and pods on a schedule that suits you. A little routine care stops most leaks before they start.

## Things that look like leaks but are not
Condensation in the mouthpiece, a little moisture around the airflow after a heavy session and liquid that has been spilled during filling can all look like leaks. Wipe the device clean, then watch it for a day. If no new liquid appears, it was not a leak.

## Frequently asked questions about leaks
### Can I fix a cracked tank with glue?
No. Glue is not suited to liquid or heat, and it can contaminate the liquid. Replace the part.

### Why does my vape leak when it is full but not when it is half full?
A full tank leaves little air, and any pressure change pushes liquid out. Fill to about three-quarters when traveling.

### Does a leaking vape need a new coil?
Often yes. Try a fresh coil first, because a worn coil is a common cause. If it still leaks, check the seals and the tank.

### Will leaks damage my device?
Liquid on the contacts or the port can cause corrosion and misfires. Wipe and dry the device, and do not charge it until the port is dry.

faq.q: What is the most common cause of leaks?
faq.a: Overfilling. Fill below the max line and never over the central tube.

faq.q: Why does my vape leak on a plane?
faq.a: Pressure changes push liquid out. Keep pods nearly empty and carry devices upright.

faq.q: Can the wrong liquid cause leaks?
faq.a: Yes. Thin liquid in a large-coil tank can seep, and thick liquid can flood small coils. Match liquid to hardware.

faq.q: How do I clean up a leak?
faq.a: Wipe with paper towels, wash your hands and the surface, dry the contacts and port and dispose of the towels responsibly.

faq.q: Can a disposable that leaks be fixed?
faq.a: No. Disposables are sealed. Contact us with your order ID and photos.

faq.q: How do I store a device to avoid leaks?
faq.a: Upright, at room temperature, in a case or a pocket where it stays upright.
